So prediction 2 (**78 → ≥ 86**) needs **at least 8 of the 35 crossers** to be repaired, and the 85–95% band's
measured rate (81.0% on §13.79's run) implies about **28 of 35** — a prediction of 89 rather than 86. The
registered threshold is the conservative side of its own arithmetic, which is the right direction for a
prediction whose mechanism was measured on one previous run only.

The third row is the one to remember afterwards: **36 MR questions cannot be reached by any budget**, because
their gold never enters the pool at all or enters above rank 146. That is the size of the ranking problem that
survives this experiment, and it is comparable to the 29-question gap to the reference pipeline.

## 13.82 The budget buys the room exactly, and the 85% step does not survive it

### 13.82.1 The readings (`39260774611`, 2h02m36s, drift 500/500)

| #     | prediction (§13.81.2)                  | observed   | verdict                                         |
| ----- | -------------------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| **1** | MR's delivered share 72.9% → **≥ 83%** | **86.92%** | **holds** (estimator said 87.11%, error 0.19pp) |
| **2** | MR's correct count 78 → **≥ 86**       | **83**     | **falsified**, short by 3                       |
| **3** | roster 394 → **≥ 402**                 | **403**    | **holds**                                       |
| **4** | TR 89 → **≥ 94**                       | **93**     | **falsified**, short by 1                       |

Registered statistic **+35.10pp** (was +33.50pp), McNemar p = 1.79e-31. Union **444/500 = 88.80%**, the
campaign's best (was 438, best 439). Per capability: ABS 29, IE 135, KU 63, MR 83, TR 93.

### 13.82.2 The mechanism is exact, and the gain is located where the arithmetic said

`--window` reads **144 turns on MR and 151 on TR** against 68 and 74, at **46,165 and 47,129 characters**
against 22,180 and 23,150 — a 2.1× room spending 2.0× the characters, with no over-budget record. The partition
§13.81.6 wrote down before the run, scored after it:

| group                          | n   | was | now    | delta  |
| ------------------------------ | --- | --- | ------ | ------ |
| already ≥ 85% at 68 turns      | 50  | 41  | **40** | **−1** |
| crosses 85% only at 146 turns  | 35  | 17  | **22** | **+5** |
| never reaches 85% at 146 turns | 36  | 20  | **21** | **+1** |

The whole MR gain is the middle row, which is the row §13.81.6 said prediction 2 was about. The crossers
converted at **62.9%** (22 of 35) against the 48.6% they converted at before — a +14.3pp lift — while the
already-covered group **lost one question**. That is the shape of dilution: more room buys more gold and also
more noise, and the two effects are within one question of cancelling outside the crossing group.

### 13.82.3 The step was a property of that run's evidence, and this is what retired it

MR's accuracy by coverage band, this run against §13.79's:

| band         | §13.79 (68 turns) | §13.82 (144 turns)   |
| ------------ | ----------------- | -------------------- |
| 25–50%       | 50.0%             | 20.0%                |
| 50–75%       | 50.0%             | 55.6%                |
| 75–85%       | 50.0%             | 75.0%                |
| **85–95%**   | **81.0%**         | **64.0%**            |
| **95–100%**  | **86.7%**         | **77.0%**            |
| exactly 100% | —                 | **88.6%** (31 of 35) |

**The step does not replicate.** §13.81.3's second branch is the one that happened: coverage crossed and the count
did not follow. What replaces it is a slope — 20%, 56%, 75%, 64%, 77% — with a jump only at **exactly complete**
coverage, where the reader is at 88.6% and therefore at parity with the reference pipeline's 85.1% on that
capability. Two consequences follow and both are load-bearing:

- **coverage is not a sufficient statistic.** The same 86.9% delivery buys 68.6% accuracy here and bought 64.5%
  at 72.9%; the composition of the window matters as much as its coverage, which is why the band table has to be
  recomputed on every run rather than carried forward (§130.3 said the same and this is the second confirmation).
- **the reader is not the deficit.** When every gold turn is carried the reader answers 31 of 35. MR's gap to the
  reference pipeline is retrieval, not comprehension, and §13.82.6 prices how much of it any budget can still buy.

### 13.82.4 The price was not what the registration said

§13.81.2 predicted passes "near 50 minutes" and called the 90-minute ceiling worth watching. The run took
**2h02m36s** against the previous 1h58m — **four minutes** for double the evidence. Prefill is not the binding
cost on this workload; decode is, and decode is one short answer either way. The cost line in §13.81 was
therefore wrong in the direction that matters: raising the budget is nearly free in wall clock, so the ceiling
that decides where the room stops is scientific rather than operational.

### 13.82.5 Adoption

Adopted. Predictions 1 and 3 hold and both are about the quantity the campaign is scored on — delivered gold and
the roster — while 2 and 4 miss by 3 and 1 on counts whose direction was right (+5, +4). The two regressions are
IE 136 → 135 and ABS 30 → 29, each **one question**, inside the ±2-per-capability resolution §109.4 measured;
KU rose 61 → 63. Roster 394 → 403, union 438 → 444, delta +33.50pp → +35.10pp.

What the adoption does **not** claim: that the budget is why MR gained. The partition in §13.82.2 locates the
gain in the crossing group and the loss in the covered group, which is consistent with the room and inconsistent
with any reader change — but there was no second room to compare against, so the magnitude carries one run's
noise. The next section is designed around what the partition says the room cannot reach.

### 13.82.6 The room is nearly exhausted; the next lever is in the retrieved set's composition

`--pool` on this artifact: MR's gold partitions into 182 never surfaced, **297 cut by the budget** (median rank
**189**), 3,180 delivered. Raising the window to ~250 turns would deliver **94.68%** of MR's gold, but only
**22 more questions** would cross 85% and **16 of those 22 are already correct** — so the expected gain is about
three questions for another 70% of evidence. The room's marginal return has fallen from +5 (68 → 144) to ~+3
(144 → 250), and the next doubling would be smaller again.

What the budget cannot fix is visible in the same table: **182 gold turns never surface at all**, and the 38 MR
errors are not dominated by "the gold was one rank away":

| missing gold turns        | 0     | 1   | 2   | 3   | ≥4  |
| ------------------------- | ----- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| wrong MR questions (38)   | **4** | 9   | 3   | 2   | 20  |
| correct MR questions (83) | 31    | 15  | 8   | 7   | 22  |

Four questions are wrong with **complete** evidence, and "missing one" is as common among the correct as among the
wrong — so the deficit is not a missing neighbour. It is that **the window's 144 slots are not all worth having**.

## 13.83 The room is half full of the assistant's own words

### 13.83.1 The measurement that names the next lever

The window is now 144 turns on MR and it spends 46,165 characters. Reading the roles out of those turns —
the `[date] role:` prefix the dataset's haystack carries — gives the composition of the room:

| capability | rendered characters from user turns | from assistant turns | cap in force |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------ |
| **MR**     | **48.1%**                           | **51.9%**            | 400          |
| **TR**     | **49.9%**                           | **50.1%**            | 400          |
| IE         | 22.7%                               | 77.3%                | none         |
| KU         | 22.7%                               | 77.3%                | none         |
| ABS        | 24.2%                               | 75.8%                | none         |

**On the two routes that decide the SOTA gap, half the evidence room is the assistant's own prose.** The
reference pipeline does not have this problem, and its source says why in one sentence: retrieval is _"restricted
to user turns because the facts live in the user's statements; assistant turns are verbose generated chatter that
dilutes the answer signal (and for temporal questions, drown the date-bearing turns)"_
(`natural-language-memory.ts`, `answer`). That pipeline reaches 85.1% on MR with a **24,000**-character budget,
against this arm's 68.6% with 48,000.

This is not a hypothesis about what might help. It is the one structural difference between a system that scores
85% on this capability and one that scores 69%, stated in the code of both, and it is measurable in the artifact
as the table above.

### 13.83.2 The registration

**One variable, two inputs, the same shape as §13.73**: `evidenceRoles: user` reaches
`multi-session,temporal`. Everything else is §10.3's adopted configuration, including the 48,000 budget.

The reach is scoped rather than global for a measured reason: IE, KU and ABS are at 135, 63 and 29 of 150, 72 and
30, and a global filter would move three capabilities the experiment is not asking about — with 77% of _their_
characters coming from assistant turns, that is not a neutral change for them. The scoping also gives this
section its internal control: the three untouched capabilities must reproduce **61.0, 62.0 and 72.0 turns** and
their `promptChars` to the character, exactly as §13.75 required of the previous reach.

| #     | prediction                                                                                   | falsified if   |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| **1** | MR's rendered user share rises 48.1% → **≥ 95%**, and its window grows 144 → **≥ 170** turns | < 95% or < 170 |
| **2** | MR's delivered share rises 86.92% → **≥ 92%**                                                | < 92%          |
| **3** | MR's correct count rises 83 → **≥ 90**                                                       | ≤ 89           |
| **4** | TR 93 → **≥ 96**                                                                             | ≤ 95           |
| **5** | IE, KU and ABS reproduce 135/63/29, 61.0/62.0/72.0 turns and their `promptChars`             | any changes    |
| **6** | The roster rises 403 → **≥ 410**                                                             | ≤ 409          |

Prediction 2 is derived, not guessed: the filtered ranking puts user turns at 242 characters each against the
400-character cap, so 48,000 characters hold about **190** user turns, and the 95%-coverage rank in a _user-only_
ranking is not computable from this artifact's ranks — which is why the prediction is stated as a threshold and
its mechanism (prediction 1) is measured separately.

### 13.83.3 What each outcome would mean

- **1–4 hold**: the composition of the retrieved set is the lever, the room is not, and the next question becomes
  whether the assistant turns carry anything the user turns do not — which is measurable by adding back only the
  assistant turns that share a session with a retrieved user turn.
- **1 holds, 3 does not**: the filter moved the room as designed and the reader still misses, which would locate
  the deficit in the ranking _within_ user turns and make the expansion channel the next experiment.
- **1 fails**: the filter did not do what the arithmetic says, which would point at the selection's interaction
  with the cap rather than at the roles — the same failure mode §13.81.5 was written to catch, and `--window` is
  again the first thing to read.

### 13.83.4 What was built, and why the boundary sits where it does

**The product owns the filter; the arm owns the format.** `CortexMemoryOptions` gained `evidenceRoles`,
`evidenceRolesRoutes` and `roleOf`, and the product never learns that a haystack prefixes `[date] role:` —
`roleOf` is a callback. That boundary is the whole point: a parser in `cortex-memory` would make the product's
behaviour a fact about one dataset, and the next dataset would be either unsupported or silently unfiltered. The
arm supplies `roleOfTurn`, whose regex is anchored at the start with a non-empty bracketed stamp so a turn that
merely _mentions_ `assistant:` is not mislabelled.

**Three states, each refused or kept for a stated reason.**

| state                        | behaviour                                                        | why                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `evidenceRoles` absent       | no filter runs; the prompt is byte-identical to the archived one | every prior artifact has to stay reproducible                  |
| `roleOf` returns `undefined` | the turn is **kept**                                             | a classifier failure must not read as an empty dataset         |
| `evidenceRoles: []`          | **refused at construction**                                      | it admits nothing on every reached route: a decline every time |

A filter without a classifier is refused at construction as well, which is §10.10's class — a value the artifact
records and the run does not apply. The check is at the seam where the two arrive together, so the state is
unrepresentable rather than invisible.

**Where it applies, and what it therefore measures.** After admission and before selection, on all three prompt
paths (`#prompt`, `#promptWithDate`, `#promptSessionAware`), and on the session path **per session** — a session
the filter empties is dropped, because a boundary with nothing behind it would be printed as a heading and paid
for out of the budget. `lastRetrievedContext` and `admittedEvidence` are recorded **after** the filter, so the
artifact's `retrieved` is what the reader could have been shown; a filter applied after the capture would leave
every coverage count describing a room the model never saw.

**The instrument the mechanism prediction needs.** `readout-arm-run.py --roles` reports the rendered characters
by role per capability, with the run's own `maxTurnChars` applied where its reach covers the route — read from the
artifact, for §13.81.5's reason. An unreadable role is **its own column** rather than folded into either role,
because that folding is the same defect as a filter that drops what it cannot classify. On `39260774611` it
reproduces §13.82's hand-computed numbers exactly: MR 48.1% user / 51.9% assistant / 0.0% unreadable.

**The two inputs are registered at the identity.** `§10.3` records `evidenceRoles: all` and
`evidenceRolesRoutes: all`, which is the state every prior run is in; the experiment overrides both through
`--set`, and the parity test that binds §10.3 to the dispatch table therefore keeps passing on a run that is not
this experiment.

**Tests, and what each pins.** `cortex-memory`'s `evidence-roles.test.ts` covers the filter per route, byte
equality on an unreached route, the unknown-role case, the emptied-list decline on both the flat and temporal
paths, the session path including the all-sessions-empty decline, the offer recorded after the filter, and both
construction refusals. `cortex-eval`'s arm tests cover the readers (identity, dedupe, unknown role, `none`,
`named-no-role`), the shared reach reader, the config projection and line, the disabled-arm projection, and the
classifier's prefix rule. `tools/__tests__/test_readout_arm_run.py` covers the composition table: the split, the
cap applied, the cap not applied because its reach does not cover the route, the unreadable column, and the
refusal on a roster without turns.

## 13.84 The role filter pays: roster 419, union 452, and a metric that stops meaning what it meant

### 13.84.1 The readings (`39298662801`, 1h44m27s, drift 500/500)

| #     | prediction (§13.83.2)                                           | observed                                              | verdict                                             |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| **1** | MR's user share 48.1% → **≥ 95%**, window 144 → **≥ 170** turns | **100.0%**, **174**                                   | **holds**                                           |
| **2** | MR's delivered share 86.92% → **≥ 92%**                         | **48.35%**                                            | **falsified** — see §13.84.3, and not by the filter |
| **3** | MR's correct count 83 → **≥ 90**                                | **90**                                                | **holds**, at the line                              |
| **4** | TR 93 → **≥ 96**                                                | **98**                                                | **holds**                                           |
| **5** | IE/KU/ABS reproduce 135/63/29 and their windows                 | 135/**67**/29; windows **identical to the character** | **falsified on one count**, mechanism holds         |
| **6** | roster 403 → **≥ 410**                                          | **419**                                               | **holds**                                           |

Registered statistic **+36.80pp** (was +35.10pp), McNemar p = **4.92e-37**. Union **452/500 = 90.40%**, the
campaign's best by eight questions. Per capability: ABS 29, IE 135, KU 67, MR **90**, TR **98**.

### 13.84.2 The mechanism is exact on every route, including the three it did not touch

`--roles`: MR and TR read **100.0% user / 0.0% assistant / 0.0% unreadable**, against 48.1/51.9 and 49.9/50.1 on
the previous run. `--window`: MR's window grew **144 → 174 turns** while spending **46,186** characters — 20 more
turns in the same room, because a user turn is 265 characters where the mix averaged 319.

The three untouched capabilities reproduce their control **exactly**, which is the internal control §13.75
established and §13.83 predicted: ABS 72.0 turns / 46,694 characters, IE 61.0 / 46,864, KU 62.0 / 46,827 — the
same numbers to the character as `39260774611`. Their `total` counts moved (135/67/29 against 135/63/29) and that
is the repetition's own resolution, not the filter: §109.4 measured it at 6.1%, which is ±4 on KU's 72.

The churn is large and that is the evidence the treatment did something: **MR 17 questions turned correct and 10
turned wrong** (27 of 121 changed), TR 13 and 8. A noise-level effect does not move a quarter of the roster in
both directions.

### 13.84.3 Prediction 2 failed because the metric stopped meaning what it meant

MR's delivered share reads **48.35%**, and nothing about the room explains it: the window is 20 turns _wider_ and
the ranking is untouched. The reason is in the denominator. `goldOverlap` compares the turns the record carries
against the dataset's gold turns **by text**, and the record now carries only the turns the policy admits — so a
gold turn in an excluded role can never be counted, whatever the prompt did.

Two independent readings of the same artifact say so:

| reading                           | previous run                | this run                    |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| MR delivered gold                 | 3,180 of 3,663 = **86.92%** | 1,771 of 3,663 = **48.35%** |
| MR "cut by the budget" (`--pool`) | 301                         | **1,710**                   |
| MR questions above 75% coverage   | 86                          | **0**                       |

The budget did not change — 46,165 characters then, 46,186 now — and the second row's increase is entirely gold
in the excluded role, which `pool - carried` cannot tell apart from gold the room refused. `--pool` now prints a
`NOTE` on any artifact whose configuration filters roles, saying exactly that; before this section it would have
read as a four-fold collapse in the budget's reach.

**So prediction 2 was filed against a metric, and the treatment changed the metric.** That is a defect in how the
prediction was written and a defect in the instrument, and the second is what §13.85 fixes.

### 13.84.4 Adoption

Adopted: `evidenceRoles: user` reaching `multi-session,temporal`. No capability regressed — ABS 29 and IE 135 are
unchanged from the previous run, KU rose 4, MR rose 7, TR rose 5 — the roster is up 16, the union is up 8, and the
registered statistic is up 1.7pp with p at 4.92e-37.

What the adoption does not claim: that the 19 remaining `numeric_mismatch` questions and the 9 abstentions would be
better under the full mix. Ten MR questions turned **wrong** under this filter, and the plausible reading — that
some numbers are stated by the assistant rather than the user — is exactly what §13.86's next experiment would
test. It is not registered here because its mechanism is a coverage claim, and coverage is the thing §13.85 repairs.

## 13.85 The coverage denominator has to follow the policy

### 13.85.1 The defect

`goldOverlap.total` is the dataset's gold turn count and `carried` is the subset the record delivered. Under a role
filter those two count different populations: `carried` can only ever contain admitted turns, `total` contains
every gold turn. The ratio is then bounded by the policy, not by the room, and every section that reads it —
`--coverage`'s bands, `--pool`'s partition, the per-capability medians — inherits the bound.

§13.84.2's run is the first where this mattered and the first where it produced a reading that looks like a
retrieval collapse rather than a policy.

### 13.85.2 The repair

`goldOverlapOf` gains the gold turns the **policy** admits, and `total` becomes that number. Two properties are
required and each has a failure it prevents:

- **an unfiltered run is byte-identical.** Every archived artifact stays comparable, which is §13.15's rule
  applied to a denominator: absent filter, absent change.
- **a filtered run's `total` is stated beside the filter, so a reader cannot compare it against an unfiltered
  run without seeing why.** The roster gains `goldOverlap.totalAll` — the dataset's count — so the difference is
  a number in the artifact rather than a footnote in a document.

Acceptance, and what each clause can actually be checked against:

- **an unfiltered run is unchanged** — testable offline and tested: `unfiltered['totalAll']` is absent and `total`
  is the dataset's count.
- **a filtered run on an unreached capability is unchanged** — tested with `IE` and a two-route reach.
- **a filtered run on a reached capability carries `totalAll` beside `total`** — tested with `MR`.
- **the archived artifacts cannot be re-derived**, because re-deriving needs the run. `39298662801` keeps its
  published numbers and keeps the `--pool` warning that they are not a budget reading; the first artifact made
  after this section is the one whose partition is exhaustive over the policy's gold.
- **`--pool` and `--coverage` now distinguish the two states** by the presence of `totalAll`: a mixing warning on
  an old artifact, a denominator statement on a new one, and nothing at all on an unfiltered run.

### 13.85.3 Why this precedes the next experiment

The next hypothesis is that **some assistant turns carry numbers the user turns do not** — ten MR questions turned
wrong under a filter that removed them all. Testing it means a middle policy (assistant turns that share a session
with a retrieved user turn), and the mechanism prediction for that policy is a coverage claim. A coverage claim
measured on a denominator that mixes populations is not a measurement, so the instrument comes first.

## 13.86 A replication that measures the premise for the next experiment

### 13.86.1 Why a run with no variable is the right next one

§13.84 adopted an effective configuration and left one question open: **ten MR questions turned wrong** when
assistant turns left the room, and the plausible explanation is that some numbers are stated by the assistant. That
explanation has never been measured, and the artifact that would measure it did not exist until §13.85 — the record
now says, per question, how many gold turns the policy admits (`total`) beside how many the dataset names
(`totalAll`). The difference **is** the count of gold turns in an excluded role.

So the next run changes nothing about the system. It exists to be read three ways: the instrument's first output,
the second sample of an adopted configuration, and the premise for §13.87's companion policy.

### 13.86.2 The registration

Configuration: §10.3 exactly — `evidenceRoles: user` reaching `multi-session,temporal`, 48,000 characters,
cap 400 on the same two routes, `retrieval-hybrid` at k=256. Dispatched from the corrected code.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                                      | falsified if                                                              |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **1** | `totalAll` appears on **MR and TR** records whose gold the policy narrowed, and on **no** IE/KU/ABS record                      | any record outside those two capabilities carries it, or MR/TR carry none |
| **2** | the roster reproduces **419 ± 4**, and no capability moves by more than 4                                                       | any capability moves further                                              |
| **3** | among the ten MR questions that turned wrong in `39298662801`, **at least five** carry assistant-role gold (`totalAll > total`) | fewer than five                                                           |

Prediction 1 is the instrument's own acceptance, run on real data rather than a fixture. Prediction 2 is the noise
floor applied to a run that changed nothing — if the roster does not reproduce, the ±4 the campaign has been using
is wrong and every earlier per-capability claim needs restating. Prediction 3 is the one that decides whether a
companion policy is worth building at all.

### 13.86.3 What each outcome would mean

- **3 holds**: assistant turns carry gold on most of the questions the filter damaged, so a middle policy — keep an
  assistant turn when its session also contributes a kept user turn — has something to recover, and §13.87
  registers it against that set of questions.
- **3 fails**: the ten flips were the reader reacting to a different evidence _order_, not to missing texts. The
  next lever is then the window's ordering rather than its composition, and the companion policy is not built.
- **2 fails**: the campaign's per-capability resolution is not 6.1% and the last three sections' count readings have
  to be restated with the measured one.

## 13.87 The replication says the counts do not reproduce, and the gold is exactly half assistant turns

### 13.87.1 The readings (`39347010711`, 1h49m41s, drift 500/500)

| #     | prediction (§13.86.2)                                               | observed                                                | verdict       |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| **1** | `totalAll` on MR and TR records only                                | **121 MR + 127 TR**, zero on IE/KU/ABS                  | **holds**     |
| **2** | roster **419 ± 4**, no capability moving more than 4                | **407**; MR 90 → **83**, KU 67 → **63**, TR 98 → **97** | **falsified** |
| **3** | ≥ 5 of the ten flipped-wrong MR questions carry assistant-role gold | **10 of 10**                                            | **holds**     |

Registered statistic +35.75pp (was +36.80), McNemar p = 1.98e-33. Per capability: ABS 29, IE 135, KU 63,
MR 83, TR 97 — roster **407**.

### 13.87.2 Prediction 2 failed, and it is the most important result in this section

Nothing about the system changed between `39298662801` and `39347010711`: same commit's configuration, same code,
same data. MR moved **90 → 83**. That is the same seven-question distance the campaign read as a finding one
section earlier.

The artifact already recorded the answer and the campaign was not reading it. `featureAggregate` is the spread over
the **four repetitions** of one run:

| run           | configuration | roster per repetition | mean      |
| ------------- | ------------- | --------------------- | --------- |
| `39260774611` | every role    | 394 – 403             | **398.0** |
| `39298662801` | user only     | 397 – 419             | **406.0** |
| `39347010711` | user only     | 398 – 407             | **402.0** |

Two runs of one configuration have means four questions apart and ranges nineteen questions wide. The headline
"+16" in §13.84 compared **two single repetitions** — one run's best against another run's best — while the
registered statistic beside it was a mean over four. Both numbers were on the same page and they were measuring
different things.

**Corrected statement of the filter's effect**: the roster's mean moves 398 → 402–406, i.e. **+4 to +8**, not +16,
and a single run cannot resolve it. MR's 83 / 90 / 83 across three runs of two configurations is not evidence of
anything about MR.

### 13.87.3 The structural finding, which is independent of any sample

`totalAll / total` is **exactly 2.0 on 120 of 121 MR questions and 125 of 127 TR questions** — the gold set carries
each statement twice, once as the user's turn and once as the assistant's reply to it. So the policy removes
**50.01% of MR's gold and 50.03% of TR's** by construction, and the reader's accuracy did not fall.

That is a statement about the dataset that no run-to-run noise can touch, and it explains why the filter works: the
assistant half is a **restatement** of the user half, so removing it removes duplication rather than information.
It also sets the ceiling of the companion policy §13.86 was meant to license: the most an assistant turn can add is
the half of the gold that is a paraphrase, and the ten flipped questions show that half is sometimes decisive.

### 13.87.4 The instrument this section needs, registered

Every per-capability count in every artifact is **one repetition's**. The register's delta is a mean over four.
Reading a capability's movement from the first and its significance from the second is how a seven-question swing
became a finding twice.

§13.88 records the repair: per-capability correct counts **per repetition**, aggregated to min / mean / max beside
the overall aggregate, so a per-capability claim can be stated with its own spread. It needs no new run — the
ablation already holds each repetition's correctness vector and the dataset holds each question's capability; what
is missing is the projection into the artifact.

Until it exists, this document's rule is: **a per-capability movement below ten questions is not a finding**, and
any adoption argued from one is argued from the mean instead.

## 13.88 Per-capability counts across repetitions, so a movement can be stated with its spread

### 13.88.1 The defect §13.87 exposed

`ablation.featureAggregate` is min / avg / max over the four repetitions of one run. Every **per-capability**
count in the artifact is one repetition's. Two numbers with different units sit on the same page, and §13.84 and
§13.87 both read a capability's movement from the first while quoting the second's significance.

### 13.88.2 The registration

`AblationResult` gains `featureByCapability` and `baselineByCapability`: for each capability, the correct count per
repetition aggregated to min / avg / max, computed from the vectors the ablation already holds and the dataset's
own capability labels. Three properties:

- **absent when there is one repetition.** With `runs: 1` a min and a max are the same number and a "spread" of
  zero reads as perfect stability. The field is absent, not degenerate.
- **the mean is the register's unit.** `avg * questions(capability)` is a count a reader can compare against a
  single-run count only by knowing which one they hold, which is why all three are recorded.
- **no new run.** This is a projection of data already in memory at the end of an ablation.

Acceptance, and what each clause can be checked against:

- **the projection is correct** — tested with a scripted system that is right on even passes and wrong on odd ones,
  so min, mean and max are three different numbers. A deterministic fixture would make them equal and hide any
  aggregation bug.
- **a single repetition omits the field** — tested, because a spread of zero reads as perfect stability.
- **the aggregate agrees with the roster on the first repetition** — tested, because those two numbers are the pair
  §13.87 read in different units.
- **the Markdown states the unit** — tested: the header says "first repetition" and the spread columns appear only
  when the artifact holds them.
- **the archived artifacts cannot be re-derived** — the field did not exist when they were produced. The next run
  is the first that carries it, and `--caps` refuses on the old ones with a message naming the reason.
- **`--caps` reads it** — tested for the present case, the absent case, and a half-written field (spreads without
  denominators cannot become a rate).

## 13.90 A third sample of the adopted configuration, whose second purpose is the instrument's real output

### 13.90.1 Why

§13.88's projection is tested against fixtures; the bench path that fills it is an entry point and is not covered.
The cheapest honest way to know the field reaches a real artifact is a run that changes nothing and reads
`--caps` on it.

It also gives a **third** sample of one configuration, which is what the corrected reading rule needs: the two
existing samples put the roster's mean at 406 and 402, and a third narrows the band a per-capability claim would
have to clear. The same run is the first whose MR mean exists at all — the previous two recorded only one
repetition per capability.

### 13.90.2 The registration

Configuration: §10.3 exactly. No variable.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                                | falsified if         |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| **1** | the artifact carries `featureByCapability`, `baselineByCapability` and `questionsByCapability`, and `--caps` renders them | any is absent        |
| **2** | the roster's mean lands in **398 – 406** and no capability's mean departs its two earlier single readings by more than 7  | outside either bound |
| **3** | MR's mean sits between its two single readings, **83 ≤ mean ≤ 90**                                                        | outside              |

Prediction 2's upper bound is the highest mean measured so far and its lower bound the control's; a run outside
that band would say the configuration's own spread is wider than three samples suggest, which would make every
threshold in §13.89 need restating before that experiment is registered.

## 13.91 The third sample: the instrument works, and every capability now has a mean

### 13.91.1 The readings (`39367801501`, 1h56m35s, drift 500/500, §10.3 unchanged)

| #     | prediction (§13.90.2)                                                                          | observed                                   | verdict   |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | --------- |
| **1** | the three fields are present and `--caps` renders them                                         | all three present; the table renders       | **holds** |
| **2** | roster mean **398 – 406**, no capability mean more than 7 from its two earlier single readings | **405.0**; largest departure **5.75** (MR) | **holds** |
| **3** | MR mean **83 – 90**                                                                            | **84.25**                                  | **holds** |

`--caps` on a real artifact, for the first time:

| capability | total | min | **mean**   | max |
| ---------- | ----- | --- | ---------- | --- |
| ABS        | 30    | 29  | **29.25**  | 30  |
| IE         | 150   | 133 | **134.25** | 135 |
| KU         | 72    | 60  | **62.5**   | 64  |
| **MR**     | 121   | 81  | **84.25**  | 88  |
| **TR**     | 127   | 94  | **94.75**  | 95  |
| **roster** | 500   | 397 | **405.0**  | 412 |

Registered statistic +36.55pp (p = 2.86e-32); the first-repetition roster is 407 and the union is 446.

### 13.91.2 What the means do to the last four sections' claims

Three samples of one configuration now agree within their own spreads — 406, 402, 405 — and the control's single
sample was 398. **The filter's effect on the roster is +7 in the mean**, and that is the number the campaign can
defend.

Two headlines have to be restated and both move in the same direction, down:

| claim | as published              | with the mean          |
| ----- | ------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| MR    | 90 (§13.84) / 83 (§13.87) | **84.25**, range 81–88 |
| TR    | 98 (§13.84) / 97 (§13.87) | **94.75**, range 94–95 |

**TR is the sharper correction: both single readings sit above the mean.** The treatment's TR is not 97–98; it is
94.75, and the reference pipeline reads 87–88 in the same three runs. The lead is real and smaller: **+7 to +8**,
not +10.

MR's mean 84.25 against the reference's 104–105 is a gap of **20 questions**, not the 15 that §134's best single
reading implied.

### 13.91.3 What this changes about the method, permanently

The campaign now has, for the first time, a per-capability mean and range on every run. The rules that follow are
not preferences:

- **a per-capability claim is stated as `mean (min–max)`,** because the spread is on the record;
- **adoption compares means**, and a single run's number is quoted with "single";
- **a movement smaller than the range is not a finding** — MR's range alone is 7 questions.

§13.89's companion experiment can now be registered against a real threshold instead of a guess: MR's mean is
84.25 and §13.87.3 established that the assistant half of the gold is a restatement, with ten of ten flipped-wrong
questions carrying it.

## 13.92 The list is a recollection, not a walk: `ask: sweep` on the multi-session route

### 13.92.1 The premise, and the one §13.86 thought it had measured

Two things have to be said before the registration, and the second is a correction.

**The list is two items long.** `--lists` on `39367801501` reads a median Step 1 list of **2.0 items**
across all 121 MR records, against a window that carries **174 turns in roughly thirty sessions**. The
response is not enumerating the document; it is enumerating what it happened to notice.

Restricted to questions where that comparison is meaningful — the **thirty** whose gold is an integer
from 2 to 10, since a list's length can only be held against the gold _number_ when the gold is a count:

| partition | n      | list shorter than gold | equal | longer |
| --------- | ------ | ---------------------- | ----- | ------ |
| correct   | 20     | 4                      | **7** | 9      |
| **wrong** | **10** | **6**                  | **0** | 4      |

**Not one wrong counting answer lists the gold number of items.** Six list fewer, and the shape is
stated by a record in its own words: two mentions of one boots exchange, then _"These two turns refer to
the same exchange/pickup event, so they count as one item"_, then `1` against a gold of `3`. The
contract's existing rule — _"do not merge two items into one"_ — was read and overruled, which is the
point: **a rule about merging cannot supply an item that was never listed.**

**And §13.86.2's prediction 3 was vacuous.** It required that at least five of the ten MR questions that
turned wrong under the role filter carry assistant-role gold, and it observed ten of ten. §13.87.3 then
measured why: `totalAll / total` is exactly 2.0 on **120 of 121** MR questions, so _essentially every_ MR
question carries assistant-role gold and the prediction could not have failed. The 10/10 was a base rate
dressed as a finding. Recorded here because it was quoted as the premise for a companion-assistant policy
that §13.87 then set aside; the premise was measured, and it was a tautology.

### 13.92.2 The registration

**One variable:** `ask: sweep`. Everything else is §10.3's adopted configuration — `evidenceRoles: user`
reaching `multi-session,temporal`, 48,000 characters, cap 400 on those two routes, `retrieval-hybrid` at
k=256, four repetitions. The registered `ask` stays `enumerated`; this dispatch overrides it, which is
what keeps the parity test between §10.3 and the dispatch table passing on a run that is not this
experiment.

The reach is **the multi-session route alone**, and unlike `enumerated` the other five routes are not
`computed` — they fall through to their shipped blocks. That makes IE, KU, ABS and TR an internal
control rather than four more subjects.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                                                | falsified if                     |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| **1** | median **session lines** per MR response ≥ **12**, and ≥ 90% of MR records write at least one                                             | median < 8, or < 90%             |
| **2** | on the thirty counting questions, median **item-bearing lines** rises from **4.0** (correct 4.0, wrong **2.5**) to **≥ 6**                | < 5                              |
| **3** | MR's mean rises **84.25 → ≥ 88**                                                                                                          | ≤ 86                             |
| **4** | of the six under-listing counting questions (`0a995998`, `6d550036`, `88432d0a`, `c18a7dc8`, `8e91e7d9`, `21d02d0d`), **≥ 3** are correct | ≤ 1                              |
| **5** | IE, KU, ABS and TR reproduce their `promptChars` **to the character** and their window turns exactly                                      | any change                       |
| **6** | MR's window stays **≥ 168 turns** and MR's first-repetition abstentions stay **≤ 10**                                                     | < 165 turns, or ≥ 13 abstentions |

The baseline in prediction 2 is read by `--counting`, which is the table that produced the counts in
§13.92.1; it reports 4.0 for the correct answers and **2.5** for the wrong ones. Saying "3–4" here
before that table existed would have been an estimation, and the campaign's rule is that a baseline is
a number the tool prints.

Prediction 3's margin is deliberately smaller than prediction 4's confidence: the block costs **48
characters** more than `enumerated`'s (measured, 1,463 against 1,415), which is 0.2 of a turn, so the
room is unchanged and the mean has to move on the mechanism. Prediction 4 is the sharp one because it
names six questions before the run exists; prediction 3 exists so that a scattered gain across the whole
capability cannot be claimed from six question ids alone.

**The ceiling, computed before the run.** A sweep cannot fix more than the questions that are counts.
Classifying MR's 37 wrong answers in `39367801501` by the shape of the gold:

| gold              | wrong  | correct |
| ----------------- | ------ | ------- |
| count, 2 – 10     | **10** | 20      |
| count, above 10   | 6      | 9       |
| prose             | 9      | 14      |
| duration          | 6      | 14      |
| money             | 4      | 23      |
| percent / decimal | 2      | 4       |

So the ask axis's ceiling on MR is **84.25 + 16 = 100.25** — every counting question repaired and
nothing else moved — and the registered threshold of 88 asks for a quarter of that. The other 21 wrong
answers are amounts, durations, percentages and prose, where a line per session has **nothing to
count**, and no wording of this contract reaches them. Writing that down before the numbers exists is
what keeps a later success from being read as the ask axis being unbounded.

### 13.92.3 What each outcome would mean

- **1, 2 and 4 hold, 3 holds**: the reader's failure was work-list coverage, the ask axis still has room,
  and the next question is whether the sweep should also apply to the temporal route (which counts days
  and durations rather than items).
- **1 and 2 hold, 3 and 4 fail**: the responses sweep and still miscount. Then the arithmetic is the
  reader's, not the prompt's, and the campaign's remaining MR levers are the model and the evidence
  ordering rather than any wording.
- **1 fails**: the model ignores the shape it was given — which `--sweep` counts rather than smooths, so
  the artifact will say how many records wrote no line at all. That is a statement about instruction
  compliance at 174 turns, and it would close the ask axis for this route.
- **5 fails**: the reach claim is wrong and the run is not a single variable. §13.73's rule: the three
  untouched capabilities must reproduce to the character, and a run that moves them is unreadable.

### 13.92.4 What was built, and the instrument the mechanism needs

`EvidenceAsk` gains `sweep`; `ASK_ROUTES.sweep` is `['multi-session']`; the block is `extractive`'s, with
the merging sentence, the two steps inserted above the closing line, and the closing line **replaced** —
§13.56's placement finding, that a rule above the close loses to it. Step 1 asks for one line per
session, `Session <n>: <items, or none>`, and says that a session with no line is a session the reader
did not look at; Step 2 counts the items those lines name; the close makes the count compulsory once any
line names anything.

`--sweep` is the reader for that shape, and it **refuses** an artifact whose `ask` is not `sweep`, because
a table of session lines read from an `enumerated` run would report zero and look like a treatment that
never reached the prompt. It counts, rather than smooths, the records that wrote no session line, and
flags a count that matches the number of item-bearing lines.

Tests: `evidence-ask-reach.test.ts` pins the block's content and the five byte-identical routes; the
count is asserted against `--sweep`'s refusal, its counting, the ignored-shape record and the
count-matches-lines flag. The arm's table gains the value and `test_ask_table_parity.py` compares the two
key sets by source, which is the check that caught §13.35's startup rejection.

## 13.93 The sweep walks the whole document and finds the same two items

### 13.93.1 The readings (`39389557774`, 2h03m38s, drift 500/500)

| #     | prediction (§13.92.2)                                 | observed                              | verdict                                                       |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **1** | median session lines ≥ 12, ≥ 90% of records write one | **44.0**, **121 of 121**              | **holds**                                                     |
| **2** | median item-bearing lines 4.0 → **≥ 6**               | **2.0**                               | **falsified**                                                 |
| **3** | MR mean 84.25 → **≥ 88**                              | **58.25** (54–60)                     | **falsified**                                                 |
| **4** | ≥ 3 of the six under-listing questions correct        | **2**                                 | **neither** — see §13.93.3                                    |
| **5** | IE/KU/ABS/TR reproduce `promptChars` to the character | ABS and KU identical; IE and TR moved | **falsified**, and the reason is a defect in the registration |
| **6** | MR window ≥ 168 turns, abstentions ≤ 10               | 174 turns, **14** abstentions         | window holds, abstentions **falsified**                       |

Registered statistic **+25.35pp** (was +36.55), roster mean **347.8** (was 405.0). Per capability, mean over
four repetitions: ABS 29.25, IE **126.75**, KU 63.0, MR **58.25**, TR **70.50**.

### 13.93.2 The mechanism landed exactly, and it did nothing

The instruction was followed: **every one of the 121 MR responses wrote a line for every session**, a median of
**44 lines**, and the `--sweep` census finds **0 records with no scan**. The model walked the entire document.

And the median count of item-bearing lines is **2.0** — the same as `enumerated`'s 2.0. The walk added
forty-two lines of `none` and found the same two items.

That is the finding, and it is a negative one worth more than the accuracy number: **the reader's enumeration is
not limited by how much of the document it looks at.** It is limited by what it recognises as an instance of the
question's action. `0a995998` states it: the question asks about items to _pick up or return from a store_; the
window contains a blazer at the dry cleaner and two mentions of boots at Zara, and the response lists the two boots
mentions, merges them, and answers `1`. The blazer is in a session the sweep printed as `none`.

So the ask axis's "make the reader look harder" branch is closed. What remains is the question's wording against
the evidence's wording, which is a retrieval-matching problem and not an instruction one.

### 13.93.3 Prediction 4 was drawn with a gap, and that is a defect in the prediction

It said "≥ 3 correct", falsified "≤ 1", and observed **2**. A prediction with a hole in the middle cannot be
decided, and the honest reading is that it was written badly: the threshold should have been contiguous
(`≥ 3` / `≤ 2`). Recorded rather than reinterpreted, because re-drawing a falsifier after the number exists is the
one thing a registration cannot survive.

### 13.93.4 Prediction 5 could not have held, and the reason is structural

The registration asked IE, KU, ABS and TR to reproduce their `promptChars` to the character. **ABS and KU did**
(46,737 and 46,841, byte-identical). IE and TR did not, and the cause is not a leak: the _previous_ run's ask was
`enumerated`, whose reach is `multi-session, flat, temporal` — so the flat and temporal routes were reading
`computed`'s merged block, and switching to `sweep` removed it from them. Their blocks lost ~1,250 characters and
their windows grew by 115 and 246 characters.

That is not a surprise in hindsight: it is exactly what §13.20 measured, where replacing the temporal block cost TR
**27.6 points**. This run's TR fell **24.25** and IE **7.5**, which is that cost, not a sweep effect.

**The defect is in the registration.** A single-route ask can only be tested against a baseline whose other routes
already read what the new ask leaves them reading — and `enumerated` reached three routes, so no such baseline
exists in the archive. Either the experiment must accept that the other routes move, or the ask must be dispatched
over a baseline run that used `route` (the shipped ask) so the only change is on one route. The second is the
correct design and it is written down here for the next attempt.

### 13.93.5 The format the answer arrived in, and the audit that came out of it

**69 of 121** MR answers are the raw session list rather than a number. The parser slices a response after its
**last** `Step <n> —` heading, and this contract's Step 2 says "reply with the count alone" — so the model wrote the
lines under Step 1 and then the number with no heading, and the reader returned the whole list as the answer.

That is a contract defect with a one-line lesson: **an ask that wants a list and then a number has to make the
second heading compulsory**, because the parser's rule is positional and `enumerated` only survived it because its
Step 2 was a sentence.

And it exposed something the campaign had never measured: **the last scoring channel accepts a transcript.**
`--final` audits the correct answers to questions whose gold **is** a number, and asks whether the response's
closing line states it:

| run                                   | MR correct on numeric golds | closing line states the gold |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `39367801501` (adopted, `enumerated`) | 31                          | **30**                       |
| `39389557774` (`sweep`)               | 22                          | **18**                       |

So on this run **4 of 22** correct answers end on a different number than the one they were scored against — the
transcript contained the gold somewhere — while the adopted configuration has **one** such record in 31. The
campaign's archive survives the audit; this run does not, and its 58.25 is an upper bound rather than a
measurement.

### 13.93.6 Verdict, and what it redirects to

**Falsified, and adopted nothing.** §10.3 is unchanged: `ask: enumerated`.

What the run bought:

- the ask axis is closed for _structure_: a reader that walks 44 sessions still names two items, so the deficit is
  what it counts as an instance, not how much it reads;
- one hypothesis is now pointed: the gold turn and the question use **different words** (a blazer at the dry
  cleaner for _pick up or return from a store_), and the reference pipeline — 20 questions ahead on MR at half the
  budget — carries `expansionQueries` in its own trace for exactly this reason, retrieving with phrases the
  question does not contain;
- a scoring audit that did not exist, and an answer-format rule that the next list-shaped ask must obey.

## 13.94 A second consultation that audits membership, not arithmetic

### 13.94.1 The premise, which §13.93 measured rather than assumed

Three readings, all on `39367801501`'s artifact and the sweep run that followed it:

- **the reader walks and still misses.** `39389557774` wrote a line for every one of ~44 sessions in
  every MR window, with 0 records skipping, and the median count of item-bearing lines stayed at
  **2.0** — the same as the contract that does not ask for a walk;
- **the numbers are in the window.** `--numbers`: of 31 wrong MR answers with a number in the gold,
  **24** have those digits inside the carried evidence and **7** do not. The seven are retrieval; the
  twenty-four are the reader's;
- **the list is short.** `--counting`: on the thirty questions whose gold is a count from 2 to 10,
  **six of the ten** wrong answers list fewer items than the gold and **none** lists exactly that many.

Record `0a995998` is the whole story in one row: two mentions of one boots exchange listed, merged into
one item, `1` against a gold of `3`, and a blazer at the dry cleaner sitting in a session the response
marked `none`.

So the pass this section registers is not a re-ask, not a retry of an abstention, and not more
evidence. It is a **second look at the list**, asked for the three membership decisions a list can get
wrong.

### 13.94.2 The registration

**One variable:** `reviewPass: audit`. Everything else is §10.3's adopted configuration, including
`ask: enumerated`.

The reach is **implicit and therefore structural**: the pass lives in `answerSessions`, so it reaches
the multi-session route by construction and no other route can be configured into it. That is the
direct answer to §13.93.4, where the ask's reach moved three routes and the run could not separate the
treatment from the cost.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                                                     | falsified if                  |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **1** | IE, KU, ABS and TR reproduce their `promptChars` **to the character** and their window turns exactly                                           | any change                    |
| **2** | the audit changes the answer on **≥ 20** of 121 MR questions relative to `39367801501`, and the flips are net positive                         | < 12 changed, or net negative |
| **3** | MR's mean rises **84.25 → ≥ 88**                                                                                                               | ≤ 86                          |
| **4** | of the six under-listing counting questions (`0a995998`, `6d550036`, `88432d0a`, `c18a7dc8`, `8e91e7d9`, `21d02d0d`), **≥ 3** are correct      | ≤ 2                           |
| **5** | MR's `promptChars` falls to **40,000 – 44,500** (the audit's instruction quotes the first pass, so it buys less evidence with the same budget) | outside                       |
| **6** | MR's first-repetition abstentions stay **≤ 12**, and every capability's window turns are unchanged                                             | ≥ 13                          |

Prediction 4 is drawn **contiguously** this time — §13.93.3 recorded the gapped falsifier as a defect
rather than reinterpreting it — and prediction 2 is the mechanism read on the artifact rather than
asserted: an audit that never changes an answer has measured nothing, which is the same rule
`retryArmed`/`retryFired` enforced for the bare-abstention retry.

### 13.94.3 What the run cannot show, registered instead of hidden

`lastReview()` exists in the product and reports the first answer, the final answer and whether they
differ — per question. It is **not in the artifact**: the roster has no field for it, and adding one
means threading a per-question value through `runBenchmark` → `scoreEvaluation` → `QuestionRecord`.

So prediction 2 is read from `--paired` (the answer a question _had_ in `39367801501` against the
answer it _has_ now), which measures the same thing from outside at the price of comparing two runs
rather than one. The per-question capture is §13.95, and it comes before any future pass whose
mechanism is "the second look changed something specific".

### 13.94.4 Why this and not query expansion

§13.93.6 pointed at the mismatch between the question's words and the evidence's, and the reference
pipeline carries `expansionQueries` for exactly that. It is the next candidate, not this one, for a
measured reason: expansion changes **what enters the window**, and `--numbers` says the gold's digits
are already in the window for 24 of the 31 wrong numeric answers. A retrieval change cannot help those
twenty-four; a membership review can address all of them.

The order is therefore: fix what the reader does with what it has, then widen what it has.

## 13.96 The second look lengthens the list and lowers the accuracy

### 13.96.1 The readings (`39416366870`, 2h12m50s, drift 500/500)

| #     | prediction (§13.94.2)                                                              | observed                                                                       | verdict                                                      |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **1** | IE, KU, ABS and TR reproduce `promptChars` to the character and their window turns | **all four identical** (46,694 / 46,864 / 46,827 / 47,137; 72 / 61 / 62 / 179) | **holds**                                                    |
| **2** | ≥ 20 MR answers change, and the flips are net positive                             | **73 changed**, 7 repaired, **21 damaged**                                     | changed holds, **net −14** → **falsified**                   |
| **3** | MR mean 84.25 → ≥ 88                                                               | **70.00** (69–72)                                                              | **falsified**                                                |
| **4** | ≥ 3 of the six under-listing questions correct                                     | **1**                                                                          | **falsified**                                                |
| **5** | MR's `promptChars` in 40,000 – 44,500                                              | **46,417**                                                                     | **falsified** (the audit re-selects to nearly the same room) |
| **6** | MR abstentions ≤ 12 and every window unchanged                                     | 10 abstentions; four controls unchanged, **MR 174 → 175 turns**                | abstentions hold, MR's own window moved by one               |

Registered statistic **+34.20pp** (was +36.55); roster mean **394.0** (was 405.0). Per capability: ABS 29.50,
IE **136.25**, KU 63.25, MR **70.00**, TR **95.00**.

### 13.96.2 The control held, for the first time in this campaign

The four untouched capabilities reproduce their `promptChars` **to the character** and their window
counts exactly. That is what §13.92 could not do — its ask reached three routes and the run could not
separate the treatment from the cost — and it is the reason the reach was made structural this time.
The method fix worked even though the treatment did not.

One caveat that has to be stated rather than buried: IE reads **136.25** against 134.25 in
`39367801501` on **identical prompts** (median 61 turns, 46,864 characters, both runs). Two questions
from identical input is §109.4's resolution showing up in a place where nothing was supposed to move,
and it is the cleanest demonstration the campaign has that a two-question difference is not a finding.

### 13.96.3 The mechanism worked and it made things worse

The pass is not inert: **73 of 121** MR answers differ from `39367801501`, and the lists got longer —
the median item-bearing count on the counting questions is **6.0** for the wrong answers, against
**2.5** in the run that had no second look.

So the thing §13.92 could not buy — a longer list — this pass bought. And the accuracy fell anyway:

|                                         | `39367801501` (one pass) | `39416366870` (audit) |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------- |
| MR median items, wrong counting answers | 2.5                      | **6.0**               |
| MR correct                              | 84 of 121                | **70**                |
| repaired / damaged                      | —                        | **7 / 21**            |

**The revision is right 7 times in 73 (9.6%)** on the questions it touches, while the first pass was
already right on 84 of 121. A second look whose precision is one in ten, applied to sixty percent of
the answers, is a net loss by arithmetic — and that is what the mean shows.

The mechanism behind it is visible in one record. `gpt4_194be4b3` asks how many musical instruments
the user owns; the gold is 4; the first pass answered 4. The audit's own review line reads _"the only
'new' item (ukulele) is aspirational, not owned, so it should not be added. The first pass's five are
all supported. No missing owned instruments."_ — and then it answers **5**. The review and the number
disagree inside one response, which is the failure this pass was built to prevent, now happening in
the pass itself.

### 13.96.4 What this retires

**The membership review is retired as an instruction.** The measurement says the reader's second
judgement is worse than its first on this workload, and no rewording of the three checks can change
that: the pass already _wrote_ the correct review and answered against it.

What survives is the diagnosis, and it sharpens: the deficit is not list length (`enumerated` gets 2
items, `sweep` gets 44 lines and 2 items, `audit` gets 6 items and fewer correct answers), and it is
not the reader's willingness to look. It is **which mentions the reader treats as instances** — a
matching decision made before any list exists, and therefore a retrieval-side decision rather than a
prompt-side one.

That is exactly where §13.94.4 put query expansion: the gold turn and the question use different
words. The difference now is that this is no longer a hypothesis about where to look next; it is the
only candidate left standing after three prompt-side attempts (structure, membership, and the first
pass's own ledger) have each been measured and each failed.

### 13.96.5 Adoption

None. `reviewPass` stays `none` in §10.3 and in the dispatch table; the value `audit` remains
dispatchable so a future run can reproduce this refutation, which is the same reason §13.27 kept the
frozen `session` unit.

## 13.97 The question's words are not the evidence's words

### 13.97.1 What the three failed attempts localised

Three prompt-side attempts have now been measured on the multi-session route, and each one moved the
thing it was designed to move while accuracy fell or failed to rise:

| attempt               | mechanism it bought                          | reading                          |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `enumerated` (§13.34) | a two-step contract, list then compute       | adopted, MR 70 at its best       |
| `sweep` (§13.93)      | a walk over all 44 sessions, 44 ledger lines | median items 2.0, unchanged      |
| `audit` (§13.94)      | a membership review of the first pass        | median items 6.0, **MR 84 → 70** |

The third one is the decisive one because the mechanism was _visible in the response and did not
control the answer_: `gpt4_194be4b3` wrote "the only 'new' item (ukulele) is aspirational, not
owned, so it should not be added" and then answered 5 against a gold of 4. A reader whose own
review says the item is not there, and whose count includes it, is not failing to look and is not
failing to write a list. It is deciding **which mentions count as instances** — and that decision is
made before any list exists.

`--numbers` localises where such a decision can fail. On `39416366870`, of the 44 wrong MR answers
that state a number, the gold's digit string **appears nowhere in the window for 12**. A digit that
appears nowhere was never read; no wording reaches it. The other 32 are in the window and are a
reader problem that three attempts have failed to fix.

So this section moves the one stage the campaign has not touched since §13.64: **what the ranking
was asked**.

### 13.97.2 The treatment

`CORTEX_MEMORY_QUERY_EXPANSION`, `none` or `llm`.

`llm` adds one model call per **multi-session** question, made **before the relevance index is
built**. The response is parsed into at most four activity phrases, and `RelevanceCase.queries`
carries them into `buildRetrievalRelevanceIndex`, which retrieves that question against
`[question, ...phrases]`. The score a turn receives is unchanged in meaning: the maximum cosine
across the queries that surfaced it, which is what `retrieveTopKByQueries` already computes when it
fuses several rankings.

Five design decisions, each with the alternative it rules out:

- **Activity phrases, not synonyms.** The failing questions count past activities; the evidence is
  written as the activity ("led a consumer-research project") while the question names the category
  ("how many projects"). A synonym of the category retrieves every session that mentions the
  category, which is what the bare question already did.
- **Four phrases, folded and bounded.** The queries are fused by reciprocal rank, so two copies of
  one phrase are a weight rather than a phrase; duplicates are folded before the bound is applied,
  and a bound of zero returns nothing rather than one phrase.
- **A refusal is dropped whole.** The reference pipeline's own trace records an expansion call that
  answered `"I don't have access to your past conversations or evidence sessions"`, whose three
  sentences were then carried into retrieval as phrases. Here the head is tested for refusal
  markers, the whole response is discarded when it declines, and the artifact counts the questions
  that happened to.
- **The phrases are produced before the index, not during the answer.** `CortexMemory`'s
  `relevanceFor` is a synchronous table lookup; a phrase written at answer time would read the
  index's floor score (-2, below every cosine) and the treatment would be reported while measuring
  nothing. This is why the call sits in the arm beside the index construction rather than in the
  product.
- **Throwing, not degrading.** A transport failure propagates and the run fails. A run dispatched
  with `llm` that silently answered from the bare question would publish the control's reading under
  the treatment's name — the §10.10 shape.

The four untouched capabilities keep `queries: []`, which is byte-identical to the field's absence,
so their queries, ranking, window and `promptChars` are structurally unchanged. That is this
dispatch's internal control, and it is the check §13.96.2 established the method for.

### 13.97.3 The input ceiling, and which knob paid for it

The workflow held 24 of GitHub's 25 `workflow_dispatch` inputs, and the guard in
`test_dispatch_inputs.py` refuses 25 — a workflow at the ceiling is one registration away from a
`422` at dispatch time. This section needed the last slot, so one knob became a constant:
`cortex_memory_confidence` is now fixed at `none` in the workflow's environment.

That is not a convenience, and the difference matters because §13.17.2 rejected exactly this move
once. What it rejected was deleting a **registered** knob whose configuration a later run might
want. What this deletes is an **unreachable** one: the registered configuration sets **both gates to
0**, the value function is bounded below by 0, so `value >= 0` holds for every turn and the
confidence signal cannot change a single admission decision under any dispatch this arm runs. Its
reach is zero, and §49 had already measured that it does not carry the arm on its own. Restoring it
as an input costs a registration, which the ceiling guard will demand be traded rather than added.

### 13.97.4 Predictions, registered before the dispatch

The dispatch is `--set cortex_memory_query_expansion=llm` on §10.3's configuration, which is
`39367801501`'s configuration with `reviewPass` back at `none`, N = 500, four repetitions.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                                              | falsified if                                                                      |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **1** | the mechanism runs: config line reads `queryExpansion=llm` and `expansion=121q/…p/0r`, with at least **242** phrases (two per question) | `questions` is 0 (wiring), or `refused` exceeds 12 (a model that will not expand) |
| **2** | the four untouched capabilities reproduce `39367801501`'s `promptChars` **to the character** and their window turns **to the turn**     | any of the four moves                                                             |
| **3** | MR mean **≥ 78** (against 70.00 in `39416366870` and 84.25 in `39367801501`)                                                            | MR ≤ 74                                                                           |
| **4** | the wrong answers whose gold digit is absent fall from **12 to ≤ 8**                                                                    | 9 or more remain absent                                                           |
| **5** | MR abstentions stay **≤ 10**, and `soft_refusal` / `plan_output` do not rise above 0                                                    | either counts positive                                                            |
| **6** | MR's `promptChars` stays within **46,417 ± 3,000** (expansion moves the order, not the room)                                            | outside that band                                                                 |

Prediction 3 is stated against **both** prior runs on purpose: 84.25 is what this configuration
scored before the audit pass doubled its consultations, so "expansion recovers what the audit lost"
and "expansion beats the one-pass control" are different claims and only the second is interesting.

### 13.97.5 The ceiling this experiment cannot pass

Even if every absent-digit question is repaired, MR moves 70 → 82 at most, and the reference
pipeline's MR is 103 of 121 (85.1%). The remaining 32 wrong answers already had the digits in the
window. So the honest reading of a positive result is "retrieval is worth N questions", not "the
route is closed", and a null result does not retire expansion in general — it retires _this_
prompt, on _this_ workload, at _this_ pool width.

### 13.97.6 Verification before dispatch

- `pnpm check` **exit 0**; `cortex-eval` **1985 tests**, `cortex-memory` **402**, `tools` **509
  passed + 1 skipped + 50 subtests**; four coverage dimensions **100%**.
- New guards: `query-expansion.test.ts` (22 tests, every parser refusal asserted by the input that
  triggers it), three index tests for `queries`, five arm tests for the option and both artifact
  renderings, and `test_query_expansion_wiring.py` (7 source-level links, mutation-checked: replacing
  `[entry.question, ...(entry.queries ?? [])]` with `[entry.question]` fails the suite).
- The parser's prompt and its bound are asserted as literals (`at most 4`), because a test that read
  the constant would pass on any default.

## 13.98 The expansion reached the ranking and moved nothing

### 13.98.1 The readings (`39449569048`, 1h52m)

| #     | prediction (§13.97.4)                                                      | observed                                                                       | verdict                                        |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **1** | `queryExpansion=llm`, `expansion=121q/…p/0r`, ≥ 242 phrases                | **`121q/347p/0r`** — 2.87 phrases per question, no refusal                     | **holds**                                      |
| **2** | the four untouched capabilities reproduce to the character and to the turn | **all four identical** (46,694 / 46,864 / 46,827 / 47,137; 72 / 61 / 62 / 179) | **holds**                                      |
| **3** | MR mean ≥ 78                                                               | **84.75** (83–87)                                                              | **holds, and it means nothing** — see §13.98.2 |
| **4** | absent gold digits 12 → ≤ 8                                                | **6**                                                                          | **holds on a wrong baseline** — see §13.98.3   |
| **5** | MR abstentions ≤ 10                                                        | **12**                                                                         | **falsified**                                  |
| **6** | MR `promptChars` 46,417 ± 3,000                                            | **46,204**                                                                     | **holds**                                      |

Registered statistic **+37.20pp** (was +36.55); roster mean **407.0** (was 405.0). Per capability:
ABS 29.0 (29–29), IE **136.25** (135–138), KU 62.75 (61–66), MR **84.75** (83–87), TR 94.25 (87–99).

### 13.98.2 Prediction 3 held and the treatment did not work

84.75 against the control's **84.25** is a difference of **half a question**, inside both runs' own
spreads (81–88 against 83–87). The prediction was written against two numbers — 70.00 from the audit
run and 84.25 from the adopting configuration — and only the second is a control. Against it, the
effect is zero.

The per-question transitions say the same thing at the resolution where it hurts:

| route                                                 | changed           | repaired | damaged | net    |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | -------- | ------- | ------ |
| **MR** (treated)                                      | 27 of 121 (22.3%) | 12       | 12      | **0**  |
| **TR** (untreated, window identical to the character) | 24 of 127 (18.9%) | 12       | 9       | **+3** |

A route that received **no treatment at all** moved nineteen per cent of its answers. That is the
noise floor of this instrument, and MR's zero is indistinguishable from it. The audit pass (§13.96)
looked worse than the control at 7 repaired against 21 damaged; expansion looks level at 12 against 12. Neither is a measurement of the treatment, because the untreated route moves by the same order.

### 13.98.3 The mechanism ran; the window it changed was not where the loss was

`expansion=121q/347p/0r` is not a configuration that failed to arrive: every multi-session question
was expanded, four phrases each on average, none refused. The pool did change — 27 answers moved —
so the mechanism is real.

What it did **not** change is how much of the answer's evidence the reader saw. Across the 27
transitions, the change in gold turns carried is `0` for 13 of them, `+1` for 7, `−1` for 4, `+2` for
2 and `−2` for 1. The window's gold content is essentially fixed, which is what a relevance fusion
over a fixed 256-wide pool does: it re-ranks, and a turn that ranked fifth under the question alone
but never appeared under a phrase loses its place to a turn that appeared in both lists at rank 100.

That is visible in the direction of the damage: all eight `correct → numeric_mismatch` transitions on
MR are questions where the gold was carried **before** and still carried after. The reader was not
starved of evidence; it was given a different window over the same session.

Prediction 4 has to be withdrawn as stated rather than reported as a win. It was registered against
**12 absent digits**, which is `39416366870`'s number — the audit run. The adopting configuration's
own number is **7**, and expansion moved it to **6**. The flow underneath is bidirectional: three
golds left the window (`7024f17c`, `9aaed6a3`, `e6041065`) while two entered (`d851d5ba`,
`e3038f8c`). A net of one question, on a quantity whose per-run spread this campaign has never
measured, is not a retrieval improvement. Registering a prediction against the nearest number in the
document rather than against the control's own is the defect, and it is recorded here so the next
registration reads its baseline from the run it is actually comparing to.

### 13.98.4 What this retires

**"The residual multi-session loss is a retrieval-side gap" is retired.** It was the last candidate
