standing after three prompt-side attempts, and this section administered the strongest form of it:
a model-written, route-scoped, four-phrase expansion that reached every question. It changed a fifth
of the answers and left the score where it was.

What survives is not another hypothesis about the arm. It is a fact about the instrument: **the
answer layer is unstable at 18–22% per route per re-run**, while the evidence layer is stable to the
character. Every experiment this campaign could run next is a search for an effect of five questions
or fewer — and five questions is a fifth of MR's gross movement (27 of 121).

Gross is not net, and the distinction is the whole of §13.99: a five-question effect is only
detectable if the **net** difference between two runs of one configuration is smaller than five, which
nobody has measured. No threshold is stated in this section for that reason.

### 13.98.5 Adoption

None. `queryExpansion` stays `none` in §10.3 and in the dispatch table; `llm` remains dispatchable so
a later run can reproduce this refutation, and the implementation stays because the _mechanism_ was
verified even though the _effect_ was not.

## 13.99 The next variable is the instrument, not the arm

### 13.99.1 Why the arm cannot be moved next

§13.98.2 measured the noise floor without trying to: TR received no treatment and its window was
identical to the character, yet 24 of its 127 answers differ from the control's. Until that number is
measured deliberately — twice on the same configuration, with the per-route agreement counted — no
future registration can state a threshold that distinguishes an effect from a re-sample.

So the next dispatch is the **control against itself**: §10.3's configuration with
`queryExpansion=none`, read against `39367801501` with the same paired transition table this section
used. Its product is a **noise floor per capability**, not an accuracy claim.

### 13.99.2 Predictions

| #     | prediction                                                                                                   | falsified if      |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| **1** | MR agreement between two runs of one configuration is **75–85%** (i.e. 18–30 of 121 answers differ)          | outside that band |
| **2** | TR agreement is **75–85%**, the same band, because §13.98.2 measured 19% on a route no treatment touched     | outside           |
| **3** | ABS agreement is **≥ 93%**, because its answers are a token or a short phrase and its state is nearly binary | below 93%         |
| **4** | the roster mean of the re-run is within **±6** of 405.0                                                      | outside           |
| **5** | the four window medians reproduce `39367801501` **to the character**                                         | any moves         |

If predictions 1 and 2 hold, the campaign's resolution is stated as a number, and every later
registration must name an effect **larger than twice that band** to be detectable. If they fail —
agreement above 90% — then §13.98.2's TR movement came from something other than the endpoint, and
that becomes the defect to find.

### 13.99.3 What is built beside it

`tools/readout-arm-run.py --stability <before.json> <after.json>`, because the transition table this section
quotes was produced by an inline script and §13.38 forbade exactly that. The subcommand prints, per
capability: answers compared, changed, changed share, and the transition matrix; plus the same counts
restricted to the treated route. Its tests pin the two properties the floor depends on — that an
identical pair reads as 0% changed, and that a state change and a text change are counted separately,
because a run whose answers are re-worded but scored the same must not look unstable.

Built and green before the re-read: four tests in `test_readout_arm_run.py` (identical pair reads
0.0%; a re-worded pair reads a text change and no state change; a scored change appears in the
transition block; two rosters naming different questions are refused), `tools` **513 passed + 1
skipped + 51 subtests**. Run against `39367801501` and `39449569048` it reads the answer layer's own
instability: **text** differs on 286 of 500 answers (57.2%), **state** on 65 (13.0%) — and the per
capability split is the floor §13.99.2 is registered against.

| capability | `39367801501`    | `39509698041`       | net       |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ------------------- | --------- |
| ABS        | 29.25 (29–30)    | 29.5 (29–30)        | +0.25     |
| IE         | 134.25 (133–135) | 134.5 (134–136)     | +0.25     |
| KU         | 62.5 (60–64)     | 60.5 (59–63)        | −2.0      |
| **MR**     | 84.25 (81–88)    | **85.2** (83–87)    | **+0.95** |
| **TR**     | 94.75 (94–95)    | **97.0** (95–99)    | **+2.25** |
| **roster** | 405.0 (397–412)  | **406.8** (400–415) | **+1.8**  |

Registered statistic **+36.15pp** against +36.55. Five predictions, all of them held:

| #     | prediction (§13.99.2)                   | observed                                      | verdict   |
| ----- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| **1** | MR agreement 75–85%                     | **80.2%** (24 of 121 changed)                 | **holds** |
| **2** | TR agreement 75–85%                     | **81.1%** (24 of 127)                         | **holds** |
| **3** | ABS agreement ≥ 93%                     | **100%** (0 of 30)                            | **holds** |

### 13.100.2 The number every later registration has to clear

The net difference between two runs of one configuration, by capability:

| capability | repaired | damaged | **net** |
| ---------- | -------- | ------- | ------- |
| ABS        | 0        | 0       | 0       |
| IE         | 3        | 3       | 0       |
| KU         | 2        | 3       | −1      |
| MR         | 11       | 13      | **−2**  |
| TR         | 8        | 12      | **−4**  |

**A four-question net movement happens with no treatment at all.** So a single run cannot support a
claim smaller than five questions on any route, and the two runs' means differ by 1.8 questions on the
roster. This is an observation, not a confidence interval — two runs give one difference, and the
interval needs repetitions this campaign has not spent. It is stated as a **lower bound on the
threshold**: whatever the true spread is, it is at least four questions on TR and two on MR.

That is the resolution figure §13.96 and §13.98 were missing. Every measurement in this document
that claimed a movement of one to three questions — the audit pass's −14 on MR is the exception —
was inside it.

### 13.100.3 What the two runs agree on, and why it matters more than the disagreement

The text layer moved on 281 of 500 answers (56.2%) while the state layer moved on 59 (11.8%). A model
that rephrases six answers in ten and re-scores one in ten is a model whose **answers are noisy but
whose judgements are mostly stable** — and it means any future mechanism must be judged on states,
never on strings. The `--stability` subcommand exists to make that distinction runnable rather than
remembered.

ABS moved zero answers in both directions, twice. It is now the campaign's **fixed control**: thirty
questions whose answer is a token, whose window is identical to the character, and which have not
moved a single state across any pair of runs measured. A treatment that moves ABS has broken
something.

### 13.100.4 Adoption

The configuration is unchanged; the _reading_ is what changed. §10.3 keeps `queryExpansion: none`, and
the roster's registered point estimate stays with `39367801501` until a run beats **406.8 ± 4** by more
than the noise.

## 13.101 Self-consistency: spend the noise instead of fighting it

### 13.101.1 Why this and not a fourth prompt

Three prompt-side attempts and one retrieval-side attempt have been measured. The reading that
survived all four is §13.100.2: the reader's **judgement** flips on 11.8% of questions between two
identical runs, and 24 of 121 MR answers change with no treatment at all.

A mechanism that samples that flip and takes a majority is the only candidate in the campaign whose
target is the measured defect itself rather than a hypothesis about it. It is not a prompt change —
the prompt is byte-identical — and it is not a retrieval change: the window is unchanged. It is three
consultations of the same question over the same evidence, and a strict majority.

The alternative — a stronger reader model — was considered and deferred, not rejected: a reasoning
model's latency would multiply every pass by an unknown factor against a 90-minute per-pass ceiling,
and the first thing to measure is whether voting helps at all, on the model every archived artifact
was produced with.

### 13.101.2 The treatment

`CORTEX_MEMORY_SELF_CONSISTENCY`, `none` or `3`.

`3` consults the model three times with the **same prompt** on the multi-session route, parses each
response, and returns the answer held by a strict majority (more than half of the three, `null`
included). With no strict majority — three different answers — the first pass is returned and the
question is recorded as a split. The four other routes are untouched by construction: the sampling
lives in `#promptSessionAware`, which only `answerSessions` reaches.

Three decisions worth stating:

- **`null` is a candidate.** A majority of declines is a decline. Excluding it would let two wrong
  answers outvote one abstention on a question the evidence cannot answer, which is the failure mode
  §13.34's closing line was written to prevent.
- **The first pass is the fallback, not the longest or the most confident.** With three distinct
  answers there is no majority to take, and inventing a tie-break would make the mechanism's behaviour
  depend on a string heuristic nothing measured.
- **The artifact records the agreement.** `vote=<unanimous>/<majority>/<split>` per run, so a null
  result can be read as "voting never disagreed" (the mechanism did not fire) rather than as "voting
  did not help".

### 13.101.3 The input ceiling, again

The workflow is at 25 inputs and `test_dispatch_inputs.py` refuses 25. `cortex_memory_threshold`
becomes the constant `0`.

The argument is the same one §13.97.3 used for `cortex_memory_confidence`, and it is a reach claim
rather than a preference: **the admission gate has been at 0 in every run this arm has ever
dispatched**, its one non-zero excursion (§10.9's `retrievalThreshold: 0.25`) abstained on 479 of 500
and lost 186 questions, and §12.3 measured the hit and miss score distributions to overlap almost
completely, so no cut in the reachable range can carry the arm. Admission-wide-open is the premise of
every experiment here, not a variable within it. `retrievalThreshold` — which decides whether admitted
evidence may be answered from — stays dispatchable, because that one gates a decision the runs
actually exercise.

### 13.101.4 Predictions, registered before the dispatch

| #     | prediction                                                                               | falsified if                                                                                           |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **1** | the mechanism runs: config reads `selfConsistency=3`, and `vote` is not `0/0/121`        | `unanimous + majority + split` is not 121                                                              |
| **2** | votes disagree often enough to matter: **split > 0** and unanimous ≤ **75%**             | unanimous = 100% (the endpoint is deterministic after all, and §13.100.2's movement has another cause) |
| **3** | MR mean **≥ 89** (85.2 + 4, i.e. above the measured floor)                               | MR ≤ 87                                                                                                |
| **4** | the four untouched capabilities reproduce `39509698041` to the character and to the turn | any moves                                                                                              |
| **5** | MR abstentions ≤ 10 and MR `promptChars` unchanged                                       | either moves                                                                                           |
| **6** | wall clock ≤ 3h                                                                          | longer                                                                                                 |

Prediction 3 is the one that decides adoption, and it is set at the floor rather than at a hoped-for
effect: four questions is the largest net movement two identical runs have produced, so a result at or
below it would not be evidence.

### 13.101.5 What a positive result would and would not mean

It would mean the arm can convert sampling noise into accuracy, which is a mechanism no prompt or
retrieval change has produced. It would **not** mean the arm is SOTA: MR at 89 is still below the
reference pipeline's 102, and the reference pipeline gets its 102 from a single sample of the same
model. What changes is that the mechanism is now measurable at the resolution the instrument actually
has.

## 13.102 Voting sampled the noise and could not spend it

### 13.102.1 The readings (`39529234665`, 2h17m)

| #     | prediction (§13.101.4)                                 | observed                                                          | verdict                                                            |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **1** | config reads `selfConsistency=3`, `vote` sums to 121   | **`vote=120/192/172`** — sums to **484**, four repetitions of 121 | **falsified as written** — the registration forgot the repetitions |
| **2** | `split > 0` and unanimous ≤ 75%                        | unanimous **24.8%**, majority 39.7%, split **35.5%**              | **holds**, far past the expectation                                |
| **3** | MR mean ≥ 89                                           | **86.2** (82–91)                                                  | **falsified**                                                      |
| **4** | four untouched capabilities reproduce to the character | identical (46,694 / 46,864 / 46,827 / 47,137)                     | **holds**                                                          |
| **5** | MR abstentions ≤ 10 and `promptChars` unchanged        | **10**; 46,186                                                    | **holds**                                                          |
| **6** | wall clock ≤ 3h                                        | **2h17m**                                                         | **holds**                                                          |

Registered statistic **+37.70pp** (was +36.55); roster **408.8** (399–421). Per capability: ABS 29.2
(29–30), IE 136.2 (136–137), KU 62.8 (59–67), **MR 86.2** (82–91), TR 94.2 (93–96).

### 13.102.2 The mechanism fired and the answer did not move

Three consultations of a byte-identical prompt disagreed on **75%** of questions: 172 of 484 votes
were three-way splits and only 120 were unanimous. So the treatment was administered, in the
strongest possible form — a reader that cannot reproduce itself three times in four.

MR moved 85.2 → **86.2**, one question, inside the ±2–4 floor §13.100.2 published. KU moved 60.5 →
62.8 and TR 97.0 → 94.2 with **no treatment at all**, which is the same floor seen from the other
side.

The reason is visible in what a vote can and cannot fix. A majority selects one of three readings;
it does not create a fourth. If all three readings share the same misreading — and §13.102.3 shows
they do — the vote faithfully returns it. Voting is a variance reducer, and this arm's error is
**bias**, not variance: the same 15 questions are under-counted by one in every sample.

### 13.102.3 Where the 37 wrong answers actually are

Classified by arithmetic direction against the gold (`39529234665`, first repetition). The split is
`tools/readout-arm-run.py --arithmetic`, not an inline script — §13.38's rule, and the reason
§13.103's fourth prediction can be re-derived by a reader:

| direction                         | count  | share |
| --------------------------------- | ------ | ----- |
| **under** (stated less than gold) | **15** | 41%   |
| abstention                        | 10     | 27%   |
| over                              | 6      | 16%   |
| non-numeric gold                  | 5      | 14%   |
| no number stated                  | 1      | 3%    |

Twelve of the fifteen under-counts are **off by exactly one** (`3→2` six times, `2→1` three times,
`5→4`, `4→3`, `23→22`). A constant offset is a membership decision, not a sampling one: one item is
systematically excluded.

Two candidate explanations were tested against the questions and **both are weak**:

- **Conjoined operands** ("led _or_ am currently leading", "pick up _or_ return") — 5 of the 15
  under-counts, and 3 of the 6 overs. Not the driver.
- **Time-window qualifiers** ("in the last month", "in April", "since I started") — common in the
  under-counts but present in the correctly answered ones too; the campaign has no measurement that
  separates them.

What the record does show, in the responses themselves, is the two failures the reference pipeline's
aggregation prompt names explicitly: an exchange counted once instead of twice (`0a995998` says _"the
same exchange/pickup event"_ and answers 1 against 3), and a decline taken on a question whose
operands are present (`a1cc6108` has Alex's age and declines the user's age at his birth).

### 13.102.4 What this retires

**Self-consistency is retired at three samples.** It is a variance reducer and the error is bias;
the census (75% disagreement, +1 question) is the measurement that says so, and it is the cleanest
negative result in the campaign because the mechanism provably ran.

It also retires the framing that produced it. For four rounds the assumption was that the reader's
mistakes were unstable and therefore averageable. They are stable and therefore not.

### 13.102.5 Adoption

None. `selfConsistency` stays `none`; `3` remains dispatchable so the refutation can be reproduced,
and the vote census stays in the artifact because it is what makes the refutation legible.

## 13.103 The aggregation shape, and the three rules this arm never stated

### 13.103.1 Why this is not a fifth prompt attempt

Four attempts have been measured — structure, membership, retrieval, voting — and all four added
instructions to a contract whose _shape_ this arm invented. The reference pipeline answers **102 of
121** on the same capability, with the same model, the same dataset and a **smaller** window, and its
multi-session prompt differs from this arm's in three decisions that are not wording:

| decision                  | this arm's `enumerated`                                            | the reference pipeline                                                                                                                                         | the record it explains                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| What an exchange is       | "do not merge two items into one"                                  | **an exchange is two items**                                                                                                                                   | `0a995998` merges a drop-off and a collection and answers 1 against 3; `bf659f65` does the same with purchase and download |
| How Step 2 decides        | "compute exactly as the question asks"                             | **four form→operation lines** (distinct → count; hours/days in total → sum durations; how much money → sum amounts; what time/which → that value, not a count) | `a4996e51` asked for hours in total declines; `73d42213` asked for a time declines                                         |
| When declining is allowed | a bare decline is forbidden, a non-empty list may still end in one | **only when the evidence says nothing**; deriving is not a reason                                                                                              | 7 of the 10 MR declines are questions whose operands the evidence states                                                   |

That is the whole change: the shape, not the tone. It is also the first candidate in this campaign
derived from a system that **demonstrably solves the capability**, rather than from a hypothesis about
why this one fails.

### 13.103.2 What it does not copy

The reference pipeline's `Answer:` output contract. This arm's parser reads the last line and its
numeric gate reads the last number; changing the output shape in the same run would move the parser
and the prompt together, and every prior measurement is comparable only because the shape held.

The reach is the multi-session route alone. All five other routes keep the shipped block **byte for
byte**, so this run has five controls rather than three.

### 13.103.3 Predictions, registered before the dispatch

Dispatch: `--set cortex_memory_ask=aggregation` on §10.3's configuration (so `selfConsistency` and
`queryExpansion` are both `none`), N = 500, four repetitions. The control is **`39509698041`** — the
same configuration without the ask — not the voting run.

| #     | prediction                                                              | falsified if      |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| **1** | mechanism: config reads `ask=aggregation`, `askRoutes=multi-session`    | either differs    |
| **2** | five controls reproduce `39509698041` to the character and to the turn  | any moves         |
| **3** | MR mean **≥ 91** (86.2 + 5, i.e. past the floor, measured against 85.2) | MR ≤ 87           |
| **4** | the under-counts fall from **15 to ≤ 10**                               | 11 or more remain |
| **5** | MR abstentions fall from 10 to **≤ 7**                                  | 8 or more         |
| **6** | MR `promptChars` unchanged at **46,186 ± 500**                          | outside           |

Prediction 3 is set at five questions because that is the floor §13.100.2 published; prediction 4 is
the mechanism check, because the contract's first and third rules are both about a missing item.

### 13.103.4 What a positive result would mean, and what it would not

It would mean the gap to the reference pipeline is a **shape** difference rather than a capability
difference — that the same model, on the same evidence, can be brought from 86 to the low 90s by
telling it what an exchange is and what each question form asks for. It would not mean parity: the
reference pipeline's 102 comes from its own retrieval, its own session truncation and its own critique
pass, none of which this run changes.

## 13.104 The aggregation run is void, and what it found anyway

### 13.104.1 The readings (`39641088296`, 1h45m)

| #     | prediction (§13.103.3)                                 | observed                                   | verdict                                    |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| **1** | `ask=aggregation`, `askRoutes=multi-session`           | both as registered                         | **holds** — and the registration was wrong |
| **2** | five controls reproduce `39509698041` to the character | **IE 46,864 → 46,980; TR 47,137 → 47,383** | **falsified**                              |
| **3** | MR mean ≥ 91                                           | **87.5** (82–91); first repetition **82**  | **falsified**                              |
| **4** | under-counts 15 → ≤ 10                                 | **14**                                     | **falsified**                              |
| **5** | MR abstentions 10 → ≤ 7                                | **16**                                     | **falsified**                              |
| **6** | MR `promptChars` 46,186 ± 500                          | **45,964**                                 | holds                                      |

Roster **380.5** (367–391) against 406.8; delta +31.30pp against +36.15. The capability table is the
reason this run cannot be used: **TR 94.2 → 72.8** and **IE 136.2 → 127.5**, on a run registered as a
single-variable test on multi-session.

### 13.104.2 Why the control broke, and it is one sentence

`aggregation`'s fallthrough returned `own` — the **control's** block — while `enumerated`'s returns
`withMergingSentence(own)` on the flat path and the temporal route. So the run administered a
treatment to MR and a **removal** to two routes nobody was measuring, and the control it was
registered against is an `enumerated` run whose blocks still carried that sentence.

The reach table said one route and the fallthrough said five; they are two statements of one fact and
they disagreed. §13.103.2 asserted "all five other routes keep the shipped block byte for byte" — a
sentence about the code that the code did not implement, which is §13.55's defect class arriving in a
document rather than in a parser.

Fixed in `prompt.ts` and in the arm's table: `aggregation` now reaches exactly the three routes
`enumerated` reaches and differs from it on one, which is what the registration always claimed. The
suite pins it — the flat path and temporal route must match `enumerated` **byte for byte**, and
`evidence-ask-reach.ts` asserts the two reach sets are equal.

### 13.104.3 What the broken control measured, which is worth more than the run

With the merging sentence removed, **TR fell 21.4 questions and IE 8.7**. That is the largest
single-sentence effect this campaign has measured, and it was found by accident: §13.21 adopted
`aggregate` on TR 27.27% → 44.63%, and this is the same sentence priced at the current window, pool and
cap. It also explains why every ask since §13.34 composed onto `computed` rather than replacing it.

Two defects were found by reading the artifact rather than by a test:

- **`vote=0/0/0` on a run that never voted.** The product always exposes `voteCounts()`, so a control
  run published a census of three zeros — claiming a mechanism that never ran, which is exactly the
  reading §13.101.2 says the census exists to prevent. `voteCountsOf` now treats a sum of zero as
  absent, and a test holds it.
- **A reach table that disagreed with its own fallthrough** (§13.104.2).

### 13.104.4 Verdict on `aggregation`: retired

Prediction 3 missed by 3.5 questions and prediction 5 missed in the wrong direction — abstentions went
**up** by six, not down by three. The run's control is void, so the honest statement is narrower than a
paired comparison: **on the questions the contract actually changed, it produced 87.5 and sixteen
declines**, against 85.2 and ten. Both numbers are worse than the floor can excuse.

The mechanism the contract was built on — an exchange is two items, four form→operation lines, a
narrower decline — did not survive contact. `ask` stays `enumerated` in §10.3; `aggregation` remains
dispatchable, and the next run of it must be read against a control whose flat and temporal blocks are
identical.

### 13.104.5 The instruction grew and the window shrank

MR's `promptChars` fell by 222 characters, because the contract is longer than `enumerated`'s and the
evidence room is what pays for it. Six additional declines against a window 222 characters smaller is
consistent, and it is a fact about any future contract: **a longer instruction buys declines**, because
the budget is charged to the evidence. That is now on the record for the next one.

## 13.105 The unit of retrieval, at the budget this arm actually runs

### 13.105.1 Why re-test a unit that lost

`relevanceUnits: session` and `session-fill` were refused by §13.32–13.34. Every condition that
produced that verdict has changed:

|                 | when the unit lost              | now                  |
| --------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| evidence budget | 24,000 characters               | **48,000**           |
| pool width      | 64                              | **256**              |
| role filter     | none (52% assistant characters) | **user only**        |
| cap             | none                            | **400 on MR and TR** |
| MR              | 51%                             | **86–87%**           |

A turn unit scatters a session across the window; a session unit completes it. At 24,000 characters
and a 64-wide pool a completed session displaced too much, and the verdict was correct for that
configuration. §13.79 raised the pool until the gold's median rank (114) sat inside it, and §13.82
doubled the room. The question "does completing the session help" was never asked at a budget where a
session fits.

The reference pipeline retrieves **sessions**, truncates each one, and answers 102 of 121.

### 13.105.2 The treatment, and why it needs no code

`relevanceUnits: session` is implemented and has been measured before; the dispatch is one flag. The
unit applies to the multi-session route only — `buildPrompt` carries no session boundary, so the flat,
temporal, knowledge-update, abstention and assistant routes cannot express a session selection and are
inert by construction.

### 13.105.3 Predictions, registered before the dispatch

> **RESULT: this dispatch ran, and the headline prediction was falsified.** The run is
> **`39699987781`** (2026-10-22), and its MR is **62.81%** against the registered floor of
> **≥ 91**. The unit of the budget is closed as a lever by §13.105.4's own
> criterion. All six predictions are judged in `MEASURE-MR-UNITS.md` §2, which also corrects the
> `86–87%` MR figure in §13.105.1 above: **no `cortex-memory` run has ever read that on MR**, the
> figure belongs to `reference-pipeline` in the same runs. The text below is kept as registered.

Dispatch: `--set cortex_memory_relevance_units=session` on §10.3's configuration. Control:
**`39509698041`** (`enumerated`, `turn`, 48,000, k=256, user roles, cap 400).

| #     | prediction                                                               | falsified if |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ |
| **1** | mechanism: config reads `relevanceUnits=session`                         | it does not  |
| **2** | the four untouched capabilities reproduce `39509698041` to the character | any moves    |
| **3** | MR mean **≥ 91**                                                         | MR ≤ 87      |
| **4** | MR abstentions **≤ 10**                                                  | 11 or more   |
| **5** | the under-counts fall from **15 to ≤ 10** (`--arithmetic`)               | 11 or more   |
| **6** | MR `promptChars` within **46,186 ± 1,000**                               | outside      |

Prediction 3 is the floor. Prediction 5 is the mechanism: a completed session is what supplies the
item a turn-scattered window leaves out, and a constant offset of one is what §13.102.3 measured.

### 13.105.4 What a null result would close

If a completed session at 48,000 characters and a 256-wide pool does not move MR, then the unit of
retrieval is not the lever at any configuration this arm can express, and the remaining difference from
the reference pipeline is either its per-session truncation (`maxSessionChars`) or the reader itself.
That would be worth knowing before another prompt is written.

## 13.106 The reach table is now a test rather than a claim

### 13.106.1 What §13.104 left behind

§13.104.2 found that `aggregation`'s reach table said one route while its fallthrough installed the
**control's** block on the other five. Both statements described the same fact and they disagreed, and
nothing in the suite compared them: every reach test in `evidence-ask-reach.test.ts` had been written
by hand for the ask its section introduced, so the file asserted eight asks and verified none of them
against the table that publishes their reach.

The cost was a void run — TR 94.2 → 72.8, IE 136.2 → 127.5 with no treatment — and, on the way, the
campaign's largest single-sentence measurement. That is a good accident, not a method.

### 13.106.2 The invariant, stated once

For **every** ask in `ASK_ROUTES` and **every** route this product can build a prompt for, the
instruction block the route receives must differ from the shipped block on exactly the routes the table
names. Eight asks × six routes, one assertion, no per-ask prose.

Three properties make it a real check rather than a restatement:

- **It drives the routes.** The block is read out of the prompt the model would receive, not out of
  the source. A table and a fallthrough can agree in text and disagree in code — that is precisely
  what §13.104 was.
- **It compares against the shipped ask.** `askRoutes` in an artifact means "routes this dispatch
  changes, relative to no ask". Any comparison between two asks answers a different question and would
  have passed on the run that broke.
- **It checks the names.** A route name in the table that no scope produces is invisible otherwise:
  the artifact would publish a reach for a route nothing can move, and the claim would be untestable
  rather than wrong.

**Mutation check.** Reverting `aggregation`'s fallthrough to `own` — the exact line that produced the
void run — turns three tests red: the two per-route byte-identity tests §13.104 added, and the new
generic one. Restoring it returns all 64 to green.

## 13.107 The census counted consultations, and every count in the artifact is about questions

### 13.107.1 The defect, found while auditing an artifact rather than a run

`--audit` (§13.107.4) was written to check an artifact's fields against each other, and the first field
it disagreed with was the census. On `39529234665` — the voting run — `abstentionReasons` sums to
**2,968** against the **2,000** its roster implies (`500 questions × 4 repetitions`).

The surplus is exactly accounted for: **968 = 484 × 2**, the two additional samples of each of the 484
multi-session question-answers. The census was tallied inside `#consult`, the per-**call** method, so
`selfConsistency: 3` turned one question into three outcomes. `reviewPass: 'audit'` did the same thing
with one surplus call, so `39416366870`'s census was inflated by 484 as well.

### 13.107.2 Why this is a measurement defect and not a cosmetic one

Every count in this artifact is about **questions**: `questionCount x runs` declares how many answers a
run produces, the per-capability tables divide by it, and `abstentionRate` is read against it. A field
whose denominator silently changes with the treatment makes an abstention rate incomparable with any
control run's — and nothing in the artifact said the denominator had moved.

The scoping matters: **no published claim in this document used the inflated figure.** Abstentions were
always read from the roster (`answer === null`), which is per question by construction, and §13.102.1's
"10 abstentions" and §13.104.1's "16" are roster counts. What was wrong is the field, and a field is
what a later reader consults.

### 13.107.3 The fix, and why the tally moved to the route

`#consult` now only asks and parses. `#recordOutcome(answer)` counts one question's outcome and
**returns its argument**, so every call site reads `return this.#recordOutcome(await ...)` and cannot
record one answer while returning another. Four call sites: the two single-consultation routes, the
vote's majority, and the audit pass's final answer.

That last one is the property the audit pass needed and did not have: it discards the first pass, so
the first pass must not be counted. Four tests hold it, and three of them failed before the fix
(`expected 3 to be 1`, `expected 2 to be 1`, `expected 1 to be +0`, `expected 6 to be 2`).

### 13.107.4 `--audit`: seven checks, and the two that were refused

`tools/readout-arm-run.py --audit <report.json>` prints PASS/FAIL per check and exits 1 on any failure:

| check         | invariant                                                                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `roster`      | the roster is as long as `questionCount` says                                        |
| `census-unit` | `abstentionReasons` sums to `questionCount × runs`                                   |
| `budget`      | no prompt exceeds the `maxPromptChars` it declares                                   |
| `reach`       | `askRoutes ⊆ renderingRoutes`, and empty exactly when `ask` is the shipped ask       |
| `vote`        | the census exists exactly when the run voted, and sums to `MR × runs`                |
| `expansion`   | the counts exist exactly when the run expanded, and name every distinct MR question  |
| `roles`       | a route in `evidenceRolesRoutes` carries no assistant turn when the roles are `user` |

Two candidate checks were **refused**, and the refusals are the design:

- **`evidenceTurns` above `relevanceTopK`.** Thousands of windows "violate" it, and none is broken: the
  pool is counted in records and a record expands to its turns.
- **Turns longer than `maxTurnChars`.** 1,912 MR windows carry a turn longer than 400 characters, and
  none is broken: the cap is applied when the prompt is rendered (`contentFor`), while the roster keeps
  what was selected.

A check that fires on a legitimate run is worse than no check, because it teaches a reader to skip the
output. Both are named in the tool's docstring so the next person does not add them back.

**Read against the five archived runs, it reproduces both defects that were found by hand** —
`39529234665` fails `census-unit` (2,968 vs 2,000) and `39641088296` fails `vote` (`vote=0/0/0` on a
run that never voted) — and passes the three clean ones. The two failures are the tool working on
artifacts produced before the fixes.

### 13.107.5 The gate

The workflow runs the audit **after** the upload and with `if: always()`, so a red job never costs the
artifact: the artifact is published, the job's colour says its own fields contradict each other, and
the reading step has both. Four source-level assertions hold the wiring (`test_artifact_audit_gate.py`),
including that the audited path is one the upload glob can match — an audit of a file nobody downloads
is the §13.55 shape. Deleting the step turns three of them red.

### 13.107.6 What this changes about the campaign's method

The last three defects were each a disagreement **between two fields of one run**. None needed a
control, a provider, or a repetition: they needed someone to divide 2,968 by 484. From this round on
that division is a step in the pipeline, and a run that contradicts itself is red before anyone reads it.

| **2** | four untouched capabilities reproduce `39509698041` to the character | **identical** (46,694 / 46,864 / 46,827 / 47,137; 72 / 61 / 62 / 179) | **holds**                                 |
| **3** | MR mean **≥ 91**                                                     | **82.5** (76–87), first repetition **76**                             | **falsified**                             |

### 13.108.2 The unit barely moved the window, so it could not move the score

|                            | turns   | chars  | chars/turn |
| -------------------------- | ------- | ------ | ---------- |
| MR, `turn` units (control) | **174** | 46,186 | 265        |
| MR, `session` units        | **168** | 45,546 | 271        |

A completed session at 48,000 characters, a 256-wide pool and a user-only role filter changes the
multi-session window by **six turns and 640 characters** — 3.4% and 1.4%. §13.32–13.34 retired the session
unit at 24,000 characters and a 64-wide pool, where completing a session displaced too much; this run shows
what the budget increase actually bought: not a unit that now helps, but a unit that no longer has room to
do anything. The lever is inert at this configuration, which is a different fact from "the lever is wrong".

The movement it did produce is the §13.98 shape again: 29 of 121 MR states changed, **7 repaired and 18
damaged**, and MR's gold turns carried moved by 0 for most transitions.

### 13.108.3 The untreated route moved more than the treated one

TR changed **27 of 127** states (21.3%) — `correct → abstention` 6, `abstention → correct` 4,
`correct → long_prose` 4 — with a window **identical to the character**. That is −5.0 questions on a route
no treatment reached, against −2.7 on the route the treatment reached. §13.100.2 measured TR's same-config
net at −4; this is one question past it, and it is the third independent confirmation that the answer
layer moves by more than any effect this arm can produce.

### 13.108.4 What this closes

§13.105.4 pre-committed to the reading: _"if a completed session at 48,000 characters and a 256-wide pool
does not move MR, then the unit of retrieval is not the lever at any configuration this arm can express."_
It did not move MR; it moved it the wrong way by less than the untreated route moved. **The unit hypothesis
closes**, and with it every remaining "how the evidence is packed" candidate:

| layer                                                                | status                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| pool width, room, roles                                              | adopted, and they carried the arm                                    |
| unit (turn / session)                                                | **closed here**                                                      |
| prompt shape (structure, membership, retrieval queries, aggregation) | closed, four attempts                                                |
| sampling (self-consistency)                                          | closed, error is bias not variance                                   |
| **what remains**                                                     | per-session truncation (`maxSessionChars`) and **the reader itself** |

### 13.108.5 Adoption

None. `relevanceUnits` stays `turn` in §10.3. `session` remains dispatchable so this refutation can be
reproduced.

## 13.109 The next lever is the reader, and it needs a different instrument

Every layer this arm controls has now been measured and closed. The remaining 36 MR questions are not
addressed by anything the arm can dial, and §13.108.3 puts the instrument's own movement at 5–6 questions
per route — larger than any single knob's remaining headroom.

So the next experiment is not another flag. It is the **reader**: the same window, the same prompt, a
stronger model. The campaign has deliberately held the model fixed so that every reading since §13.31 is
comparable, and that decision has now bought everything it can. Changing it needs:

1. a **pinned model identity in the artifact** (`llm=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, date, temperature), so a
   reading can never be attributed to the wrong reader;
2. a **per-route re-baseline**: the four capabilities that reproduce to the character under a fixed model
   will not do so across models, so the comparison becomes "same questions, new reader, new control";
3. the **same floor discipline**: §13.100.2's net movement was measured on one model, and a new model's
   floor is unknown until it is measured — the first run of a new reader must therefore be a
   **control-against-itself**, not a treatment.

That third point is the one that is easy to skip and expensive to skip: without it, a new reader's first
treatment run is unreadable, and the campaign would spend a run to learn nothing.

---

## 13.110 A stronger model id is a weaker reader at this contract

§13.109 registered the reader axis and fixed three conditions before the run existed: a pinned model
identity in the artifact, a per-route re-baseline, and a floor for the new reader. The first run of the
axis is `40698883428`, one dispatch of the adopted configuration with exactly one value changed —
`DEEPSEEK_MODEL: deepseek-v4-pro`. Nothing else moved: the artifact's `memoryArmConfig` compares equal to
`40698867439`'s on every field, including `reviewPass: bare`, `maxPromptChars: 48000`,
`relevanceSignal: retrieval-hybrid`, `relevanceTopK: 256` and `evidenceRoles: user`.

| capability | `deepseek-chat` (`40698867439`) | `deepseek-v4-pro` (`40698883428`) | Δ                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| IE         | 141/150                         | 129/150                           | **−12** (−8.0 pp)  |
| MR         | 83/121                          | 80/121                            | −3 (−2.5 pp)       |
| KU         | 64/72                           | 56/72                             | **−8** (−11.1 pp)  |
| TR         | 100/127                         | 86/127                            | **−14** (−11.0 pp) |
| ABS        | 29/30                           | 30/30                             | +1 (+3.3 pp)       |
| **total**  | **417/500 (83.40%)**            | **381/500 (76.20%)**              | **−36 (−7.20 pp)** |

**The reading order §13.109 fixed, answered in that order.**

1. **Model identity in the artifact.** Present, but the artifact names it in the _environment_, not in
   `memoryArmConfig`: the report's `featureConfig`/`memoryArmConfig` block carries no reader field, and the
   model id is only recoverable from the job log's `DEEPSEEK_MODEL:` line. That is condition 1 not yet
   met — the identity exists but not where a reader of the artifact looks. Recorded as debt rather than
   argued away, because the next reader run would inherit the same blind spot.
2. **Per-route re-baseline.** Done above, and it is why the headline is readable: the movement is not
   uniform. `ABS` improves, `MR` barely moves, and the three capabilities that need the reader to hold a
   format lose 8 to 14 questions each.
3. **The floor.** Unmeasured for this reader — §13.109.3 warned exactly this would happen and the run was
   dispatched as a treatment anyway. What makes the conclusion survive it is the size: §13.100 measured
   this arm's own movement at 5–6 questions per route, and −36 across four of five capabilities with a
   consistent sign is six times that. A second run would turn `−7.20 ± unknown` into `−7.20 ± measured`,
   and it is not worth 500 questions to learn that the sign does not move.

**What the four pre-registered checks returned.** R1 (|Δ| ≥ 5 points) **met** at 7.20. R2 (逐题候选集相同)
**unverified**: the artifacts carry `featureRetrievedContexts` but no per-question retrieval index, so
"same candidates" cannot be asserted, only assumed from an identical config line. R3 (`ABS` moves by at
most one question) **met** at +1. R4 (any gain concentrated in MR and TR) **falsified twice over** — there
is no gain, and the largest movements are losses in TR and IE with MR the _least_ moved capability. The
registration assumed the axis could only help; the falsification is that reader strength and reader
compliance are different quantities and the second dominates here.

**What the artifact says about the mechanism.** Three facts, in decreasing order of how much they support:

- **Answer shape.** Median answer length is **60 characters against 19** on the control (p90 513 against
  715). The prompt's closing line for the enumerated ask is `Reply with the Step 2 number alone.` The chat
  reader obeys it; this reader does not, and the answer carries its own arithmetic.
- **Decline shape.** 53 declines, of which **7** were the bare token. The control has 51 declines, of
  which 23 were. So the difference between the two readers is not how often they decline — it is how they
  spell it. §13.111 takes this apart, because it changes what the retry _is_.
- **Failure content.** On the discordant questions read by hand, the failures are enumeration and
  arithmetic, not retrieval: a charity total answered `8,750` against a gold of `$3,750`; a rollercoaster
  count answered `7` against `10` after dropping one event from its own list; a kit count answered `6`
  after listing three items. The evidence reached the reader in each case.

**What this does not claim.** It does not claim `deepseek-chat` is the better model — it claims
`deepseek-chat` is the better reader _for this prompt contract_, which is a narrower and more useful
statement. It does not claim the reader axis is closed for other model families: a reader that obeys the
contract and reasons better is still the most plausible way past §13.108.3's 5–6-question floor, and this
run only says that model size is not a proxy for that property. And it does not claim the −7.20 is
reproducible to the tenth of a point: it is one run per side.

## 13.111 The retry's population is a property of the reader

§13.94 built the bare-decline retry on a shape: `isBareDecline` matches a reply that is the abstention
token and nothing else. That predicate was derived from a measurement of _one_ reader — "of 45 wrong
declines on the shipped arm 30 are that bare token" — and the five adopted readings (22/19/25/22/23) are
all that reader's.

`40698883428` is the first time the predicate met a different reader, and it sees **7 where the control
sees 23**, on the same 500 questions, the same routes, and a nearly identical decline count (53 against
51). Fourteen of the treatment's consultations simply do not exist for this reader, not because it
declines less but because it declines in prose:

| reader            | declines | bare-token declines | retry consultations |
| ----------------- | -------- | ------------------- | ------------------- |
| `deepseek-chat`   | 51       | 23 (45.1%)          | **23**              |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | 53       | 7 (13.2%)           | **7**               |

**The rule this hands the next increment.** A retry keyed on an exact token measures the reader's
formatting, not its uncertainty. Two consequences, both actionable and neither implemented:

1. **The population is not the phenomenon.** 22 of 51 declines on the shipped reader, and 46 of 53 on this
   one, are declines _with content_ — prose that says the evidence does not answer the question. Whether
   those are also recoverable is unmeasured, and it is the larger population on both readers.
2. **A predicate on content is portable; a predicate on shape is not.** "The reply asserts nothing about
   the question" is checkable against either reader; "the reply is exactly `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`" is a
   property of how one model was trained to close. §13.92's `recover` value already keys on structure (a
   non-empty Step 1 list), which is why it is the closer analogue — and it is registered-but-unrun.

This also retro-explains §6.0's open item in `cortex-docs`: MR moved +6.75 across the four treatment runs
while the pass cannot reach MR at all. The pass's reach is a property of the reader and the route, and an
effect on an unreached capability is sampling by construction, not a mechanism.

## 13.112 The registration and the script that reproduces it were two runs

The workflow's default for `cortex_memory_review_pass` moved to `bare` in the commit that adopted the
pass. §10.3 and `tools/dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py` did not move with it, and every guard in
`tools/__tests__/test_preregistration_config.py` stayed green — because each of them compares §10.3 against
the script, and both were consistently wrong.

The cost is measurable, and `40698867439` is the run that measures it. It was dispatched with **no**
`review_pass` input at all, so it landed on the workflow default, and it read **417/500 = 83.40%** with
`reviewPass: bare` in its own artifact. A dispatch through the script would have sent `none` explicitly
and read the control's 81.0%. Two procedures, both describable as "run the registered configuration",
differing by 2.45 points, and no field in either artifact able to say which one produced it.

**The repair is a guard, not a number.** Three values moved (`bare` in §10.3, `bare` in the script, and
the §13.94 bullet's own wording); the thing that prevents the recurrence is
`TestTheShippedDefaultAgreesWithTheRegistration`, which asserts the direction neither existing guard could
see: a `workflow_dispatch` default is the only place in the repository that expresses **what a run gets
when nobody chooses**, so it cannot disagree with the registration. `limit` and `ablation_runs` are
exempted by name with their reason — they are the cheap button-run budgets and they answer a different
question than §10.3 answers. Verified against the defect rather than assumed: with the workflow default
set back to `none` the guard fails and names both values.

**Generalised, this is the fifth form of the §7.3 side channel**, and it completes the table §4 of that
test file started:

| form | wrong where                                                    | caught by                        |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 1    | input not declared in the workflow                             | `test_dispatch_inputs.py`        |
| 2    | declared but not forwarded into `env`                          | `test_dispatch_inputs.py`        |
| 3    | forwarded but never read by the arm                            | `bench-memory-arm.test.ts`       |
| 4    | read correctly, dispatch never sends the registered value      | `test_preregistration_config.py` |
| 5    | **the workflow's own default disagrees with the registration** | **the new class in that file**   |

## 13.113 Every question sits at the budget, and 48,000 was never measured as a ceiling

§13.82 raised the evidence budget from 24,000 to 48,000 characters and adopted it, on a run where MR's
delivered gold rose 72.9% → 86.9% and the roster rose 394 → 403. §13.81 registered it as the one lever
that buys room without truncating a turn, and the option's own documentation says the quiet part out loud:
"only the second has no measured floor".

The artifact of `40698867439` says how binding that lever is, and the answer is _completely_:

| statistic over 500 questions                      | value          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `featurePromptEvidenceChars` median               | **46,851.5**   |
| p90                                               | 47,311         |
| questions whose room is within one turn of 48,000 | **500 of 500** |

Not one question leaves room on the table. The prefix-fit allocator fills every prompt to within the next
turn's width, which means the budget — not the retriever's reach, not the pool's width, not the route
composition — is the constraint that decides what the reader sees, on every single question this arm
answers. Two earlier measurements bound the direction:

- **Downward is refuted twice.** At 24,000 the room held 68 turns on MR and 74 on TR against 144 and 151
  at 48,000 (§13.82), and buying room by truncating instead of by budget — a 200-character cap — reached
  100 turns and lost MR to 29 of 121 (§13.80).
- **Upward is unmeasured.** §13.82 is the last word on 48,000, and it was chosen by a run that compared
  it against 24,000, not by a run that found it better than 96,000.

**Registered: `cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars=96000`**, dispatched as `40722772896` on the commit
carrying §13.112's repair, everything else at §10.3. One variable. The mechanism under test is
**coverage against dilution**, and the literature makes it a live fork rather than a formality: RAW-RAG's
ablation (`arXiv:2610.30755`) reports that retrieval depth is stable from k = 5 to k = 60 and **loses
14.57 points at k = 120**, which is the only published measurement of what happens when a fixed reader is
given more evidence than it can use.

Predictions, each with a number:

1. **MR gains ≥ 3 questions.** MR has the widest gold sets (a median gold session of 24 per §13.26), so
   extra room is worth most there, and 96,000 holds roughly 240 turns of 400 characters against 144.
2. **IE loses no more than 2 questions.** Dilution, if it exists, shows first on questions that need one
   turn: a room twice as large holds twice as many places for the wrong turn to be.
3. **`goldOverlap` rises on MR and TR.** The claim is not "the reader does better" but the narrower "the
   right turn is in the window more often", and that is what this field measures.

Stopping rule: one dispatch, read in the order above. If MR ≤ 0 and IE < −2, the budget has a ceiling at
48,000, §13.82 is the last word, and no further sweep is run — the arm's remaining headroom is then
precision (which turn), not volume (how many), and that is the rerank increment's question rather than
this one's.

## 13.114 The arm has never sent a temperature, and every artifact said it had

The workflow declares a `temperature` input with a default of `'0'` and a description that reads
"Sampling temperature (0 = deterministic)". The dispatch script sends it. `§10.3` registers it. Every
document that describes a reading says the runs were taken at temperature 0.

Nothing on this arm's path reads it.

```
benchmark-cortex-memory.yml   TEMPERATURE: ${{ github.event.inputs.temperature || '0' }}   # forwarded
cortex-eval/src/llm-factory.ts   createLlmFromEnv(env)   -- reads DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, _BASE_URL, _MODEL, _THINKING
cortex-memory/src/memory.ts      #consult -> this.#llm.complete(prompt)   -- no options
cortex-ai/src/llm/openai-compatible.ts   if (opts.temperature != null) body['temperature'] = ...
```

`TEMPERATURE` is read in exactly one place in the repository — `cortex-eval/bench/run.ts`, the
**reference pipeline's** runner. So on `benchmark-cortex-memory.yml` the variable is declared,
forwarded, and never consulted, which is the third form of the §7.3 side channel with a twist: the
value never becomes an option, so `bench-memory-arm.test.ts` (which guards "option set but unread")
cannot see it either.

**What it costs.** Every reading this campaign has taken was served at the provider's default
temperature — `1.0` for DeepSeek — not at 0. Two consequences, one benign and one not:

1. **The noise floor is sampling, and now it is named.** §13.100 measured the arm's own movement at
   5–6 questions per route and §13.108.3 built its argument on that number. It is consistent with
   `T = 1.0` on 500 questions, and the previous attribution ("the instrument's own movement") was
   right about the size and silent about the cause. Nothing in the campaign's arithmetic changes.
2. **Every claim of determinism for this arm is false as written.** Not the feature aggregate —
   that number is one system's own accuracy and a temperature cannot make it a lie — but any
   sentence that says a run is reproducible to the question. Two dispatches of one configuration
   are two samples at `T = 1.0`, and §13.91's `44.20%` twice in a row was the reference pipeline,
   which does read the variable.
   **This paragraph originally continued "both sides share the reader and the temperature, so the
   paired comparison is unaffected", and that half is wrong — §13.120.**

**Why it is not fixed in this commit.** Because fixing it moves every number. A reader pinned to
`T = 0` is a different reader in the sense that matters here: the distribution narrows, the mean can
move either way, and every threshold in `ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md` was calibrated against samples. A
change of that size gets its own dispatch, its own control, and its own section — not a line in a
documentation round. So this section records the defect and the artifact records the fact:

`MemoryArmConfig.reader` is new, and `reader.temperature` is `number | null`, populated by
`resolveReaderIdentity(env)` — the same function `createLlmFromEnv` calls, so the reader that
answers and the reader the artifact names cannot be two readings of one environment. `null` means
"the request carried no temperature", which is the state of every run before this field existed, and
it renders as `temp=default` rather than being omitted, for the reason `reviewPass` renders `none`:
a fact and a missing field must not be the same bytes.

**What the run to fix it has to show.** Registered, not dispatched:

- **Prediction 1.** Pinning `T = 0` shrinks the per-route movement below the 5–6 questions §13.100
  measured. That is the observable the field exists for, and it is checkable before any threshold
  moves.
- **Prediction 2.** The mean moves by less than the movement it removes. If it moves more, the arm's
  configuration is tuned to a sampling artefact rather than to a mechanism, which would be a far
  more uncomfortable finding than a wrong temperature.
- **Kill clause.** If `T = 0` and `T = default` produce the same 500 answers, the temperature was
  never doing anything and the input should be deleted rather than fixed — a declared input that
  changes nothing is worse than an absent one, because it costs a reader's attention every time it
  appears in a config line.

Until that run exists, every sentence in `cortex-docs` that says "temperature 0" is corrected to say
what the artifact now says: **no temperature was sent**.

### 13.115 The reranking stage: the one RAW-RAG part this arm does not have

§13.110 priced the reader and the price was negative; §13.113 measured the budget and every question
sits against it. Both closed a road. This section registers the increment those two leave standing, and
it is the only mechanism in `SOTA-LANDSCAPE.md` §4.9 that this arm has never had **at all**.

**The mechanism, in one causal sentence.** Retrieval here is bi-encoder: the question and each turn are
embedded independently and compared by cosine, then the recall channels are fused by reciprocal rank.
Neither representation can see the other, so "this turn answers _this_ question" is expressed as a
distance between two independently chosen vectors. A cross-encoder scores the `(question, turn)` pair
**jointly** — the interaction is the model's input rather than a by-product of two encodings — and it is
the standard last stage of a retrieval pipeline for exactly that reason. RAW-RAG runs it over the whole
retrieved pool and reads a prefix of the result; this arm reads a prefix of the _fusion_.

**Why it is not an optional refinement.** RAW-RAG's own ablation is single-variable on 20,000 bootstrap
samples with Holm correction, and removing the reranker costs them **−3.92** (48.32 → 44.40) — more than
any mechanism they _added_ (atomic facts −19.62 and summaries −5.81 are additions that hurt; the graph
−5.78 the same). §4.6's reading was "adding mechanism is the hypothesis, not the default"; this is the
one case where the mechanism is **already in the strongest published pipeline** and simply absent here.

**The instrument, and the state it has to make visible.** `memoryArmConfig.rerank` carries the identity
(`provider`, `model`, `host`), the declared wire limits, and a census:

| counter     | what it answers                                         | why it is not optional                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `calls`     | scoring invocations (one per question on this arm)      | pairs with `fallbacks`; `calls = 0` is a stage that never ran        |
| `pairs`     | `(question, passage)` pairs scored                      | the cost, and the only number that says how much text was judged     |
| `fallbacks` | invocations whose reply could not be trusted            | **`> 0` is an assembly failure**, not a null result                  |
| `changed`   | questions whose order moved                             | `0` with `fallbacks: 0` is a reranker that ran and agreed — a result |
| `clipped`   | passages shortened to the endpoint's per-document limit | says how often the ordering judged a prefix                          |

`cortex-core`'s `rerankHits` degrades to the retrieved order on a thrown request, a short reply or a
non-finite score — the right behaviour for the ranking and the wrong one for the measurement. Without
these counters, an arm whose endpoint answered `401` five hundred times produces **the same accuracy**
as one whose cross-encoder agreed with the retriever every time. The report prints that sentence beside
the counters rather than leaving a reader to work it out from a `0.00pp` delta. This is §13.107's
`reviewPass` lesson applied before the run instead of after it.

**Two endpoint facts that became part of the design, not of the deployment.** The Runner's rerank
provider is Zhipu, whose `/rerank` is the OpenAI-compatible shape `cortex-ai` already speaks — and its
published limits are **128 documents** per call and **4,096 characters** per document, with the whole
call refused above either bound. Two consequences:

1. **The pool must fit one call**, so the reranking experiment is registered as a **pair of runs at
   `relevanceTopK` 128**: with the stage on, and with it off. That is one variable plus one
   re-registration of the pool width — the control for the treatment is the same width, so the only
   thing that moves between them is the stage. 128 is also RAW-RAG's own `K`, which makes the eventual
   same-reader comparison closer than it would be at 256.
   Batching a wider pool was **refused rather than implemented**: `relevance_score` is normalised per
   call, so a batch-local winner can outrank a true winner from another batch while every number still
   looks plausible. The index therefore rejects a pool wider than the declared limit at construction,
   before a single retrieval, rather than discovering it as `fallbacks: 500` after forty minutes.
2. **Long turns are clipped at the boundary.** This corpus carries turns up to 15,369 characters
   (§13.67: median 272, p90 2,305), and one over-length document rejects the whole call — not itself.
   Clipping keeps a technicality out of `fallbacks`, and `clipped` says how often the ordering judged a
   prefix. The **reader still sees whole turns**: this is the ranking's input, not the prompt's.

**Set and control.** LongMemEval-500, paired within one invocation, same reader (`deepseek-chat`), same
judge, same embedding cache. Control = the same run at `relevanceTopK 128` with `rerank: none`. Nothing
else moves: `retrieval-hybrid`, `evidenceRoles: user`, `maxPromptChars: 48000`, `reviewPass: bare`.

**Criterion, written before the number exists.**

- **Met** if MR ≥ **+3 questions** and no capability falls by more than **2**, with `fallbacks = 0`.
- **Assembly failure, not a result**, if `fallbacks > 0`: the run cannot be read at all until the
  endpoint answers every one of the 500 questions. §13.110's precedent — a condition stated before the
  run, checked after it, and reported as debt rather than argued away.
- **No room, delete it**, if `fallbacks = 0` and `changed = 0`: the cross-encoder agreed with the retriever
  on all 500 questions. That is a real outcome and it means the reranking question is settled negatively
  for this corpus, not that the stage is broken.
- **Delete the stage** if `fallbacks = 0`, `changed > 0` and MR moves ≤ 0. §4.6's rule applies in the
  direction that costs us: a mechanism that the strongest competitor needs and we do not is either a
  difference in the corpus or a difference in what it is reranking, and both are findings.

**Three predictions**, so the run can be wrong in a specific way:

1. `changed` is **substantial** — at least 60% of questions reordered. A large pool of turns that a
   bi-encoder could not separate is exactly where a joint scorer moves the order; a small `changed`
   would say the fusion ranking already agrees with the cross-encoder, which contradicts §13.64's
   finding that the fusion's reach did not improve.
2. The movement is **concentrated in MR and TR**, and `ABS` stays 30/30 — the same shape §13.110 saw for
   the reader, but in the opposite direction.
3. `fallbacks = 0` and `clipped` non-zero: at least one question in five hundred carries a turn over
   4,096 characters, given p90 = 2,305.

**Cost.** One HTTP call per question (500), 128 documents each, about 4.4k input tokens per call on this
corpus's median turn (~2.2M tokens for the run), and a serialized build phase in front of the ablation —
so the run is longer than a control run by the time the endpoint takes, not by the ablation's own work.
No new secret: `RERANK_API_KEY` is the Zhipu key the Runner already holds.

**What this section does not claim.** It does not claim the 4.08pp to RAW-RAG is the reranker. It claims
that the reranker is the one component of their published pipeline this arm lacks, that their own
ablation prices it highest, and that 4.08 points is the budget for finding out whether that transfers.
If this increment lands and the gap does not close, the remaining explanations are their reader, their
window unit (256/32 token windows against our 272-character turns), and their `k = 15` — each of which
is a measurable question rather than an inference.

**A plumbing fact this registration created, recorded because it will bind the next one.** The arm's
dispatch surface was at **24 of GitHub's 25 inputs** and this registration needed a slot. Rather than
sit at the ceiling — which `test_dispatch_inputs.py` refuses, because the next registration then could
not be dispatched at all — the per-pass wall-clock ceiling (§13.30's `budgetMinutes: 90`) moved out of
the dispatch surface and into the workflow's job environment. It is a hang detector rather than a
treatment, its value is unchanged, and the precedent is `evidenceTurnsPerRecord` (§13.94), moved for the
same reason one registration earlier. The surface is back at 24, with the margin the guard asks for.

### 13.116 The abstention line: what _kind_ of change a flip is

**The instrument this registers, and the one it refuses to register.** The plan for this step said "build a
per-question ledger: `bought`, `sold`, `kept`". Halfway through, the ledger turned out to exist. `runAblation`
already publishes the two flip **counts**, the **ids** of every flipped question (`discordantQuestions`), a
**per-capability** table with its own McNemar p-value, and Wilson intervals on both sides — and
`formatAblationReport` already renders all of it. A `ledger.ts` computing `{bought, sold, kept}` would have
been a second definition of numbers that already had one, which is the defect this register spends its length
removing. So the module was not built.

What was missing is one bit per flip that no existing field carries: **which side of the abstention line the
question was on.** `correct` is a boolean, `answers` is `string | null`, and the report reads only `correct`.
So "this question went from declining to answering" and "this question went from answering wrongly to
answering rightly" arrive downstream as the same event — a bought question — and a net of **+3** built from
four recovered and one lost belongs to a completely different mechanism than a +3 built from four corrected and
one broken. §13.110 priced the reader, §13.113 measured the window, §13.115 registers the reranker: all three
are increments whose _shape_ of gain is the finding, and the artifact could not express the shape.

**The mechanism, in one table.** A decline is `answer === null`, which is the predicate `metrics.ts` already
uses when it counts abstentions — there is deliberately no second definition of the word, because a private
predicate could disagree with the scorer about the same answer and neither would fail.

|                       | treatment answered     | treatment declined |
| --------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------ |
| **baseline answered** | `corrected` / `missed` | `declined`         |
| **baseline declined** | `recovered`            | — (concordant)     |

`recovered` + `declined` is the **decline flow** — questions that crossed the line in either direction, which
is a change in _whether_ the system speaks. `corrected` + `missed` is the **content flow** — questions that
stayed on the answering side and changed verdict, which is a change in _what_ it says. Concordant questions
(right in both, wrong in both) are not counted at all: they carry no information about a change, which is the
same reason McNemar conditions on the discordant pairs.

**The identity that keeps it a refinement.** `recovered + corrected` must equal the bought count and
`declined + missed` must equal the sold count. `answer-transition.test.ts` asserts both against a real
`runAblation` rather than against a fixture, so the split cannot drift into a rival count: if a future edit
double-counts a flip, the build fails naming the disagreement rather than publishing two numbers that differ
by one. Both sums are also printed in the report beside the table, so a reader checks the refinement without
opening the JSON.

**The reading rule, computed and not written.** The report prints one sentence under the four cells, and the
sentence comes from `dominantFlow` rather than from the author of the run:

- `decline` — every flipped question crossed the line: the increment changed **whether** the system speaks.
- `content` — no flipped question crossed it: the increment changed **what** it says.
- `both` — both happened, so the net is the **sum of a response-shape effect and a knowledge effect** and must
  not be reported as either one alone.
- `none` — no question changed verdict. A null result, printed as a sentence rather than as four zeroes.

**What it binds, before those runs happen.** §13.115's second prediction is "the movement is concentrated in
MR and TR, and `ABS` stays 30/30". `ABS` moving is now a statement about `recovered` and `declined` on thirty
questions, which is exactly the quantity this split reports and exactly the quantity a per-capability accuracy
column cannot distinguish from a content change. The same holds for §13.113's budget: a 96,000-character
window is a prompt change, so a gain it buys should be overwhelmingly `recovered` — turns that used to be cut
now fit, the reader stops declining, and if it instead shows up as `corrected` then the window bought
_evidence_, not _room_. Those are different findings about the same +3 and the run is dispatched once.

**Cost: nothing.** The two answer vectors and the two verdict vectors are already in hand on the two
`ScoredEvaluation`s `runAblation` owns; no extra API call, no extra pass, no change to any dispatch input.

**What this section does not claim.** It does not say **why** a decline appeared or vanished. An over-length
prompt, a stricter parse, a different system prompt and a genuine refusal all arrive as `null`, and `rawOutput`
— captured on the feature side only — is the field that separates them. This registers the question "did the
decline line move", which is what decides whether the raw output is worth reading at all; it does not answer
"what ended the decline", which is a per-question question and needs the text.

**An artifact written before this field existed** renders one sentence saying the split was not recorded, not
four zeroes. Four zeroes would be a measurement — "nothing crossed either line" — and a missing field that
renders as a null result is how a null result gets claimed by accident.

### 13.117 A missing re-export, and the gate that was bypassed by the transport

**What broke.** `toRerankRecord` was written in `bench-memory-arm.ts`, called by the arm's bench and by its
own test, and never added to the package entry (`index.ts`). `pnpm build` passed — each package's build
compiles `src`, and `bench/` is excluded from it by design, because the bench is not part of the published
artifact. CI went red on the first push: `pnpm typecheck` runs `pnpm -r typecheck`, and the memory package's
`typecheck` script compiles **both** `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.bench.json`. `TS2305: has no exported
member 'toRerankRecord'`.

**Why the local gate said green, which is the part worth recording.** Every push from this sandbox goes
through the Git Data API, because the proxy admits `api.github.com` and not the git transport. So `git push`
never runs — and husky's `pre-push` hook, the thing built to catch exactly this, never runs either. The hook
was not skipped with a flag; it was **bypassed by the transport**. What I ran before pushing was
`pnpm -r build` plus the two packages' test suites and the census — a subset of `pnpm check` that happens to
omit the one command that compiles `bench/`.

**The rule this leaves.** Before an API push, the command is **`pnpm check`**, not a subset chosen by
judgement about what the change touched. A subset is a hypothesis about blast radius, and this change's blast
radius was a file the change did not touch: an export list. The cost of the full gate is about four minutes;
the cost of the red run was a round trip plus this section.

**Why no other instrument caught it, and why none is added.** `tools/export-census.mjs` asks "does this export
have a caller", and `toRerankRecord` has one — the bench. It does not ask "is this symbol reachable from the
package entry", which is the property that broke; and the instrument that does ask it is the typechecker.
Adding a second test that parses the bench's import statements and checks them against the built entry would
be a re-implementation of `tsc` for one file pattern, so it is not added: `pnpm typecheck` already covers it,
which is precisely why CI caught it and the local subset did not.

**A second finding the full gate produced, in the same run.** The census baseline was **stale by one**: it
still listed `cortex-core: rerankHits` as an orphan, and `relevance-index.ts` had been calling it since the
previous round. `export-census.mjs --check` did not notice, and that is not a defect in it — its contract is
"fail on an orphan **absent** from the baseline", so the ledger can rot in the leaving direction forever. The
`cortex-core` test that asserts the report matches the baseline **exactly** is what noticed, which means the
stricter gate already existed and was on the other side of the same omission: the run that would have executed
it is the run I had not been running. Baseline rebuilt with `tools/rebuild-export-census-baseline.py`; the diff
over `knownOrphans` is one removal and no additions, verified as a set difference rather than by reading the
patch, because the file's own totals and line numbers churn on every rebuild.

**Relation to §13.47.** That section records the same shape one layer up: a module that reads its own
