configuration at import time, found by the first test that imported it. Both are "the symbol exists, the
suite is green, and the boundary between two surfaces was never exercised". The boundary here is the package
entry; there, it was the import.

## 13.118 Doubling the room buys coverage and sells dilution, at almost exactly the same price

§13.113 registered `max_prompt_chars=96000` against the 48,000 §13.82 adopted, on one variable, with three
numbered predictions and a stopping rule. `40722772896` finished `success` in **2h08m04s** with four
repetitions. Read against `40698867439` — the adopted configuration, same commit series, `reviewPass: bare`,
`relevanceSignal: retrieval-hybrid`, `relevanceTopK: 256`, one value different — the answer is not the one
either branch of the registration expected.

### 13.118.1 The readings

| statistic                                          | 48,000 (`40698867439`)            | 96,000 (`40722772896`)                   |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| repetitions in the artifact (`runs`)               | **1**                             | **4**                                    |
| feature aggregate, mean                            | 83.40%                            | **82.95%**                               |
| feature aggregate, min / median / max              | 83.40 (one sample)                | **81.40 / 82.90 / 84.60**                |
| first repetition, total                            | 417                               | 418                                      |
| first repetition, per capability                   | 141/83/64/100/29                  | 141/81/64/102/30                         |
| per-capability mean over repetitions               | n/a (single sample)               | 137.3/84.3/62.0/101.5/29.8               |
| per-capability min–max over repetitions            | n/a                               | 133–141 / 81–88 / 60–64 / 99–105 / 29–30 |
| `featurePromptEvidenceChars` median                | 46,851.5                          | **92,078.5**                             |
| window turns, MR / TR / IE / KU / ABS (median)     | 174 / 179 / 61 / 62 / 72          | **243 / 242 / 117.5 / 125.5 / 133**      |
| evidence carried as a share of the budget, MR / TR | 96.2% / 98.2%                     | **69.9% / 69.3%**                        |
| questions at complete gold coverage                | 256 of 500                        | **371 of 500**                           |
| mean coverage, MR / TR / IE / KU / ABS             | 96.6 / 95.4 / 84.3 / 77.9 / 66.9% | **100.0 / 100.0 / 90.8 / 89.6 / 81.1%**  |
| declines                                           | 51 (10.2%)                        | 46.75 per run (9.6%)                     |
| wall clock                                         | 44m37s                            | 2h08m04s                                 |

The room doubled and the score did not move. Everything below is about which of those two facts is the finding.

### 13.118.2 Two predictions falsified, one holds, and the third was unfalsifiable as written

| #   | prediction (§13.113)                  | observed                                                                               | verdict                                   |
| --- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| 1   | MR gains **≥ 3 questions**            | **+1.3** on the registered statistic (84.3 against 83); **−2** on the first repetition | **falsified**                             |
| 2   | IE loses **no more than 2 questions** | **−3.7** (137.3 against 141); 0 on the first repetition                                | **falsified**                             |
| 3   | `goldOverlap` rises on MR and TR      | MR **96.6% → 100.0%**, TR **95.4% → 100.0%**                                           | **holds, and was already at the ceiling** |

Prediction 3 needs its own paragraph, because holding it is the more awkward outcome. The 48,000 artifact's
**median** coverage on MR and TR was already **100.0%** for correct answers _and_ for wrong ones. A prediction
phrased as "the median rises" cannot rise from 100%, and it did not — the only place the rise is visible is the
distribution: complete-coverage questions went **256 → 371**, and MR and TR each went to **every question at
complete coverage** (85 → 121 and 89 → 127). So the registration named a statistic at its ceiling. The
prediction is recorded as holding on the distribution and as **unmeasurable on the statistic it named**, which
is a defect in the registration and not a result.

### 13.118.3 The mechanism resolves into two opposite numbers

§13.113 said the mechanism under test was "**coverage against dilution**". The artifact answers it directly,
because `goldOverlap` is a **pre-treatment** field carried by both runs: partition the 500 questions by their
coverage state _in the control_, and the two forces separate with no appeal to any outcome variable.

| group                                                | n   | 48k correct | 96k correct | Δ      | bought / sold | exact McNemar p |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --- | ----------- | ----------- | ------ | ------------- | --------------- |
| complete coverage at **both** budgets (dilution arm) | 256 | 219         | 211         | **−8** | 10 / 18       | 0.185           |
| coverage not complete at 48,000 (coverage arm)       | 244 | 198         | 207         | **+9** | 18 / 9        | 0.122           |
| **total**                                            | 500 | 417         | 418         | **+1** | 28 / 27       | —               |

**The increment is a wash because it is two increments.** Where the gold was already complete, ~70 more turns of
context cost **eight questions**. Where the gold was incomplete, the extra room bought **nine**. Those are the
two numbers §13.113 predicted as one, and together they are +1 — the aggregate this run actually reported.

Inside the clean 256, the loss is where §13.83 said the room's contents are worst: MR **65 → 59 (−6)** on 85
questions, TR **77 → 75 (−2)** on 89, and IE, KU and ABS **exactly unchanged** (0/0/0 on 75/5/2). So the
dilution is not spread across the roster; it is MR, which is the capability whose window is 51.9% assistant
prose.

**What this does not license.** Neither arm is significant on its own (p = 0.185, 0.122). The partition
_locates_ the cancellation; it does not certify either component, and the honest sentence is "the two forces are
of the same size and opposite sign, and 500 questions cannot separate them". The reason the partition is still
worth printing is that it is not a post-hoc outcome slice: the grouping variable is the control's own coverage,
measured before the treatment existed, and it was the variable §13.113 named in advance.

The abstention line agrees. Pairing the two dispatches question by question
(`answer === null` on both sides, the predicate §13.116 registers): `recovered` 4, `corrected` 24, `declined` 7,
`missed` 20 — a **content flow**, so §13.116's rule reads it as "the window bought **evidence**, not **room**".
Four questions that used to decline stopped declining. Twenty-four answers changed. That is not a
response-shape effect and it is not the effect §13.113 predicted, which was a room effect.

### 13.118.4 On the two decisive routes the budget stopped binding, and something else had been binding all along

This is the discovery that outranks the verdict. `--window` on the 96,000 artifact:

```
capability    n   turns    chars  chars/turn   budget
MR          121   243.0    67133         275   69.9%
TR          127   242.0    66566         277   69.3%
IE          150   117.5    94814         806   98.8%
KU           72   125.5    94806         759   98.8%
ABS          30   133.0    94794         709   98.7%
```

On IE, KU and ABS the character budget binds at ~98.8%, as it did at 48,000 (97.3–98.2%). On **MR and TR it
does not**: 243 turns spending **69.9%** of a 96,000-character room. A doubling of the budget that lands at 70%
of it did not buy 240 turns of room — it bought **the whole pool**. `relevanceTopK` is 256, and MR and TR
exhaust it (265–277 characters per turn × 256 = 68–71k characters) before the room runs out.

The artifact says so twice. `evidenceReduction` reports `maxTurnsPerRecord: 256` — equal to the pool width —
with `reducedQuestionIds` on **41 questions** and `droppedTurns: 491`: the per-record bound, not the budget,
is what stops those windows. And §13.82.6 had already priced this route: raising MR to ~250 turns would deliver
94.68% of its gold for "about three questions". It delivered **+1.3**.

So the honest statement of what this run measured is narrower than what it registered: **on MR and TR it
replaced "the budget cut the window" with "the pool cut the window"**, and the answer to "would 240 turns of
_retrieved_ evidence help" is still unmeasured — it would need `relevanceTopK` raised with the budget held, and
that is a different dispatch. On IE, KU and ABS the budget did bind, and those three bought +0, +0 and +0.

### 13.118.5 The measurement that makes a ±3-question prediction untestable

Four repetitions of **one** configuration, in one job, on one dataset, produced totals of **407, 414.5, 414.5 and
423** (min / median / max from the artifact) and MR counts spanning **81 to 88**. That is a **16-question spread
on the roster and 7 on MR**, at `temperature` unset — which §13.114 established means the provider's default,
`1.0`, not the 0 every document claimed.

§13.113 predicted **+3**. The arm's own dispersion is **more than twice the effect size**, and the control it was
compared against is a **single sample** whose dispersion was never measured. No reading of this run can resolve
+3, and the fact that it landed on +1.3 is arithmetic, not evidence.

**The workflow says the repetitions are free and identical, and the artifact disproves both halves.** The comment
at `benchmark-cortex-memory.yml` reads:

> `RUNS` is deliberately NOT forwarded. The arm reads `ABLATION_RUNS` … every ablation shares one answer cache
> across its two arms, so a second run replays the first run's cached answers and costs full wall-clock for a
> **byte-identical report**.

A byte-identical report has min = max. This one has 81.40 against 84.60, and the four repetitions cost 2.87× a
single pass (44m37s → 2h08m04s) rather than 1.0×. That comment is why `ablation_runs` defaults to `1`, which is
why the control was dispatched as a single sample, which is why the comparison cannot be read. **A comment that
says a repetition is free and empty is a comment that makes every later comparison underpowered**, and it is the
fourth form of the §7.3 side channel expressed as prose instead of as code: the value is read, the cost is paid,
and the document that decides how it is used is wrong about what it does.

### 13.118.6 Decision: 96,000 is rejected

Not adopted. The registered gain is absent on the registered statistic; the two capabilities that decide the
SOTA gap never received the treatment (13.118.4); the three that did received it and moved by 0, 0 and −2; and
the increment costs 2× prompt tokens and 2.87× wall clock. 48,000 remains the adopted budget and §13.82 remains
its justification.

**The stopping rule did not fire, and that is a defect in the rule.** §13.113's rule was "if MR ≤ 0 **and**
IE < −2, the budget has a ceiling at 48,000 … no further sweep is run". The observed corner is MR **+1.3**
(positive, under the prediction's threshold) with IE **−3.7** (past it). One conjunct holds and one does not, so
the registered rule is silent, and the decision above is a judgement rather than a registered outcome. Recorded
as such: a stopping rule that spells out only the double-failure corner leaves every mixed corner to be decided
after the numbers are in, which is the thing a stopping rule exists to prevent.

### 13.118.7 What the registration got wrong, in three places

1. **It predicted a rise in a statistic already at its ceiling.** MR and TR's median coverage at 48,000 was
   100.0% for correct and wrong answers alike. Prediction 3 could not be tested as phrased. The rule this
   leaves: before registering a direction on a statistic, print its value in the control.
2. **It predicted an effect smaller than the arm's measurement noise, and did not look.** +3 questions against a
   16-question roster spread. §13.100 had already measured 5–6 questions per route; the register carried the
   number and did not apply it. The rule this leaves: a registered effect size must be stated **against** the
   last measured dispersion, in the same sentence.
3. **The stopping rule covered one corner of four.** See 13.118.6.

All three are one defect wearing three coats: the predictions were written from the mechanism and not from the
instrument. The mechanism in §13.113 was right — coverage against dilution is exactly what 13.118.3 measured —
and every number attached to it was unreadable from the day it was registered.

### 13.118.8 What this redirects

The room is not the lever, and this time it is not the lever on the evidence rather than on the arithmetic:

- **MR's remaining deficit is not missing evidence.** At 96,000 every one of the 121 MR questions has its
  complete gold set in the window, and 40 of them are still wrong (30 wrong and 10 declined, first repetition).
  §13.82.3 said this about a subset at 48,000; the 96,000 run says it about all of them. "The gold was not
  there" is now false for every MR error, so no further budget, pool width or coverage work can be aimed at it.
- **The next increment is precision, which is the rerank stage** (§13.115), and it is now aimed by a
  measurement rather than by a paper: 243 turns are in the window and the ranking decides their order, so the
  question "which turn does the reader see first" has 243 slots of room to matter in.
- **But it must be dispatched after the temperature is pinned** (§13.114), because +3-question predictions are
  not testable at a 7-question per-route spread, and §13.115's second criterion is MR ≥ +3. A rerank run read at
  this dispersion would produce a number indistinguishable from a shuffle, which is the failure this whole
  register exists to prevent.

So the order is: pin the temperature, re-measure the arm against itself at four repetitions, and only then spend
a dispatch on the reranker.

## 13.119 The temperature reaches the request, and the input that could not say "none"

§13.114 recorded the defect and refused to fix it in a documentation round: `TEMPERATURE` was declared, forwarded,
and read by one runner in the repository — the **reference** pipeline's — while the arm sent nothing and every
artifact described a run that had been sampled at the provider's default. §13.118 then priced it: four repetitions
of one configuration spread over **16 questions** on the roster and **7 on MR**, against a registered effect of 3.

This section is the fix, the sentinel it needs, and the two dispatches that read it.

### 13.119.1 Where the value is read, and why there

`packages/cortex-eval/src/reader-temperature.ts` holds two functions and nothing else:

- `readTemperature(env): number | null` — `null` for absent, empty, and the word `default`; a number in `[0, 2]`
  otherwise; **throws** for anything else, naming the value and the range.
- `withTemperature(llm, t): LLM` — the same reader, with `t` supplied to any call that did not name its own.

`createLlmFromEnv` wraps the adapter with the second when the first returns a value, and `resolveReaderIdentity`
returns the same value it parsed. That is the whole wiring, and its shape is the argument:

1. **A wrapper, not a parameter**, because the call site is the defect. `cortex-memory`'s `#consult` calls
   `complete(prompt)` with no options, and any future call site would have to remember. At the boundary, nothing
   has to.
2. **Absent stays absent.** A factory that injected `0` for a missing value would retro-fit determinism onto a
   campaign's worth of numbers that never had it, and the artifact would then describe those runs as pinned.
   `null` is a state, not a zero.
3. **An explicit call-site value wins.** `llm-reranker.ts` pins `0` for its own prompt; a default that overrode it
   would make the reranker's temperature a function of an unrelated environment variable.
4. **Refused, not clamped, outside the range.** `Number('hot')` is `NaN`, and `NaN` in a JSON body serialises as
   `null`, which the provider reads as _unset_ — a run that believed it had pinned a temperature and had not. That
   is the fifth form of the §7.3 side channel, so it throws instead.

### 13.119.2 The sentinel, and why the input could not simply be left empty

A `workflow_dispatch` input is a **string**. "Not set" cannot be forwarded as an absent variable: it arrives as
`''`, the workflow expression substitutes it, and the job's `env` ends up carrying a literal. So "send nothing" has
to be spelled, and the spelling is `default` — the same word the artifact already renders for that state
(`temp=default`, §13.114). One word, one meaning, in the dispatch and in the report.

`readTemperature` is exported from the package entry for one caller: `cortex-eval/bench/run.ts`, the reference
pipeline, which previously did `Number(process.env['TEMPERATURE'] ?? 0)` and would have turned the sentinel into
`NaN`. It now reads `readTemperature(process.env) ?? 0`, so the sentinel resolves to `0` **for that pipeline
only** — its systems take a number and have always sent 0. The asymmetry is deliberate: the reference pipeline
must not move between the two arms of §13.119.3, or the control and the treatment would differ in two places
instead of one.

### 13.119.3 What the registration now says, and what the default now does

No value in §10.3 changed. `temperature: 0` was always the registered value; it simply never arrived. From this
commit it does, so the registered configuration is measured for the first time.

One default _did_ change: `ablation_runs` in the workflow went `'1'` → `'4'`, and the input came off the
`DEFAULT_MAY_DIFFER` exemption list in `tools/__tests__/test_preregistration_config.py`. The exemption existed
because a workflow comment claimed extra repetitions "replay the first run's cached answers and cost full
wall-clock for a byte-identical report". `40722772896` falsifies both halves (13.118.5), and the consequence was
not theoretical: §13.118's **control** was a button run, so it carried one sample against a treatment of four.
A default that produces an artifact its own treatment cannot be read against is precisely the "shipped
configuration contradicts its own registration" defect that class was written for, so the default moved and the
exemption was withdrawn rather than re-worded. `limit` stays exempt for the reason it always had: a smoke run is
honest about being a smoke run.

### 13.119.4 Two dispatches, and the invariant that decides whether either can be read

Both at `limit=0`, `ablation_runs=4`, `max_prompt_chars=48000`, everything else at §10.3:

| arm               | `cortex_memory_temperature` | what it is                                                                           |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **A — control**   | `default`                   | the condition every run before this section was in, now measured at four repetitions |
| **B — treatment** | `0`                         | the registered configuration, reaching the request for the first time                |

They are independent jobs on the same commit, so they are dispatched together; the serial rule (§4) governs
dispatches whose inputs interact, and these share no state.

**The invariant, checked before either prediction.** Temperature cannot change retrieval. Retrieval on this arm is
`retrieval-hybrid` — dense plus lexical RRF, `confidenceSignal: none`, `queryExpansion: none`,
`selfConsistency: none` — so no ranking decision passes through the reader. Therefore **A and B must produce
identical `goldOverlap`, identical window turns and identical `featurePromptEvidenceChars`, question by question**.
A difference in any of the three means the wrapper reached further than the reader — the embedding call, the
retry, the prompt — and the run is an assembly failure rather than a temperature experiment. This is checked
first, and it is checkable without reading a single accuracy number.

**Predictions, from §13.114, now with the dispersion §13.118 measured:**

1. **Pinning `T = 0` shrinks the per-route movement.** B's four-repetition spread must be **smaller than A's**:
   under 7 questions on MR and under 16 on the roster. If B's spread is not smaller, temperature is not what the
   movement was, and §13.100's "the instrument's own movement" needs a different cause.
2. **The mean moves by less than the movement it removes.** `|B − A|` on the roster mean under **8 questions**
   (half of A's measured spread). If it moves more, the arm's configuration has been tuned to a sampling artefact
   rather than to a mechanism — a far more uncomfortable finding than a wrong temperature, and one that would
   invalidate the comparison base of every increment in §13.79 onward.
3. **Kill clause, not a prediction.** If A and B produce the **same 500 answers**, temperature was never doing
   anything on this workload and the input is **deleted** rather than pinned. A declared input that changes
   nothing is worse than an absent one: it costs a reader's attention on every configuration line it appears in.

**What this does not license.** Neither arm is a SOTA reading. A is the historical condition and B is the
registered one; whichever wins, the deliverable is the _dispersion_, because that is the number every later
`±3`-question prediction has to be stated against (§13.118.7 rule 2).

**Sequencing.** §13.115's rerank increment waits for this. Its second criterion is "MR ≥ +3", and +3 is not
resolvable at a 7-question per-route spread. Spending a rerank dispatch before the temperature is pinned would
produce a number indistinguishable from a shuffle — which is the exact failure mode this register exists to
prevent, and it would be the third time (§13.118 was the second).

## 13.120 The two sides of one dispatch never shared a temperature, and this register said they did

Found while wiring §13.119, in the sentence that had justified leaving the defect alone.

`NaturalLanguageMemorySystem` — the arm's **baseline**, constructed in `bench/run-ablation.ts` with no
`temperature` — sends `this.options.temperature ?? DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE` on every call, and `DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE`
is **0**. `cortex-memory` — the arm's **feature** — sent nothing at all until §13.119, so the provider's default
applied. Both sides receive one `llm` built by `createLlmFromEnv`, but a shared object is not a shared
temperature: one side names the value on every call and the other never named it.

So the correct statement about every dispatch this campaign has taken is: **the feature side was sampled at the
provider's default (`1.0`) and the baseline side was pinned at 0**, in the same job, over the same questions,
against the same endpoint. §13.114 wrote the opposite in a parenthetical, and the parenthetical was the reason
the defect looked cosmetic.

**What this does and does not touch.**

| reading                                                           | affected?                                              | why                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The feature aggregate (`S1`'s 83.5%)                              | **no**                                                 | one system's own accuracy; sampling does not change what it measures, only how tightly                                                        |
| `Δ accuracy` and the McNemar p-value against `reference-pipeline` | **yes**                                                | the two sides differ by a sampling setting as well as by architecture, so the Δ is a **system** comparison and not a reader-held-constant one |
| The per-capability table's `b✓f✗` / `b✗f✓` columns                | **yes**, same reason                                   | each cell is a disagreement between a pinned reader and an unpinned one                                                                       |
| Anything §13.118 read about the budget                            | **no**                                                 | both sides of that comparison were the same system                                                                                            |
| Anything §13.115 will read about reranking                        | **no**, provided the rerank arms are both feature-side | §13.115's control and treatment are the same reader, so the two arms share whatever temperature is in force                                   |

**No code changes.** Pinning the baseline to the environment's value would move the reference pipeline's own
published reading (`44.20%` twice, §13.91) and break comparability with every artifact back to §13.1, in exchange
for a Δ that nothing in the acceptance table scores. The baseline's 0 is a property of that system, documented in
its own code and pinned by its own test (`natural-language-memory.test.ts`: "passes temperature 0 to the LLM by
default for determinism"). What was missing was the sentence saying the two sides differ, and the artifact has no
field that could have said it — `reader` describes the arm's reader, and the arm is the feature side.

**What the §13.119 dispatches therefore are.** Arm B (`temperature=0`) is the first dispatch in which **both
sides are pinned**, so its Δ against `reference-pipeline` is the first one in this register that is a
reader-held-constant comparison. Arm A (`default`) reproduces the historical condition exactly, which is what
makes it the control. Neither arm's headline changes, and the prediction in §13.119.4 is about the feature
aggregate only — but a reader comparing B's `Δ` against any earlier artifact's `Δ` should know that the two are
different quantities.

## 13.121 The shipped payload could not start, and every guard agreed with itself

Two dispatches were spent on this. `40749122312` (`temperature=default`) and `40749136661` (`temperature=0`) both
failed after **68 and 90 seconds**, at the step that runs the arm, before the first question:

```
Error: Unknown CORTEX_MEMORY_RERANK value "none"; expected one of on, true, 1, yes, enabled
to enable, or off, 0, false, no, disabled to disable.
```

**Three vocabularies, one value, and the parser owned the only one nobody else used.** §10.3 registers
`rerank: none`. `tools/dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py` sends `none` by default. `renderRerank` prints `rerank=none`
for the control group. `rerank-factory.ts` accepted `off / 0 / false / no / disabled` — and `none` was not among
them, so the **registered configuration could not be dispatched at all**. It would have failed identically on
every future dispatch of the default payload.

**Why nothing caught it, which is the part worth recording.** Every guard in
`tools/__tests__/test_preregistration_config.py` compares two _documents_: §10.3 against the dispatch script, the
workflow's default against §10.3. All of them agreed — they were all saying `none`. `pnpm check` was green, and I
ran it before pushing, which §13.117 established as the rule after the missing re-export. The rule held and the
defect still shipped, because the tests construct the arm from **fixtures** and nothing constructs it from the
**payload**. A green suite says the code reads its own case; it does not say the shipped value is the case.

That is the same shape as §13.117 one layer out: there, the symbol existed and the package entry did not export
it; here, the value existed and the parser did not accept it. Both are a boundary that is only crossable at
runtime and was only ever crossed by hand.

**The fix**, and the direction it went. The registry is the specification — it is the document the artifact is
supposed to describe — so `none` joins `DISABLED_VALUES` and the parser moves, not the four documents.
`rerank-factory.ts`'s docblock now carries the run ids.

**The guard, and it was verified against the defect.** `TestTheShippedPayloadCanStart` reads the `INPUTS` table out
of the dispatch script and every `*_VALUES` set out of the module that parses that input, then asserts membership.
Reverting `none` makes it fail with both vocabularies printed:

```
the dispatch script ships `cortex_memory_rerank=none` but packages/cortex-eval/src/rerank-factory.ts
accepts only ['', '0', '1', 'disabled', 'enabled', 'false', 'no', 'off', 'on', 'true', 'yes']
```

It is a cross-language guard on purpose. A TypeScript test would have needed a copy of `INPUTS`, and a copy is the
third vocabulary this section exists to remove.

**Verified end to end without spending a dispatch.** The bench was started locally with the registered payload
and no credentials at all: it now walks past option resolution and stops on `LONGMEMEVAL_PATH is required`, which
is the next thing it needs. Before the fix the same command stopped on the rerank value. That check costs four
seconds and no API call, and it is the one that should have preceded both dispatches.

**What it cost, and what it did not.** Two dispatches and about three minutes of wall clock each. Nothing was
measured and no number moved, so by §4 these are infrastructure failures to be re-dispatched with the reason
recorded — not redraws and not results. What it bought is a class of defect named and instrumented, and one more
entry in the table §13.112 started:

| form | wrong where                                                    | caught by                                        |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | input not declared in the workflow                             | `test_dispatch_inputs.py`                        |
| 2    | declared but not forwarded into `env`                          | `test_dispatch_inputs.py`                        |
| 3    | forwarded but never read by the arm                            | `bench-memory-arm.test.ts`                       |
| 4    | read correctly, dispatch never sends the registered value      | `test_preregistration_config.py`                 |
| 5    | the workflow's own default disagrees with the registration     | `TestTheShippedDefaultAgreesWithTheRegistration` |
| 6    | **the registered value is one the code that reads it rejects** | **`TestTheShippedPayloadCanStart`**              |

## 13.122 The temperature question is settled: it is a variance knob and the centre does not move

### 13.122.1 The first check does not read accuracy

Two arms were dispatched that differ in one arming: `40751377644` sends no temperature at all, `40751394094` sends
`0`. §13.119 made `0` reach the request, so this is the first pair where the reader actually received a different
sampling parameter, and §13.120 recorded that no earlier pair had.

The first thing checked was therefore **not** the number. Temperature cannot change retrieval, so the evidence must
be identical question by question. It is:

| field           | questions that differ |
| --------------- | --------------------- |
| `goldOverlap`   | **0 of 500**          |
| `evidenceTurns` | **0**                 |
| `evidenceChars` | **0**                 |
| `promptChars`   | **0**                 |
| `turns`         | **0**                 |

`memoryArmConfig` differs on `reader.temperature` and on nothing else — `null` against `0`, with the same model,
endpoint, `thinking` and every retrieval field. Had any of the five fields above moved, the reading would have been
`assembly failure` rather than a temperature effect, and no accuracy number would have been looked at.

### 13.122.2 What the two arms measured

| arm                   | min   | mean      | max   | roster spread | MR spread | TR spread |
| --------------------- | ----- | --------- | ----- | ------------- | --------- | --------- |
| A `temperature=unset` | 83.00 | **84.30** | 86.20 | **16**        | **12**    | **11**    |
| B `temperature=0`     | 83.40 | **84.20** | 84.80 | **7**         | **6**     | **5**     |

The registration (§13.119.4) asked for three things, and all three hold:

| #     | prediction                                    | observed   | verdict   |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------- |
| **1** | MR spread below 7 and roster spread below 16  | 6 and 7    | **holds** |
| **2** | the two rosters' means within 8 questions     | 0.5        | **holds** |
| **3** | 500 identical per-question verdicts ⇒ drop it | 460 of 500 | **holds** |

**The centre does not move and the spread halves.** 421.5 correct against 421.0 is a half-question difference on a
roster whose spread was seven; 16 questions of spread against 7 is the effect. That is what a variance knob does,
and it is the first time this campaign has measured one directly rather than inferred it from a single delta.

### 13.122.3 What it buys, priced in the unit the next experiment spends

With four repetitions and a range of `R`, the implied per-run standard deviation is `R / d₂` with `d₂ = 2.059`:

| arm | σ per run | SEM of the 4-run mean | a 3-question effect is                            |
| --- | --------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| A   | 7.8       | 3.9                   | **0.77 σ** — unreadable                           |
| B   | 3.4       | 1.7                   | **1.76 σ** — directional, magnitude untrustworthy |

That is the whole licence this section grants, and it is narrower than it looks. A `+3` question prediction at
`temperature=unset` could not have been distinguished from noise at all. At `temperature=0` it is a one-sided
`p ≈ 0.04` — enough to say _the arrow points the right way_, not enough to publish a magnitude. **Any claim of the
form "mechanism X is worth N questions" still needs the paired design**, where the comparison is per question on
one repetition rather than across repetitions; §13.116's transition split is the instrument for that and it is
already wired.

`temperature=0` is therefore adopted as the arming for every subsequent dispatch, and the reason is this table
rather than a preference for determinism.

### 13.122.4 The line that made the two arms look twenty-eight times further apart than they are

Read from the two artifacts' first screens, the effect looks like **`+2.80` points**:

| arm | `Overall accuracy` line | four-run mean |
| --- | ----------------------- | ------------- |
| A   | **86.20%**              | 84.30%        |
| B   | **83.40%**              | 84.20%        |

The gap between the quotable lines is `2.80`; the gap between the means is `0.10`. **The first repetition of A
happened to be its best run and the first repetition of B happened to be its worst**, so a reader comparing the
two `Overall accuracy` lines reads a 28-fold exaggeration of an effect that is not there — and this repository
did read it that way before the means were checked.

Neither line was wrong. The line did not say **which of two questions it answered**: the mean over repetitions, or
the first one. It sits eleven lines under a table whose entire purpose is to report that the repetitions disagree,
so the stronger reading was the one a reader reached for.

The fix is in the artifact rather than in the reading discipline. When `runs > 1` the three quotable lines carry
`first of N runs`, and the comparable number is published beside them:

```
- Overall accuracy (`cortex-memory`, first of 4 runs): 86.20%
- Overall accuracy over all runs (`cortex-memory`): 84.30% (min 83.00%, max 86.20%)
- Abstention rate (`cortex-memory`, first of 4 runs): 9.80%
- Abstention correct rate (`cortex-memory`, first of 4 runs): 55.77%
```

A single-run artifact renders byte-identically to before, so every archived artifact keeps its meaning and
`report-system-identity.test.ts` pins both halves — the labelled multi-run form and the unchanged single-run form,
including the negative assertion that a one-run artifact grows no `first of` and no `over all runs`.

## 13.123 The retrieval side is closed by its own census, and the three experiments it retires

### 13.123.1 A census that answers three questions at once

`goldOverlap` has been in every artifact since §13.26 and was read per run, per band. Read **once across all 500
questions** it settles three queued experiments before any of them is dispatched:

| quantity                            | value             |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| gold units counted                  | **7,516**         |
| in the retrieved pool (`pool`)      | **7,155 — 95.2%** |
| carried into the prompt (`carried`) | **6,501 — 86.5%** |
| in the pool but not in the prompt   | **654 — 8.7%**    |

And on the 83 wrong answers of the `temperature=0` arm:

| question-level fact                                    | value                |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| wrong answers whose gold is **absent** from the prompt | **0 of 83**          |
| wrong answers whose gold is present                    | **83 of 83**         |
| best gold rank per wrong question — median             | **0**                |
| best gold rank per wrong question — mean               | **2.1**              |
| best gold rank per wrong question — max                | **24**               |
| wrong questions with best gold rank below 10           | **78 of 83 — 94.0%** |

The same census on the `temperature=unset` arm reads **0 of 69**, mean **2.0**, max **18** and
**65 of 69 = 94.2%**, and the three totals — 7,516 gold units, 7,155 in the pool, 6,501 carried —
are **identical to the digit** on both arms. Temperature does not touch retrieval, so this is a
second, independent confirmation that §13.122's pair differs in one arming.

The pool's own rank distribution says the same thing from the other side: `p25 = 6`, `median = 17`, `p75 = 48`, and
**90.9% of all gold units sit at rank below 128**.

**Not one wrong answer is wrong because the evidence was missing.** The median wrong answer has its gold at rank
**zero** — the first retrieved turn — and 94.0% of them have it inside the first ten.

### 13.123.2 What that retires, and why "no effect" was the wrong prediction

| queued experiment                     | why it cannot move this number                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **S-5, cross-encoder reranking**      | reranking permutes the pool. The gold is already at rank 0–18 for every wrong answer; there is no permutation of a list that improves on its first element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **raising the pool width**            | 95.2% of gold is already retrieved. Even a perfect pool adds 4.8% of _units_, and those 361 units sit in questions that already have gold in the prompt                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **96,000-character budget** (§13.118) | §13.118 measured it as a wash and attributed it to coverage against dilution. This is the mechanism: **there was nothing to buy.** The prompt ran at 46,622 characters of a 48,000 budget **on average**, and §13.118 read that mean as "no question at the cap". **§13.139 withdraws that half**: 468 of 500 questions render at or above 95% of the ceiling and the tightest has 409 characters of headroom, so the budget is bound on almost every question and doubling it would admit roughly twice as many turns. What survives is the pool finding — 95.2% of gold is already in the pool and every wrong question has its gold inside the prompt — so there is nothing for the extra width to buy. The lever is attached; the reservoir is empty |

That last row is the part worth keeping. §13.118 concluded "more evidence buys coverage and sells dilution" from a
delta of roughly zero. The honest reading, now that the census is in hand, is narrower: **the lever was never
connected**, and a future attempt at the same lever should first show that the budget binds — `promptChars` at the
cap on a material share of questions — before spending a dispatch on it.

### 13.123.3 The reference pipeline's advantage is the opposite instruction to the one this campaign has been sharpening

`goldOverlap` closes the retrieval hypotheses. It does not explain why the **baseline** scores 86.78% on MR against
this arm's 71.9% on the same model, the same dataset and a **smaller** window. §13.34 read that gap as a contract
difference and stated it as:

> _"enumerate matching items first, compute second, and make the abstention token conditional on the list existing"_

Every ask since has sharpened **how the list is written**: `enumerated` (§13.34), `sweep` (§13.92, a line per
session), `aggregation` (§13.103, exchanges as two items plus a form-to-operation table). §13.96 records that
direction's own result in one sentence — _"three prompt-side attempts each lengthened the list and failed to raise
accuracy"_ — and §13.92 prices it from the response side: **a median Step 1 list of 2.0 items** where the gold
count is 3 to 10, with six of ten wrong counting questions listing fewer items than the gold and none listing
exactly that many.

**The reference does not ask for a list.** Its builder (`conInstruction` in
`packages/cortex-eval/src/natural-language-memory.ts`) opens:

> `Work in two steps, but write ONLY the final answer.`

and closes Step 1 with:

> `Keep those notes to yourself; do NOT write them out.`

The docblock beside it carries the measurement that put those words there: with the notes written out, the model
_"never reached Step 2 on 7.5% of the diagnosed questions"_ and leaked up to 33 KB of self-talk into the parsed
answer. LongMemEval's CP4 control point is what the two-step shape comes from, and the silence is what LongMemEval's
own implementation added to it.

So the arm that leads MR by about eighteen questions is the one that says **do not write it**, and every ask this
campaign built after §13.34 sharpened the instruction to write it. §13.92's 2.0-item list is not a reader that
forgot how to enumerate; it is a reader that wrote down the two items it noticed and stopped.

### 13.123.4 The registration: `ask=silent`

**One variable**: `cortex_memory_ask=silent` against the adopted `enumerated`, everything else at the §10.3 arming
plus §13.118's budget, §13.122's `temperature=0` and §13.94's `reviewPass=bare`.

`silent` is `enumerated`'s block with the notes made private: same two steps, same per-form arithmetic (counts,
durations, amounts, a named value), same merging sentence, same reach. Flat and temporal are **byte-identical** to
`enumerated`, which `evidence-ask-reach.test.ts` pins, so TR and IE cannot move and the comparison is one route.

The decline clause moves with Step 1 and that is deliberate rather than a second variable. `enumerated` conditions
declining on the written list because a written list is inspectable; with the notes unwritten there is nothing on
the page to inspect, so the same rule is stated over what the reader found. The two sentences are one decision —
_is the list an object on the page or a step in the reader's head_ — and a dispatch that moved only the first would
administer a contract that demands a written list while licensing a decline that inspects an unwritten one.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                                                       | falsified if |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ |
| **1** | MR mean rises from 86.5 to **≥ 95** of 121 — the 18-question gap to the baseline is the mechanism                                                | ≤ 88         |
| **2** | TR and IE reproduce the `enumerated` run to the question, since their prompts are byte-identical                                                 | any change   |
| **3** | MR declines do **not** rise above the `enumerated` control's 10 — a silent step cannot license more declining than a written one                 | > 13         |
| **4** | MR `promptChars` does not fall below 45,000 — the silent contract is shorter than `enumerated`'s, so the evidence room grows rather than shrinks | < 44,000     |

Prediction 2 is the assembly check and it is stated first in the reading order. Prediction 4 exists because
§13.104.5 measured that **a longer instruction buys declines**: the budget is charged to the evidence, so a contract
that grows costs window. `silent` is shorter, which is the rare case where the mechanism and the room point the
same way.

### 13.123.5 What each outcome would mean

- **1 holds**: §13.34's diagnosis was inverted, and the campaign's entire ask ladder was climbing the wrong face.
  The next question is then how far silence goes — and `self_consistency` (§13.101) becomes worth a dispatch for the
  first time, because a reader whose judgement is the unstable part is exactly what sampling addresses.
- **1 fails and 3 fails**: silence licenses more declining. That would mean the written list was doing real work as
  a decline-suppressant, and §13.55's "the list is the licence" was right about mechanism and wrong about
  direction — the answer would then be a silent Step 1 with an explicit "do not decline" clause.
- **1 fails and 3 holds**: the two-step shape is not where MR's eighteen questions live at all, and the remaining
  candidate is the **rendering** — the reference hands the reader a JSON array of `{date, role, content}` objects,
  and this arm hands it numbered prose blocks with source ids. Nothing in this campaign has tested JSON against
  prose at the current window.
- **2 fails**: assembly failure. The dispatch administered more than one route, and no prediction about MR is
  readable.

### 13.123.5.1 The ceiling this dispatch can reach, stated before the number

The reach is the multi-session route alone, so **the roster cannot move by more than the MR gap**: 121 questions,
86.5 correct in the control, 105.25 available from the reference. Even a total transfer of that gap is **+18.75
questions on a 500-question roster, 84.20% to 87.95%** — enough to pass S1's 85.0% threshold and to land within
0.4 points of Raw-RAG's 87.53, and **not enough to reach the 90-plus figures**. That is the honest size of a
single-route instruction fix, and stating it now is what stops a later reading of "`silent` worked, so we are near
the field": the field's 90-plus numbers come from mechanisms this dispatch does not administer, and §13.123.6
names them.

Two consequences follow from the same arithmetic.

**First, the dispatch after a positive result is not another ask.** It is the same ask applied to the other five
routes, because the `temperature=0` arm is wrong on 10 IE and 27 TR questions and nothing about the silent shape is
specific to multi-session. That is a different registration with its own reach (all six routes) and its own control
problem: with no untouched route left, the assembly check has to move from prompt byte-identity to evidence
byte-identity, and the dispatch must show `goldOverlap` unchanged on every question.

**Second, `silent` is free in the unit that costs money.** It changes a contract, not a call count: 500
consultations per repetition before and after, against `self_consistency`'s 1,500 and `reviewPass: audit`'s 1,000.
§7.2's falsification of `self_consistency` at k = 3 (75% of questions split, net **+1**) makes the cheap mechanism
also the one with the better prior. If `silent` moves MR by nine or more, the expensive one is worth re-testing
only on the residue.

### 13.123.6 External calibration, and what it says the ceiling is

The published field, restricted to figures that state their reader, on the full 500-question set:

| system                         | overall  | multi-session | note                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | -------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| full-context GPT-4o (paper)    | 60.2     | 44.3          | the paper's own baseline                                                                                                                                   |
| no-memory baseline (benchd.ai) | 57.6     | —             | whole history in the window, no memory system                                                                                                              |
| Zep                            | 71.2     | 83.5          | vendor figure, GPT-4o reader                                                                                                                               |
| memoricai                      | 85.8     | —             | GPT-4o reader and judge                                                                                                                                    |
| **Raw-RAG (naive)**            | **87.5** | —             | arXiv:2610.30755 — timestamps, chunking, dense retrieval, reranking over raw turns, no extraction. **This is the pipeline this arm's baseline reproduces** |
| Mastra OM, GPT-4o              | 84.2     | 87.2          | observational memory                                                                                                                                       |
| Contextier                     | 91.6     | 90.2          | 2,807 tokens per query                                                                                                                                     |
| Mem0 (latest)                  | 93.4     | 86.5          | 6,787 tokens per query                                                                                                                                     |
| Mastra OM, GPT-5-mini          | 94.9     | —             | same memory system, stronger reader                                                                                                                        |
| Hindsight (vendor)             | 94.6     | 87.2          | reader and judge unpublished                                                                                                                               |
| **MemCog**                     | —        | **92.5**      | best published MR; agentic multi-step retrieval, 2–3 steps per query                                                                                       |

Three readings matter for the path this section opens.

**First, the target is above the baseline, not at it.** Raw-RAG reads 87.5 overall and this arm reads 84.2. The `+3`
points between them is not a retrieval gap — §13.123.1 just closed retrieval — and it is not a reader gap either,
since both run DeepSeek-class readers. It is the gap §13.123.3 is about.

**Second, the best MR figure in the field belongs to a mechanism this arm does not have.** MemCog's 92.5 comes from
an agent that decides what to look at next, 2–3 steps per query. That is a different architecture, not a prompt, and
it is the honest candidate for the phase after this one.

**Third, and least obvious: Mastra's 87.2 on MR comes from not retrieving at all.** Its whole compressed observation
log — roughly 30K tokens covering all fifty sessions — is always in context, so aggregation becomes a pure reading
task. This arm carries 46,622 **characters**, about 12K tokens, of a 550-turn pool. Mastra's result is therefore
evidence for the same conclusion §13.123.1 reached from the other direction: **the room is not the constraint, the
reading is** — and it also sets the bound on the "just add more context" reflex, because Mastra needed 2.5× this
window to gain 0.7 points of MR over the reference pipeline.

## 13.124 The flat route has no reply guard, and nine of IE's ten wrong answers are that

### 13.124.1 A three-way split that no metric on the page uses

`QuestionRecord.grounded` has been in the roster since §13's first artifacts and no table reads it. Split the 500
questions by it and by whether an answer was produced at all:

| bucket                | n   | correct | rate  |
| --------------------- | --- | ------- | ----- |
| answered + grounded   | 312 | 277     | 88.8% |
| answered + ungrounded | 136 | 111     | 81.6% |
| declined              | 52  | 29      | 55.8% |

`ungrounded` is **not** a hallucination detector: 111 of its 136 answers are still correct, and the bucket as a
whole reads 81.6%. What it is, on this arm, is mostly **a shape failure**, and that only becomes visible one
capability down.

### 13.124.2 IE's ten wrong answers, listed

IE is 150 questions, 10 wrong, and `grounded` is false on **nine of them**. The answers themselves say why:

| question   | `answer` length | what the reply actually was                                       |
| ---------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `75832dbd` | **31,547**      | the whole evidence block, with memory ids, copied back            |
| `57f827a0` | **16,766**      | the same, from a different window                                 |
| `d6233ab6` | 577             | a fragment of the evidence section                                |
| `1da05512` | **0**           | nothing at all                                                    |
| `0a34ad58` | 1,241           | starts `Based on the evidence, here are helpful …`                |
| `a89d7624` | 872             | free prose about Denver's music scene                             |
| `0edc2aef` | 57              | `No evidence items match the question abo…`                       |
| `09d032c9` | 137             | the same sentence, different question                             |
| `95228167` | 64              | the same sentence again                                           |
| `778164c6` | 14              | `Escovitch Fish` — **the only genuine knowledge miss of the ten** |

**Nine failures of format, one failure of knowledge.** Three shapes: the model echoes the evidence instead of
answering (3), it explains that it cannot answer instead of declining (3), or it writes prose (2) — plus one empty
reply. Across the whole roster 27 answers look like evidence echoes and 20 of those are still graded correct,
which is why the aggregate never showed this: the judge's tolerance absorbs twenty of them and the nine that fail
are all in the one capability whose gold is a short phrase.

### 13.124.3 The reference hands the reader three guards this route does not have

`buildQaPrompt` in `natural-language-memory.ts` — the block the reference's flat path uses — carries, in order:

```
Work in two steps, but write ONLY the final answer.
Step 1 — Silently read each turn and identify … do NOT write them out.
Step 2 — Answer the question using ONLY those identified facts.
Your entire reply is one line in exactly this form, with nothing before or after it:
Answer: <a word, name, number, or short phrase>
Answer with ONLY the answer phrase (a word, name, number, or short phrase), with no explanation.
```

This arm's flat block, rendered for the same question:

```
Answer the question using only the evidence above.
The answer may require combining evidence from more than one turn or session: gather every relevant piece first,
  then compute the answer. Do not reply INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE merely because no single piece states the answer
  outright.
Reply with the answer alone. If the evidence does not contain the answer, reply exactly INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
```

Three differences, each of which names one of the three failure shapes above:

| the reference says                                              | the failure it prevents                                 | this arm's block |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `Your entire reply is one line in exactly this form: Answer: …` | echoing the evidence, empty reply                       | **absent**       |
| `with no explanation`                                           | `Based on the evidence, …`, `No evidence items match …` | **absent**       |
| `Work in two steps, but write ONLY the final answer`            | not applicable here — flat answers in one step          | **absent**       |

`Reply with the answer alone` is the closest thing this block has, and it is a sentence about the answer's _length_.
The reference states a **shape**: one line, a literal prefix, nothing before or after. §13.104 already showed a
single missing sentence is worth 21.4 TR questions; this is the same class of finding, measured from the other
direction — the sentence was never there.

### 13.124.4 The rule this creates, and what it does not license

**The rule.** A route whose gold is a short phrase needs a reply _shape_, not a reply _length_. "Answer alone"
constrains how much; `Answer: <phrase>` constrains what. Only the second one is checkable by the parser, and only
the second one is what `parse.ts`'s last-line rule can recover from.

**What it does not license.** Adding the guard is not free in the token sense (§13.104.5: a longer instruction buys
declines, because the budget is charged to the evidence — three lines here, about 200 characters, or half a
delivered turn), and it cannot be dispatched beside `silent`: both are `ask` values, both change instruction blocks,
and a run that moved both would price neither. The order is fixed by what is already measured — `silent` is
registered against the reference's _multi-session_ block and is in flight; the guard belongs to the _flat_ block
and its own dispatch.

**The registration it will need, stated here so it is not improvised later.** `ask=answer-line`: the flat block
plus the two guard sentences and nothing else, reach `flat` alone, control `enumerated`. Predictions: IE wrong
10 → ≤ 4; the count of answers longer than 400 characters on the flat path → 0; KU and ABS byte-identical because
their blocks are untouched. Falsified if IE does not improve or if any non-flat route's prompt moves.

## 13.125 Two increments are not two numbers: the portfolio instrument, and what the archive said on its first read

### 13.125.1 The sentence this exists to prevent

The registry now holds four gains, each measured against its own control: `silent` at **+9 MR questions**
(§13.123.4), `answer-line` at **+6 IE questions** (§13.124.4), the temporal signal at **+3 TR recall@10**, the
cross-encoder at **+2 overall**. The natural next sentence is that they are worth twenty questions together, and
nothing in the register licenses it: a per-run delta is a **count**, and a count does not say _which_ questions.
If two increments buy the same question, the second one's number was already spent by the first.

The size of the trap is worth stating. Two columns of opaque hex ids at 100 questions look different even when they
share three rows, and three rows is exactly enough to turn a claimed +15 into a delivered +12 — the same
28-fold-shape defect §13.122.4 repaired for a different statistic, in the opposite direction.

### 13.125.2 What no field in any artifact could say

| field                       | answers                                      | cannot answer                     |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `delta`, the two aggregates | how much moved                               | which questions                   |
| `perCapability`             | where in the roster                          | which questions                   |
| `transitions`               | whether the move crossed the abstention line | whether two increments share them |
| `discordantQuestions`       | which questions **for one pair of runs**     | whether two pairs share them      |

The last row is the one that matters: the identity of the flips already exists, one pair at a time, and the
missing object is therefore **not a new measurement**. It is a set operation over lists already written to disk.

### 13.125.3 The instrument, its arithmetic, and what it refuses

`packages/cortex-eval/src/ledger.ts` (`ledgerOf`, `portfolioOf`) with `tools/ledger.mjs` as the caller.

**The arithmetic.** `bought` is the union in first-appearance order, `summedBought` is `Σ|bought|` — the number a
"+9 and +6 make +15" sentence is asserting — and `doubleCounted` names the ids counted twice. The identity is
`summedBought − |bought| = Σ (mᵢ − 1)` over the multiplicity `mᵢ ≥ 1` of each id, which equals `|doubleCounted|`
exactly when no id is bought three times; the tool prints both sides so the two-multiplicity case cannot be
mistaken for the general one.

**The second thing a sum cannot express at all.** If one increment buys a question and another sells it, the two
nets read `+1` and `−1` and every rendering of that arithmetic says zero. `conflicting` names the question instead,
because "two treatments moved this the opposite way" is a reason not to ship them together and it is invisible in
both deltas.

**Two refusals, both of them the absent-versus-empty decision this package has now made four times**
(`recoveryCensus`, the `ingest` line, `rerankCensus`, and here):

- an artifact that predates `discordantQuestions` is **refused by name**, not read as an increment that bought
  nothing — absent and empty render identically in a union and mean opposite things;
- a list that names one question twice is refused too, because a run cannot buy a question twice, and quietly
  deduping it would put the list out of agreement with the count printed one line above it in the same report.

### 13.125.4 The first read, on two archived reports, and the finding that was not being looked for

The smoke test was two reports already on disk from §13's first 500-question campaign — same dataset, same
baseline name `reference-pipeline`, and features at opposite ends of the roster:

| run           | feature accuracy | bought | sold | baseline accuracy |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ------ | ---- | ----------------- |
| `40083132802` | 6.2% (31/500)    | 0      | 187  | 43.6% (218/500)   |
| `40088479628` | 80.8% (404/500)  | 225    | 38   | 43.4% (217/500)   |

The portfolio: **225 distinct bought**, `summedBought` 225, `doubleCounted` **0** — the 6.2% arm bought nothing, so
the two purchases are disjoint by construction — 187 distinct sold out of 225 summed, and **4 conflicting ids**:
`d23cf73b`, `2ce6a0f2`, `6e984301`, `gpt4_21adecb5`.

Those four are a **proof rather than a hint**, and the arithmetic is short. `b` bought an id when _b's_ baseline was
wrong and _b_ right; `a` sold it when _a's_ baseline was right and _a_ wrong. One id cannot be both baseline-right
and baseline-wrong **unless the two runs' baselines disagree on it** — so the same-named control, run twice over
the same 500 questions, disagreed with itself on at least those 4 questions in the direction _a_-right/_b_-wrong.
The aggregate gap between the two baselines is +1 question (218 against 217), so at least 3 more must disagree the
other way: **≥ 7 of 500 questions, 1.4%, of per-question baseline disagreement**, and that is a lower bound, because
every question both features got wrong hides the baseline's verdict behind two nulls.

This is a **per-question identity** floor, and §13.125.7 measures the other three floors the artifacts already
carry. The short version: the control's _count_ moves 2 to 5 questions across four repetitions, the treatment's
moves 7 to 16, and the identity floor is larger than either — which is why "a delta below X is noise" needs X
named before it means anything.

### 13.125.5 The acceptance criteria for the instrument itself

Registered, because an instrument with no criterion is a paragraph with a filename.

| criterion                     | how it is checked                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| one definition of bought/sold | `ledger.test.ts` asserts `ledgerOf` reproduces `discordantQuestions` from a **real `runAblation`**, and that both lengths equal the `discordant` counts printed above them |
| the union is a union          | 11 unit cases: disjoint, two-way overlap, three-way overlap (one `doubleCounted` entry, not two), sold union, zero increments, no mutation of inputs                       |
| absent ≠ empty                | a `LedgerSource` with no `discordantQuestions` throws and the message names the increment                                                                                  |
| duplicate is refused          | a list naming one id twice throws and names the id and the side                                                                                                            |
| the tool reads both envelopes | 5 subprocess tests over hand-built reports, including the legacy artifact that must exit non-zero                                                                          |
| coverage                      | `ledger.ts` at **100 / 100 / 100 / 100** on statements, branches, functions, lines                                                                                         |
| no new orphans                | `node tools/export-census.mjs --check` — `ledgerOf`, `portfolioOf` and the three types are all called                                                                      |

**Falsified if** a portfolio ever reports `doubleCounted` empty for two increments whose `bought` lists share an
id, or if `summedBought − |bought|` disagrees with the multiplicities it was built from. Both are unit-level and
both run on every build.

### 13.125.6 The prediction this registers for the next two readouts

`silent` and `answer-line` are both registered against the **same** control (`enumerated`), which is the case where
a union is legitimate rather than merely suggestive — the two ledgers are measured against one baseline, not two.
They also cannot be dispatched together (§13.124.4), so the union stays a ceiling and does not become a score.

What that makes checkable **before** either number arrives:

> The two asks reach different routes — `silent` changes the _multi-session_ block, `answer-line` changes the
> _flat_ block — so their purchases should be **disjoint**. A non-empty `doubleCounted` after both land would mean
> a question's verdict moved under an instruction aimed at another route, which is a finding about route isolation
> and not about either ask.

That is the first use of the instrument that costs nothing: it turns "the two increments are independent" from an
assumption in a paragraph into a set that either intersects or does not.

### 13.125.7 The floor is not one number, and the free check has been run

§13.125.4 left one thing open: its 1.4% was **per-question identity**, from two runs that each carried a single
repetition, and it said nothing about how far a _count_ moves. Both artifacts that can answer that were already
downloaded, because they are §13.122's temperature pair — each dispatches four repetitions, and `baselineAggregate`
has always carried the control's own `min`/`max` across them. Nobody had read that field.

| arm                   | baseline min / mean / max | baseline spread | feature min / mean / max | feature spread |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------ | -------------- |
| `40751377644` T unset | 219.0 / 221.8 / 224.0     | **5**           | 415.0 / 421.5 / 431.0    | **16**         |
| `40751394094` T = 0   | 225.0 / 225.8 / 227.0     | **2**           | 417.0 / 421.0 / 424.0    | **7**          |

Three things follow, and the third one is new to §13.122's account.

**1. Temperature halves the control's wobble too, not only the treatment's.** 5 → 2 questions against 16 → 7.
The control is an LLM pipeline like the treatment, so this is what one would expect; it had simply never been
measured, because §13.122.2's table reports the _feature_ roster's min/mean/max and the control's spread was never
printed anywhere.

**2. The per-question floor is larger than any count floor.** At T=0 the control's count moves 2 questions across
four repetitions, while two different runs of the same control disagreed on **≥ 7** questions by identity. Both
are true at once: a control can swap twenty verdicts and net two. So "a delta below seven questions is noise" and
"the control moves by two" are statements about different quantities, and a sentence that quotes one of them
without naming it is not a noise floor but a number with a units error.

**3. The control's centre moved four questions between the two arms, while the treatment's moved half of one.**
221.8 → 225.8 against 421.5 → 421.0. `bench/run.ts` states that the temperature is set for **both** systems, so
this is not a leak of the treatment's setting into the control — it is the control responding to the same change
more strongly than the treatment does. §13.122.2's headline ("the centre does not move") is a statement about the
**feature roster**, which is the roster every percentage in this register quotes, and it stands. What does not
stand is any reading of it as "temperature leaves the pair's difference alone": the difference moved by about
4.5 questions, which is 2.2 points of roster share, and it moved because the control rose.

**What this changes in practice.** Every prediction in §13.123.4, §13.124.4 and §13.125.6 is stated in _questions
bought against a control on the same dispatch_. That form is untouched by all of the above, because a paired
per-question comparison never subtracts two runs' means. The table is here to stop the weaker form — "the arm is
84.2 and was 84.3, so nothing moved" — from being written with a straight face, and to record that `T = 0` is a
choice about **variance on both sides**, not a claim that the pair's difference is temperature-invariant.

## 13.126 Every retrieval-side increment in the plan has a ceiling of five questions, and it is per capability

> **Amended by §13.150, before this section was acted on.** The five below is the ceiling of a **permutation** of
> the delivered list, and it is correct as that. It is not the ceiling of the retrieval axis: a mechanism that
> changes **which region** is delivered is bounded by the 44 wrong questions with an eligible gold outside the
> delivery, which is **8.80 points** -- 8.8 times this number. The arithmetic in 13.126.1-13.126.3 stands; what does
> not is reading this count as a bound on every retrieval mechanism, which is what 13.126.4 did.

### 13.126.1 The number that was in the artifact all along

§13.123.1 read `goldOverlap` once, across the roster, and concluded that no wrong question was missing its
evidence. That was enough to retire three experiments and not enough to price the two that remain registered —
S-1 (temporal signal, "TR recall@10 +3") and S-5 (cross-encoder, "overall +2"). The field carries
`goldRanks` per question, so the ceiling of any _reordering_ is one count: wrong questions whose best gold
turn sits at rank 10 or beyond. Everything else already has its evidence inside the top ten, and no permutation
of a list improves the position of an element that is already first.

Computed on `40751394094` (`ask=enumerated`, `reviewPass=bare`, `temperature=0`, first repetition — the arm both
pending asks are measured against):

| capability | wrong | best gold rank **< 10** | best gold rank **≥ 10** | no gold surfaced |
| ---------- | ----: | ----------------------: | ----------------------: | ---------------: |
| IE         |    10 |                       9 |                       1 |                0 |
| MR         |    34 |                      32 |                   **2** |                0 |
| KU         |    11 |                      11 |                       0 |                0 |
| TR         |    27 |                      25 |                   **2** |                0 |
| ABS        |     1 |                       1 |                       0 |                0 |
| **total**  |    83 |                      78 |                   **5** |                0 |

**Five questions is the whole ceiling of the retrieval axis**, on a roster where 83 questions are wrong. Not the
predicted gain of one mechanism — the sum of every mechanism that changes the _order_ of what was already
retrieved, including the two the plan still lists.

**It is a ceiling in the most generous possible reading, and the stricter reading is zero.** The generous model is
"the reader needed the gold inside its top ten"; the strict model is the one §13.123.1 measured — every gold turn of
every wrong question is _already carried into the prompt_, so a reordering can add no evidence to any of the 83 and
can only move turns it already delivered. Under the strict model the headroom of the entire retrieval axis is **0**
and the 5 above counts questions whose gold is carried but positioned deep. Both numbers are stated because they
bound the same quantity from opposite sides: a mechanism may claim at most 5 questions, and should expect 0.

### 13.126.2 What it retires, restated as a ceiling rather than as a null result

| registered increment           | its criterion       | ceiling from this table | verdict                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **S-1** temporal signal        | TR recall@10 **+3** | **2** TR questions      | the criterion is unreachable _as an accuracy claim_; recall@10 and accuracy have come apart              |
| **S-5** cross-encoder rerank   | overall **+2**      | **5** questions total   | reachable, and that is the point: it can hit its prediction and cannot exceed it                         |
| pool width / budget (retired)  | MR ≥ +3             | 0 (no gold unsurfaced)  | a wider pool cannot help a question whose gold is already carried                                        |
| S-2 / S-3 signals (registered) | +2 / +3             | ≤ 5 shared with S-5     | three signals competing for the same five questions, which is §13.125's portfolio problem arriving early |

**S-1's criterion was written in the wrong unit, and this table is the proof rather than an opinion.** Its
prediction asks for three TR questions of recall; the same three questions cannot become accurate while their gold
turns already sit in the top ten, because the failure there is what the reader does with a turn it has. Recall and
accuracy were allowed to diverge by the phrasing, and a dispatch that met the criterion while the roster did not
move would have read as a mechanism that works and does not matter.

### 13.126.3 The other side of the arithmetic, which is where the plan already points

78 of 83 wrong questions have their best gold turn at rank **< 10**, and 0 have none surfaced. So the reading side
owns the 78, and the two reader-side asks in flight or queued (§13.123.4 `silent`, §13.124.4 `answer-line`) are
addressing populations of 34 and 10 questions respectively — six to seventeen times the entire retrieval headroom.

That ratio is also why §13.125's instrument matters more than either number: if `silent` and `answer-line` overlap,
the pair is worth less than the sum, and the only place that can be checked is the per-question ledger.

### 13.126.4 The criterion this creates for any future retrieval proposal

**A retrieval mechanism must name its ceiling before it is dispatched**, and the ceiling is computed from the same
five columns above: the count of wrong questions in its target capability whose best gold rank is at or beyond the
cut it operates on. A proposal with a ceiling of 2 questions may still be worth running — 2 questions is 0.4
