points — but it may not be described as a path to the threshold, and it may not be registered in the unit of
recall.

## 13.127 The reference's private-notes clause costs 26 MR questions, and the reader is not deterministic at zero

Run `40792853362`, `ask=silent`, four repetitions, temperature 0, everything else at the registered configuration.
This is the readout of §13.123.4's registration, and the registration it wrote is **refuted in the opposite
direction**.

### 13.127.1 The first check, which passed

One field differs from the control `40751394094`:

| field | control      | silent   |
| ----- | ------------ | -------- |
| `ask` | `enumerated` | `silent` |

`askRoutes` follows from the value and is not a second change. And the evidence is untouched: the **carried turn
text is byte-identical on 445 of 500 questions**, and on IE, KU, TR and ABS the five retrieval fields
(`goldOverlap`, `evidenceTurns`, `evidenceChars`, `promptChars`, carried turns) agree on every question.

The 55 questions that differ are all MR, and the reason is mechanical rather than accidental: `silent`'s
multi-session block is shorter (it drops the write-it-out clause), the prompt builder spends the saved room on
evidence, and each of those 55 gains exactly one turn and up to 444 characters. That is §13.104.5's budget
coupling — an instruction change is never purely an instruction change on the route it touches — and it is why
the attribution below has to be split, not just reported.

### 13.127.2 The second check, which failed — and what it means

§13.123.4 asked for TR and IE to **reproduce question for question**, because their blocks are byte-identical
between the two arms. They did not:

| capability   | prompt identical | verdict changed | correct → wrong | wrong → correct | answer text changed |
| ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ------------------- |
| IE           | 150 of 150       | **7**           | 3               | 4               | 41                  |
| KU           | 72 of 72         | **4**           | 0               | 4               | 32                  |
| TR           | 127 of 127       | **8**           | 3               | 5               | 118                 |
| ABS          | 30 of 30         | **0**           | 0               | 0               | 0                   |
| **all four** | 379 of 379       | **19 (5.0%)**   | 6               | 13              | **191 (50.4%)**     |

This is **not** an assembly failure: the prompts are identical, checked field by field on all 379 questions. It is
the **reader**. At `temperature = 0`, given a byte-identical prompt, DeepSeek returns different text for half the
questions and a different verdict for one in twenty.

**Nothing in this register had measured this, and the closest prior number is not it.** §13.122.2 counts **40 of
500** verdicts differing between two arms whose configuration differed **in temperature** — a legitimate measurement
of temperature, and usable as evidence that temperature matters (its third prediction was written as "500 identical
verdicts ⇒ drop the arming", and 460 was read as "therefore keep it"). It is not a churn measurement: the sampling
parameter differed, so the 40 belong at least partly to the treatment. The pair in this section is the first with
**both** a byte-identical prompt and an identical configuration, and it puts the floor at 5.0%.

**The rule this fixes.** The assembly check is _prompt identity_, never verdict identity. A registered criterion
that says "the untouched routes must reproduce question for question" is unsatisfiable and would have failed every
correct experiment. §13.122.1 already walked this line for retrieval fields and stopped one field short of the
verdict.

### 13.127.3 The number

| arm                  | IE  | MR     | KU  | TR  | ABS | roster (first repetition) | roster (mean of four) |
| -------------------- | --- | ------ | --- | --- | --- | ------------------------: | --------------------: |
| control `enumerated` | 140 | **87** | 61  | 100 | 29  |                       417 |    421.0 (83.4–84.8%) |
| treatment `silent`   | 141 | **61** | 65  | 102 | 29  |                       398 |    399.5 (78.6–81.0%) |

**MR: 87 → 61, a loss of 26 questions.** The registered prediction was "MR ≥ 95", i.e. a gain of nine. Everything
else is inside the floor of §13.127.2: IE +1, KU +4, TR +2, ABS 0, a net +7 across 379 unchanged prompts, which is
the same order as the 19 that churned.

### 13.127.4 The attribution, and why it is not the environment

Three explanations are available and the artifact separates them.

**1. The environment did not do it.** The four capabilities whose prompts are byte-identical — 379 questions — moved
**+7 net**. A session-level degradation would have dragged those down too, so the loss is local to MR.

**2. The extra evidence did not do it either, and here is the split:**

| MR subgroup                                    |   n | control correct | silent correct |   delta |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --: | --------------: | -------------: | ------: |
| carried turns byte-identical                   |  66 |              48 |             31 | **−17** |
| carried turns +1 (shorter block bought a turn) |  55 |              39 |             30 |  **−9** |

Two thirds of the loss happens on questions where the reader received **exactly the same turns** and only the
instruction moved. The remaining −9 coincides with one more turn of evidence per question, which is the opposite
of the §13.104.5 direction (more evidence has always cost declines, never content) and is therefore read as small-n
rather than as a mechanism.

**3. What the wrong answers look like.** Of the 22 correct→wrong flips on identical evidence, the misses are
**under-sums**, not declines and not prose. Four examples:

| question                         | gold    | control wrote         | silent wrote |
| -------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ------------ |
| `gpt4_d84a3211` (bike expenses)  | 185     | `25 + 40 + 120 = 185` | `65`         |
| `6cb6f249` (social-media breaks) | 17 days | `17`                  | `10`         |
| `36b9f61e` (luxury items)        | 2,500   | `2500`                | `2000`       |
| `gpt4_59c863d7` (model kits)     | 5       | `5`                   | `6`          |

The control's own answer to the first one is the mechanism written out in the model's hand: it adds three
numbers and shows the three. The silent arm adds two of them and shows nothing. **The written list is the state
Step 2 counts from, and a list that is not written is not a list** — Step 1's output has nowhere to live, so
"count the items you identified" becomes "count the items you can remember".

### 13.127.5 Why the reference pipeline's clause does not transfer

§13.123.3 read the reference builder correctly — it does say _write ONLY the final answer_ and _do NOT write them
out_ — and drew the wrong inference from it. The clause is one of a set in that builder:

- `Work in two steps, but write ONLY the final answer.`
- `Step 1 — Silently read each turn and identify <the items>.` — **identify**, not _enumerate across sessions_
- `Step 2 — Answer the question using ONLY those identified facts.`
- one line, literal `Answer:` prefix, `with no explanation`

This arm adopted the privacy clause while keeping its own merging sentence, which explicitly licenses combining
evidence "from more than one turn or session", and its own Step 1 that walks **every session the prompt printed**.
Those are different tasks. A per-session walk produces a list whose length is the answer; asking the same walk to
happen in the model's head, with no place to put each session's line, removes precisely the artifact that made the
count possible. The reference's version works because its Step 1 identifies items for _one_ question, and the next
sentence tells the model what to do with them; it never asks the reader to hold thirty sessions in working memory.

### 13.127.6 The falsification, stated plainly

§13.123.4 registered: "MR mean 86.5 → **≥ 95**; TR and IE reproduce question for question; MR declines ≤ 13; MR
`promptChars` ≥ 45,000." Result: MR **61** (first repetition) / mean 399.5 roster against 421.0; TR and IE moved
by 5.0% churn, which is now understood; declines were **lower**, not higher (193 against 200 model declines over
2,000 evaluations); `promptChars` behaved as predicted.

**Two of the four were right and the headline was wrong by 34 questions in the wrong direction.** §13.123.5.1's
"ceiling of +18.75 questions" is moot: the sign was wrong before the magnitude mattered.

### 13.127.7 One number that got worse while this was being read

The reference pipeline's own mean across its four repetitions differs between the two dispatches: **225.8**
(`40751394094`) against **218.0** (`40792853362`), a 7.8-question drop in the control. That is larger than the
2-question within-run spread §13.125.7 measured, and larger than the 4-question between-dispatch difference it
found in the temperature pair. So there are now three estimates of control drift, and they are not the same
quantity: **within a four-repetition session ≈ 2 questions, between two dispatches 4 to 7.8 questions**.

None of it threatens this readout, and the reason is worth stating because it is the design: every number above is
paired **inside one dispatch** (the arm against the reference in the same job), or read as a **per-question** set
difference against prompts that are byte-identical. It does threaten the weaker form — "the arm scored 84.2 and
then 79.9" — which is a cross-run comparison of a headline and inherits every drift in this section.

### 13.127.8 What the ask axis now knows

| ask           | mechanism                                       |     MR | verdict                                    |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -----: | ------------------------------------------ |
| `enumerated`  | write the list, then compute                    | **87** | the adopted value                          |
| `sweep`       | a line per session printed                      |      — | §13.92: lists stayed at 2.0 items, no gain |
| `aggregation` | list with action and date, four-form arithmetic |      — | §13.103: no gain                           |
| `silent`      | **the same steps, notes unwritten**             | **61** | **−26, refuted**                           |

Three attempts to sharpen _how the list is written_ changed nothing; one attempt to stop writing it cost 26
questions. That is the same conclusion from both ends, and it settles the direction: **the list stays.** The axis
is not "write less" — it is "write the list and constrain the reply's shape", which is exactly `answer-line`
(§13.124.4), dispatched against this same control at `ac9450fd`.

## 13.128 `reviewPass: recover` has a population of sixteen questions, and ABS cannot be in it

Registered before dispatch, and it is the first registration in this document whose population was counted **with
the product's own predicate** rather than with a script written for the paragraph.

### 13.128.1 The census

`declinedItems` and `asksForCount` from `cortex-memory`, run over the control arm's 500 records (`40751394094`,
`ask=enumerated`, `reviewPass=bare`, `T=0`, first repetition):

| capability    | declines | of which carry a Step 1 list | mean items listed | of those, counting questions |
| ------------- | -------: | ---------------------------: | ----------------: | ---------------------------: |
| ABS           |       29 |                        **0** |               0.0 |                            0 |
| MR            |       12 |                       **10** |               1.6 |                            4 |
| TR            |        8 |                            5 |               3.4 |                            1 |
| KU            |        2 |                            1 |               2.0 |                            0 |
| IE            |        1 |                            0 |               0.0 |                            0 |
| **reachable** |       52 |                       **16** |                   |                            5 |

**Sixteen questions, and every one of them is already scored wrong.** That is the whole of the pass's ceiling:
10 MR, 5 TR, 1 KU — 3.2 points of the roster if all sixteen converted.

### 13.128.2 Why this pass cannot lose on accuracy, and why that is not the same as free

The gate is `declined with a non-empty list`. A decline is scored **incorrect** on every capability whose gold is
not a decline, so the pass fires only on questions that have already lost. Three outcomes are possible for each:
it answers correctly (gain), it answers wrongly (no change), or it declines again (no change). **There is no path
to a loss in the roster**, which is a stronger property than a low predicted effect and is why this is worth a
dispatch at all.

What it is not: free. It costs one model call per reachable question (16 calls, plus the tokens of the quoted
list), and §13.104.5 makes the point that a longer instruction buys declines elsewhere — which is why the prompt
carries no evidence and the pass is gated on a decline rather than applied to every question.

**ABS is excluded structurally, not by a special case.** Zero of its 29 declines carry a list: they are the bare
token, which is the correct answer there. If a run of this pass moves a single ABS question, the guard has failed
and the run is an assembly failure rather than a reading — the `no-list` branch is the only thing standing between
"repair a contradiction" and "argue with a correct refusal".

### 13.128.3 The prediction

Dispatched against the **same** control (`40751394094`) with `review_pass=recover` as the single field:

| #     | claim                                                                                                                  | falsified by                                     |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **1** | at least **5 of the 16** reachable questions convert to correct                                                        | fewer than 5                                     |
| **2** | **ABS does not move** (29/30, question for question, or within the 5.0% reader floor of §13.127.2)                     | any ABS verdict outside the floor                |
| **3** | no question that did not decline changes verdict, beyond the reader floor                                              | a flip on a question that answered               |
| **4** | the 5 counting questions are the ones most likely to convert, because the corrective prompt names the count explicitly | zero of the 5 convert while non-counting ones do |

Claim 4 is the one that would distinguish "the reader forgot to use its own list" from "the list is shorter than
the answer needs". The lists here average **1.6 items on MR against a gold count of 3 to 10** (§13.92 measured the
same gap from the other side), so counting the listed items can produce a _specific wrong number_ rather than the
gold. A pass that produces five new wrong answers and one right one is not a recovery, and claim 4 is what makes
that visible instead of folding it into a net count.

### 13.128.4 The rule this adds to the register

**A pass that can only fire on questions already scored wrong should be registered by the size of its recovery,
not by the risk of its regression.** Every other increment in this document is a two-sided bet; this one is
one-sided by construction, so a criterion phrased as "ABS must not fall" would be measuring the wrong thing
(ABS is structurally unreachable) and a criterion phrased as "net positive" would hide a pass that repairs none
of its sixteen and merely relabels them.

### 13.128.5 Ordering

It follows `answer-line` (§13.124.4) and does not share a dispatch with it: both change what the reader reads, and
a recovery on a flat-route question could not be attributed to either. Its own control is the enumerated arm, so
the comparison is one field and no drift is inherited.

## 13.129 `answer-line` is refuted by its own subset split, and the dispatch that measured it moved three routes

### 13.129.1 The assembly check, before any accuracy was read

Run `40807829150` (`ask=answer-line`) against the `enumerated` control `40751394094`. One configuration
field differs in the artifact's own `memoryArmConfig`, and one field of the control's does not match it:

| field                                                                                                                                                          | control `40751394094`           | treatment `40807829150` |                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------- |
| `ask`                                                                                                                                                          | `enumerated`                    | `answer-line`           | intended         |
| `askRoutes`                                                                                                                                                    | `multi-session, flat, temporal` | **`flat`**              | **not intended** |
| `threshold`, `retrievalThreshold`, `relevanceTopK`, `relevanceUnits`, `embedding`, `reader`, `maxTurnChars`, `maxPromptChars`, `reviewPass`, `selfConsistency` | —                               | identical               | ok               |
| mean `evidenceChars` per question                                                                                                                              | 289,387                         | 289,387                 | identical        |

The evidence is byte-identical question for question. The prompts are not: mean `promptChars` rises
46,622 → 46,948 (+327), which is the guard's length charged against a fixed 48,000-character budget
(§13.104.5's mechanism, now with a number).

`askRoutes` is the assembly failure. The registration said "reach `flat` alone, control `enumerated`",
and the implementation read that as a reach of one route with a fallthrough to the **shipped** block —
so the two routes the ask did not name lost the control's block rather than keeping it. The artifact
printed that in one field and it was read as intended. It is not.

| capability |   n | control | treatment |       Δ |
| ---------- | --: | ------: | --------: | ------: |
| IE         | 150 |     140 |       128 | **−12** |
| MR         | 121 |      87 |        39 | **−48** |
| KU         |  72 |      61 |        66 |  **+5** |
| TR         | 127 |     100 |        88 | **−12** |
| ABS        |  30 |      29 |        29 |       0 |
| **roster** | 500 | **417** |   **350** | **−67** |

Over four repetitions the aggregate moves 84.20% → 71.55%. Only the IE column is a reading of the
guard, and even that one has to be split before it means anything (§13.129.3). The MR and TR columns
are §13.104's defect arriving a **fourth** time, and they are priced as such: removing the two-step
contract from the multi-session route costs **48** questions, and removing the merging sentence from
the temporal route costs **12**.

### 13.129.2 What the two unplanned columns price

They are not free evidence — the run was not registered to measure them — but they are not nothing
either, because each is the exact minus of a block the register already contains:

| removal                                         | measured here | prior registration                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------: | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `enumerated`'s two-step contract, multi-session |       **−48** | `silent` (which rewrites it, not removes it) was −26 |
| the merging sentence, temporal                  |       **−12** | §13.104's accident was −21.4                         |
| the guard, flat                                 |           −12 | §13.124.4 predicted **+6**                           |

The direction replicates twice; the magnitude is a different sample and a different pair of blocks, so
the two numbers are recorded as two measurements of one mechanism rather than as a contradiction.

### 13.129.3 The guard, split by the shape of the gold

IE is 150 questions of three question types and two answer shapes, and the guard was written against
the failure of one shape while being administered to both. Splitting IE by the **gold's** length —
the only observable proxy the artifact carries for "this question's answer is a phrase" — separates
them completely:

| IE subset             |   n |     control |   treatment |       Δ |
| --------------------- | --: | ----------: | ----------: | ------: |
| gold ≤ 120 characters | 117 | 116 (99.1%) | 116 (99.1%) |   **0** |
| gold > 120 characters |  33 |  24 (72.7%) |  12 (36.4%) | **−12** |

**The guard is inert on its own target and destructive on the other subset.** The nine failures it was
written for (§13.124.2) are not in the 117: they are all in the 33, and their gold is a paragraph. The
registration's prediction — IE wrong 10 → ≤ 4 — is falsified in the opposite direction: 22 wrong.

### 13.129.4 The thirteen flips, read one at a time

IE moved 140 → 128 with thirteen questions correct→wrong and one wrong→correct. The thirteen are not
one failure:

| shape                           |     n | what it is                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ----: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Answer: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` | **6** | the guard turned a preference question into a decline, written in the shape the guard demanded                                                                              |
| `Answer: <one phrase>`          | **7** | the guard truncated a paragraph answer to the single most salient noun phrase (`Answer: Godox V1`, `Answer: Virtual coffee breaks`, `Answer: Chewy chocolate chip cookies`) |

Both shapes are the guard doing exactly what it says. The block asked for one line in the form
`Answer: <a word, name, number, or short phrase>`, and a question whose gold is "the user would prefer
responses that build upon …" cannot be answered in that form. §13.124.2 diagnosed the nine as _shape_
failures and that diagnosis was right; what it did not check is **whose** shape — the failures are
answers that are too long, and the prescription was to make every answer shorter still.

### 13.129.5 The mechanism the run exposed: a labelled decline disables the retry pass

The six `Answer: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` cases are not ordinary declines:

| layer                                            | reads `Answer: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` as         |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `parse.ts` `isAbstention`, via `stripDecoration` | a decline — the label is presentation            |
| `isBareDecline` (before this change)             | **content** — `Answer:` survived the token strip |

`isBareDecline` gates the arm's bare-decline retry, which re-asks a declined question without offering
the token. In the control that pass fires on 92 consultations and converts **92 of 92**; in this run it
reported `attempted: 163, answered: 163` and never fired on the six, because their declines were not
"bare" by a predicate that only stripped wrappers. Declines per run also doubled, 50 → 108.

So a prompt that names a reply shape can switch off a recovery mechanism, and **no field of the
artifact says so**: the pass reports `attempted`, and zero is indistinguishable from "no question
declined". The repair is in the predicate, not in the ask — a prompt must not be able to disable a
recovery path by asking for a format — and it is `abstention-recovery.ts` importing `parse.ts`'s
`stripDecoration` so that one definition of "which part of a reply is presentation" serves both layers.

### 13.129.6 What the run confirms

- **KU +5 on byte-identical prompts** (61 → 66 of 72, 6.9%) is the reader floor again, on a third
  independent pair of runs. §13.127.2 measured 5.0% over 379 verdicts; this is one sample of the same
  quantity and it is recorded as one, not as a gain.
- **ABS 29/30 unchanged**, which is what the reach predicts and what `ask-changes.test.ts` now enforces
  mechanically.
- **Instruction length costs declines**: 50 → 108 per run on the same evidence. §13.104.5's claim, now
  with a measured magnitude on a 200-character instruction.

### 13.129.7 The rule this adds

**A repair aimed at a capability must be validated on the subset whose gold has the shape the repair
assumes.** IE is one capability and two answer shapes; a block that constrains shape is a different
treatment on each, and the aggregate is their sum — which is why twelve questions of damage and one
question of gain looked like "IE moved a little" before the split and like a refuted hypothesis after
it. Every future ask that constrains the _reply_ rather than the _reading_ carries this split in its
registration.

### 13.129.8 `recommend`: the next ask, registered before dispatch

The nine paragraph-gold failures, read one at a time (`40751394094`):

| shape                                  |   n | example                                                          |
| -------------------------------------- | --: | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the evidence block copied back         |   3 | `75832dbd` 31,547 chars, `57f827a0` 16,766 chars, `d6233ab6` 577 |
| the reader declining **in prose**      |   4 | `No evidence items match the question about a Miami hotel`       |
| prose answers the judge did not accept |   2 | `a89d7624`, `0a34ad58`                                           |

The four prose declines are the diagnosis: a recommendation question's gold is _generated_, and the
flat block asks it to _extract_ — "if the evidence does not contain the answer, reply exactly
`INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`" — so a reader holding the user's stated preferences concludes there is no
answer to be found. The reference pipeline says the same thing in its own source, on
`RECOMMENDATION_CONTRACT`: _"the extractive contract is wrong for preference questions … it reads as
having nothing to say and abstains"_, measured there as abstention on the preference subset moving
3.45% → 21.84%.

`ask=recommend` is the flat block plus two sentences and no shape:

```
If the question asks for a suggestion, a recommendation, or advice, build it from what the user has
  already said they like, want, or are dealing with. Declining is not the right reply when those
  statements are in the evidence.
Do not quote, copy, or list the evidence turns. Reply in your own words, in at most three sentences,
  naming the specific options the evidence supports.
```

The close becomes `If the evidence contains nothing about the user's situation, reply exactly
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.` — the token and its condition survive, and no prefix is introduced, so
`isBareDecline` keeps working.

Reach `enumerated`'s, change set `{flat}` — enforced, not asserted in prose (§13.130). Control
`40751394094`.

| #   | claim                                                               | falsified by                      |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| 1   | the 33 paragraph-gold questions convert at least 4: 24 → ≥ 28       | ≤ 27                              |
| 2   | the 117 short-gold questions do not regress beyond the floor: ≥ 113 | ≤ 112                             |
| 3   | declines per run stay near the control: ≤ 60 against 50             | ≥ 70                              |
| 4   | MR, TR, ABS prompts byte-identical; KU's too                        | any prompt moved outside `{flat}` |
| 5   | overall ≥ 85.0% (control 84.20%)                                    | < 84.2%                           |

Claim 2 is the one that would separate "licensing composition is safe" from "any change to the flat
block costs the short-gold questions" — the 117 are 99.1% correct, so their headroom is one question
and their downside is the whole block's worth of phrasing.

### 13.129.9 The result: the reach is 34 questions, and claim 1 was impossible when it was written

Run `40824682542`, `ask=recommend`, four repetitions, against `40751394094`.

| capability  | control | `recommend` | Δ      | `promptChars` moved |
| ----------- | ------- | ----------- | ------ | ------------------- |
| IE          | 140/150 | 144/150     | **+4** | **34 of 150**       |
| MR          | 87/121  | 85/121      | −2     | 0                   |
| KU          | 61/72   | 66/72       | +5     | 0                   |
| TR          | 100/127 | 102/127     | +2     | 0                   |
| ABS         | 29/30   | 29/30       | 0      | 0                   |
| **overall** | 417/500 | 426/500     | **+9** | 34                  |

Claims 2, 3 and 4 hold and claim 5 holds numerically: the 117 short-gold questions went 116 → **117**,
declines per run went 13.0 → **12.5**, no question outside `flat` moved a prompt byte, and the overall
went 83.40% → **85.20%**.

**Claim 1 is falsified: 24 → 27, and the falsifier was ≤ 27.** Not by a rounding: the claim asked for 28
and the falsifier fired at 27, which is the boundary.

The reason matters more than the miss. `recommend` reaches the `flat` route, and of the 33
paragraph-gold questions only **9** render that route — the other 24 render `multi-session`, `temporal`
or `abstention`, so their prompts are byte-identical and no treatment was administered to them. The
ceiling is therefore 24 + 3 = **27**: the nine treated paragraph questions hold three errors and claim 1
asked for four conversions out of a population where only three questions were wrong and reachable.

> **A claim whose arithmetic ceiling is below its own threshold is a wish written in the grammar of a
> prediction.** §13.129.4 said a shape-constraining repair must be validated on the subset whose gold has
> that shape; this run adds the other half — the subset must also be one the treatment **reaches**.

That is the whole of §13.135's first rule, measured the expensive way.

## 13.130 The other half of a single-variable claim, made mechanical

### 13.130.1 Four arrivals of one defect

| run           | ask           | what the fallthrough did               | cost            |
| ------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `39641088296` | `aggregation` | shipped block instead of the control's | TR −21.4, IE −9 |
| (review)      | `silent`      | the same shape, caught before dispatch | —               |
| `40807829150` | `answer-line` | shipped block instead of the control's | MR −48, TR −12  |

Three dispatches, one cause: an ask whose block is correct and whose **fallthrough** is the arm nobody
registered. Each time the prose said "the other routes are byte-identical to the control", and each
time the test asserted the bytes the implementation produced, so the claim was never checked. The
`answer-line` test states the mistake as an intention — _"the control here is the SHIPPED block rather
than `enumerated`"_ — which is a test pinning a defect while reading as coverage.

### 13.130.2 What is asserted instead

`ASK_CONTROLS` names the arm each ask is registered against; `ASK_CHANGES` names the routes whose
instruction text that ask may differ on. `ask-changes.test.ts` renders **all six routes twice** — once
under the ask, once under its control — and requires the set of routes whose instructions differ to
equal `ASK_CHANGES` exactly. A route that moves without being declared fails; a route that is declared
and does not move fails too, because an ask that claims a treatment it does not administer publishes a
delta about nothing.

The oracle is the registration, never the implementation. That is the only arrangement in which a wrong
fallthrough is a failure rather than a fixture.

### 13.130.3 Why the tables are test-only

They are the one export in this package whose only caller is a test, and that is deliberate: moving them
into the artifact would let the run under test publish its own expectation, which is precisely the
arrangement that failed three times. The alternative — deleting them and restating the reach inside the
test — is what each of the three failed runs already had. Recorded in
`tools/export-census-baseline.json` under `memory-arm-ask-oracle` rather than left as an unlisted
orphan.

### 13.130.4 The mutation check

The instrument was checked against the defect it exists for rather than assumed to work: restoring the
pre-fix branch (`return own` for multi-session and temporal) makes two cases fail with

```
expected [ 'flat', 'multi-session', 'temporal' ] to deeply equal [ 'flat' ]
```

which is the exact three-route movement that cost 48 MR and 12 TR questions. Eleven other cases stay
green, so the failure names the ask rather than the table.

## 13.131 The ledger's baseline is not the control's, and the prediction it was asked to test could not be answered

### 13.131.1 What the tool computes, read against what §13.125.6 predicted

§13.125.6 registered a prediction about the two asks:

> The two asks reach different routes — `silent` changes the _multi-session_ block, `answer-line` changes the
> _flat_ block — so their purchases should be **disjoint**. A non-empty `doubleCounted` after both land would
> mean a question's verdict moved under an instruction aimed at another route.

Run against the two artifacts on disk, the instrument answers:

| quantity                                       |                      value |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------: |
| `silent` bought / sold                         |                   233 / 52 |
| `answer-line` bought / sold                    |                   215 / 86 |
| distinct bought (union)                        |                        240 |
| sum of purchases                               |                        448 |
| **double-counted**                             |                    **208** |
| conflicting (bought by one, sold by the other) | 2 (`dd2973ad`, `b46e15ee`) |

208 of 448, and it is **not** a route-isolation finding. `ledgerOf` reads `discordantQuestions`, which every
report writes as **feature versus its own `reference-pipeline` baseline inside one run** — not treatment
versus control across runs. The two increments therefore share a baseline that is the reference arm, and both
of them beat that arm on the same questions: IE, KU and TR are where the arm wins, and each arm wins them
independently. An overlap of 208 is the expected consequence of two runs of nearly the same configuration
being compared with the same third party.

**The prediction was registered against a pair the tool does not compute.** That is the finding, and it is a
defect of the registration rather than of the instrument: the sentence "their purchases should be disjoint"
is only meaningful for purchases measured against **one** shared control, and `discordantQuestions` was never
that.

### 13.131.2 What the cross-run pair actually gives

`answer-line` (`40807829150`) against `enumerated` (`40751394094`), question by question:

|            | bought |   sold |     net |
| ---------- | -----: | -----: | ------: |
| IE         |      1 |     13 |     −12 |
| MR         |      3 |     51 |     −48 |
| KU         |      6 |      1 |      +5 |
| TR         |      4 |     16 |     −12 |
| ABS        |      0 |      0 |       0 |
| **roster** | **14** | **81** | **−67** |

Two things this table says that the aggregate could not:

- **The 14 purchases are not where the treatment was aimed.** IE — the route the guard changes — bought **1**
  question and sold **13**. The purchases are 6 KU, 4 TR and 3 MR, i.e. the reader-noise floor: KU's prompts
  are byte-identical and it moved 7 questions in both directions.
- **The sold column is concentrated where the fallthrough was**: 51 of 81 are MR, which is the route that lost
  its block.

### 13.131.3 The rule this adds

**A portfolio is only meaningful over increments measured against the same control run, and the tool must not
be able to add two increments without saying which baseline each was measured against.** `discordantQuestions`
records one pair and names neither member; two artifacts' lists are commensurable only if their control is the
same run.

The registered repair, before the next portfolio is read:

| #   | requirement                                                                                                                            | status                                                                                                         | falsified by                                            |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `tools/ledger.mjs` accepts a **cross-run pair** (`--across label=<report> --control <report>`) and computes bought/sold by question id | **done**, and it reproduces §13.131.2 exactly (bought 14 / sold 81 on the archived pair)                       | it cannot express the table in §13.131.2                |
| 2   | a portfolio that mixes a within-run increment and a cross-run one is **refused by name**                                               | **done** — the message names the offending labels and says which baseline each side carries                    | it prints a union                                       |
| 3   | the tool prints the control's identity (`path`, `generatedAt`, roster size) and marks each arm `(from across)`                         | **done**; `--json` carries `mode` and `control` so a later reader can tell the two modes apart without the log | any portfolio whose printed baselines differ            |
| 4   | a cross-run pair whose two rosters differ is refused, naming the ids                                                                   | **done**                                                                                                       | it computes a diff that is partly a diff of the dataset |

Four cases cover the mode in `tools/__tests__/test_ledger.py` (cross-run arithmetic, roster mismatch, mixing,
identity), plus two on the JSON envelope, and the within-run reading keeps its shape with a `mode` field
added — so every prior portfolio in this document stays readable and is now labelled as what it was.

The additivity question itself is still not live: both increments are negative against the same control, and
there is nothing to add. It becomes live when an increment is positive, which is the condition §13.125 was
written to serve.

## 13.132 The twelve declines refuse to join two stated facts, and the sentence that licenses joining is already in the block

### 13.132.1 The diff set, read one question at a time

§13.126 closed the retrieval axis at five questions. What is left is the reader, and MR's share of it is 34
wrong answers on the control `40751394094`. Twenty-four of them are questions the reference pipeline answers
(`ablation.discordantQuestions.baselineCorrectFeatureIncorrect`, MR column), and the useful split is not by
gold shape but by **what the reply does**:

| what the reply does     |  count | questions                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | -----: | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| declines                | **10** | `dd2973ad` `60bf93ed` `9aaed6a3` `e6041065` `d905b33f` `a4996e51` `a1cc6108` `d6062bb9` `157a136e` `c18a7dc8`                |
| answers a count, wrong  |     10 | `a9f6b44c` `681a1674` `bf659f65` `3a704032` `0a995998` `d23cf73b` `2e6d26dc` `21d02d0d` `60159905` `gpt4_2f91af09`           |
| answers the wrong shape |      1 | `5025383b` — gold _"photography and cooking"_, reply `2`                                                                     |
| derives, wrong          |      3 | `a11281a2` (350 for 100) `2b8f3739` (truncated third item) `92a0aa75` (picked the company's 3y9m instead of the role's 1y5m) |

Two further MR declines, `73d42213` and `37f165cf`, are questions the reference pipeline also misses, so the
decline population is **12** and the winnable decline population is **10**.

Every one of the twelve carries its gold turns: `goldOverlap.carried` is 12/12 at the median, 11/11 for seven
of them, and 6/10 at worst (`a1cc6108`). No decline in this set is a question whose evidence was not in the
prompt, which is why the retrieval axis and this one do not overlap.

### 13.132.2 Eleven of the twelve state their reason, and the reason is the same refusal

The reply texts are quoted verbatim in the docblock of `DERIVE_MULTI_SESSION_INSTRUCTION`, and three of them
are decisive:

- `9aaed6a3` (gold `$0.75`) — _"The 1% cashback rate is mentioned in Session 11, but that is a **separate
  session and cannot be merged**."_ It found the rate and the amount, and declined because joining them
  looked forbidden.
- `dd2973ad` (gold `2 AM`) — _"These are different Wednesdays, so the evidence **does not connect** the 2 AM
  bedtime to the day before the doctor's appointment."_ It resolved both dates correctly and declined at the
  join.
- `73d42213` (gold `9:00 AM`) — _"Since the Step 1 list is not empty, the answer must be computed from it —
  but **no item gives the arrival time**."_ This is the rule being **obeyed**: the reader checked the list,
  found it non-empty, tried to compute, and had no category for interpolating 9 AM from "left home at 7 AM"
  and "back at the office around 1 PM".

Six more say the same thing in the shape _"does not state the user's age"_ / _"does not state the purchase
date"_ / _"does not state the sale price"_: the derived operand is missing as a single stated fact, so the
question is read as unanswerable.

### 13.132.3 The sentence exists and is not read, and that is a position finding

The block already contains the licence. `MERGING_SENTENCE` reads: _"The answer may require combining evidence
from more than one turn or session: gather every relevant piece first, then compute the answer. Do not reply
`INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` merely because no single piece states the answer outright."_ That is, word for word,
the answer to `a1cc6108`, `d905b33f`, `60bf93ed`, `e6041065`, `a4996e51`, `157a136e` and `c18a7dc8`.

It is six lines from the closing rule, because `withMergingSentence` inserts it above the block's last line and
`withInsertedBeforeClose` then inserts the five-line enumeration contract **above that**. Between the licence
and the closing rule sits Step 1's _"do not merge two items into one"_, and `9aaed6a3` quotes the nearer
sentence back — _"cannot be merged"_. §13.56 measured the same shape once already: with a rule placed above the
closing line, 12 of 21 surviving MR declines had read the exception and followed the rule instead.

So the variable is **position, not wording**. `derive` renders `MERGING_SENTENCE` last and changes nothing else.

### 13.132.4 What makes this one run and not two

`aggregation` (§13.103) was the version of this idea that bundled three changes — an exchange rule, a four-line
arithmetic mapping, and a **looser** decline condition — and run `39641088296` measured MR abstentions rising
from 10 to **16** under it. Loosening the condition is not free and it is not what this run does: `derive`
keeps _"Reply `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` only when the Step 1 list is empty"_ and keeps the closing line's
condition, character for character.

Two properties hold the single-variable claim, and both are tests rather than sentences:

1. **The two blocks are permutations of one another.** `derive-licence.test.ts` compares their line multisets
   and requires equality, so a reworded licence, a duplicated one, an added clause or a Step 2 edit fails as a
   change of variable.
2. **A permutation preserves length.** The MR `promptChars` of every treated record must equal the control's
   **to the character** — 46,143 on `a11281a2`, and so on for all 121. A permutation that changes the length
   is not a permutation.

The reach is `enumerated`'s three routes and the change set is `multi-session` alone, held by
`ask-changes.test.ts`, which renders all six routes twice and requires the set of routes whose bytes differ to
equal `ASK_CHANGES` exactly. That test is what §13.104 and `40807829150` are both about.

### 13.132.5 Predictions, registered before the dispatch

Dispatch: `--set cortex_memory_ask=derive` on §10.3's configuration (`selfConsistency` and `queryExpansion`
both `none`), N = 500, four repetitions. Control: **`40751394094`** — `ask=enumerated`, `reviewPass=bare`,
`temperature=0`, first repetition 83.40% overall and MR 87/121.

| #   | prediction                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | falsified if                                       |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | mechanism: `ask=derive`, `askRoutes` = `multi-session`, `flat`, `temporal`, and MR `promptChars` **equal to the control's on all 121 records**                                                                                              | any record's `promptChars` moves                   |
| 2   | MR declines **12 → ≤ 7**                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | 10 or more remain                                  |
| 3   | of the ten winnable declines, **≥ 5 convert** (MR 87 → ≥ 92)                                                                                                                                                                                | ≤ 3 convert (MR ≤ 90)                              |
| 4   | MR accuracy **≥ 76.0%** (92/121) against the control's 71.9%                                                                                                                                                                                | < 74.4%                                            |
| 5   | the refusal vocabulary falls: **≤ 5** of the MR decline replies contain _"does not state"_, _"not stated"_, _"cannot be computed"_, _"separate session"_, _"cannot be merged"_ or _"does not connect"_, against **12 of 12** in the control | **9 or more** still do                             |
| 6   | guard: IE, KU, TR and ABS `promptChars` **identical on 500 of 500**, and TR within ±5, IE within ±7 of the control's spread (§13.122.2)                                                                                                     | any of the four moves a prompt, or TR / IE outside |
| 7   | overall mean **≥ 84.2** and first repetition ≥ 83.4                                                                                                                                                                                         | below 83.0                                         |

Prediction 5 is the mechanism reading and it is judge-free: it is a string search over the same replies the
score is computed from, so a run that scored the same while the replies stopped saying _"cannot be merged"_
would still be evidence the sentence moved, and a run that scored better while they all still said it would be
evidence of something else.

§13.125's bar of 85.0% needs **eight** conversions rather than five, and it is not the registered threshold
here: the treatment is one sentence, and asking a sentence to carry eight questions is how a registration
starts predicting its author's hopes. Five is the floor at which the reading is distinguishable from the
reader noise floor §13.127 measured — 19 of 379 verdicts (5.0%) flip on byte-identical prompts.

### 13.132.6 What a positive result would mean, and what it would not

It would mean the largest single block of MR's remaining loss is a **document-ordering** defect rather than a
capability gap: the reader can do the joins, and one sentence it was given was read last by the rule that says
not to. That would also re-price §13.56 from one rule to a class.

It would not touch the fourteen answered-wrong questions, which are a different failure: ten are counts off by
one or two (`0a995998` 3 → 2, `d23cf73b` 4 → 6, `60159905` three → 2) and that is set membership; one,
`5025383b`, answered `2` to _"What are the two hobbies"_, which is Step 2 being written as an instruction to
count rather than as a mapping from question form to operation. Those are §13.133's territory — the reference
pipeline's four-line mapping, which `aggregation` bundled and therefore never priced on its own. It would not
touch `2b8f3739` either: that reply computed $375 correctly from a third item whose amount was **truncated in
the rendering**, which is a `maxTurnChars` question and not a prompt one.

### 13.132.7 The next step if position alone does not convert

The reference aggregation prompt also carries _"a sum, a difference, an average, a percentage, an elapsed time,
or a date read from the context"_ — and that list is the exact taxonomy of the thirteen derivation questions in
the diff set. It is deliberately **not** in `derive`, because position plus wording is two changes in one run.
If prediction 5 fails while prediction 2 holds — replies stop saying _"cannot be merged"_ and still decline —
the taxonomy is the next registered sentence, and it is the one the reading most directly supports.

## 13.133 The prompt axis on MR is priced: three rules were worth one question, and the reply-shape tax is not a tax

### 13.133.1 What four prompt attempts cost and bought, on one capability

MR has now been treated by four asks, each one field against its own control, and the ledger of that axis is short
enough to read as a whole:

| ask                     | what it changed on MR                                                        | MR mean | against                                          |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------: | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `aggregation` (§13.104) | an exchange rule, a four-form arithmetic mapping, a looser decline condition |    87.5 | 86.2 (`39509698041`) — **+1.3**                  |
| `silent` (§13.127)      | the Step 1 notes made private                                                |      61 | 87 (`40792853362`) — **−26**                     |
| `answer-line` (§13.130) | a reply shape on a route MR does not read                                    |      39 | 87 (`40807829150`) — **−48**, fallthrough defect |
| `derive` (§13.132)      | the combine licence moved to the last position                               | pending | 87 (`40751394094`)                               |

The one that bundled the most was worth the least. Three membership rules — an exchange is two items, verb
exclusivity with examples, dedupe across sessions — moved MR under-counts from 15 to **14** and the mean by 1.3
questions. That is the number to beat, and it is why §13.132 registers a **position** rather than adding a fifth
sentence.

### 13.133.2 The nine remaining counting errors, and the rule they are not

Of MR's 34 wrong answers, 11 have a numeric gold and a numeric reply, and **9 differ by 1 or 2**:

| question   | gold | reply | shape of the question            |
| ---------- | ---: | ----: | -------------------------------- |
| `0a995998` |    3 |     2 | pick up **or** return            |
| `a9f6b44c` |    2 |     4 | service **or** plan to service   |
| `bf659f65` |    3 |     2 | purchased **or** downloaded      |
| `d23cf73b` |    4 |     6 | learned to cook **or** tried out |
| `21d02d0d` |    2 |     1 | fun runs I **missed**            |
| `2e6d26dc` |    5 |     6 | friends **and** family members   |
| `3a704032` |    3 |     2 | plants I **acquired**            |
| `60159905` |    3 |     2 | dinner parties I **attended**    |
| `681a1674` |    2 |     1 | Marvel movies I **re-watched**   |

Four of the nine are an explicit A-or-B union, which is what the exchange rule was written for, and it did not fix
them. Two are over-counts and seven are under-counts, so the failure is not a bias that a "count more" or "count
less" sentence can correct — it is per-question set membership, and a rule stated in the prompt is applied by the
same reader that is already getting it wrong. **The ceiling of the membership axis is nine questions and its
measured price is one**, which is the strongest available argument that the next MR increment is not a sentence.

### 13.133.3 The reply shape is not a tax on unit-bearing golds, which retires one candidate

§13.130 read the `answer-line` collapse as "a reply shape is a tax on every question whose gold is not that shape",
and the obvious next candidate was to narrow Step 2 the same way. The artifact says it would be worth at most one
question. Of the 121 MR golds, 49 are bare integers, 60 carry a unit or a sentence, and 12 carry no digit; the arm
answered **30** of the 72 non-bare-int golds with a bare number, and the judge marked **24 of those 30 correct** —
`$2,500` → `2500`, `8 days` → `8`, `70 pounds` → `70`. The numeric gate reads the last number, and the judge
accepts it against a unit-bearing gold.

The six failures in that group are misfires for a different reason: five are the off-by-ones of §13.133.2 and one,
`5025383b`, answered `2` to _"What are the two hobbies that led me to join online communities"_ whose gold is
`photography and cooking`. **So the whole value of a Step-2 form mapping, priced on this artifact, is one question**,
and it is not registered. `aggregation` carried that mapping and this is the arithmetic of why it moved nothing.

### 13.133.4 `derive` and `recover` share ten questions, and against a shared control that is now a reading

§13.128.1 counted 12 MR declines of which 10 carry a non-empty list; §13.132.1 counted 12 declines of which 10 are
questions the reference pipeline answers. They are the same ten, and the two questions that fall outside each set
are the same two — `157a136e` and `c18a7dc8`, whose Step 1 is explicitly empty.

That is not a coincidence to be explained away, it is the design: two treatments, one population, one control.
`derive` is prompt-side (the reader stops having a reason to decline) and `recover` is pass-side (a second call
repairs a decline without a list). Both are measured against `40751394094`, so the ledger's cross-run mode computes
a **real** overlap here — unlike §13.131, where two increments were both measured against the reference arm and the
208-question overlap was an artifact of the shared third party.

What the pair can say that neither can alone:

- if `derive` converts five and `recover` converts five and they are the **same** five, the two mechanisms are one
  mechanism and the cheaper one wins;
- if they convert **disjoint** fives, the ten declines are two kinds of failure and the register should stop
  treating "declines" as one population — which is already what the two empty-list questions hint at;
- if `derive` converts none and `recover` converts five, the licence was never the blocker and §13.132.7's taxonomy
  sentence is not next either; the reader needs a second call, not a better first one.

Ordering: `derive` first, because it is one dispatch with no extra model call per question and its mechanism check
(`promptChars` unchanged, refusal vocabulary falling) is judge-free. `recover` follows against the same control,
and its claim 4 (§13.128.3) already asks whether the listed items can be counted into the gold — a question only a
pass can answer.

## 13.134 The reading-side ceiling is now corroborated three ways, and the only unmeasured axis is the write side

This section registers no run. It records a direction, and the rule it follows is that a direction may only be
changed by a number that has already been paid for.

### 13.134.1 Three independent statements of one ceiling

| source    | what it says                                                                                                                       | how it was measured here                    |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| §13.126.1 | **five** MR questions are wrong with their best gold turn at rank ≥ 10; every gold turn of every wrong question is already carried | `goldOverlap` per question on `40751394094` |
| §13.133.1 | three membership rules, bundled, bought **1.3** MR questions                                                                       | `39641088296` against `39509698041`         |
| §13.132.1 | all **12** MR declines carry their gold turns (median 12/12, worst 6/10), so none is a coverage miss                               | `goldOverlap.carried` per decline           |

A reordering of what was already retrieved can therefore move at most five questions, and a rule stated in the prompt
is applied by the reader that is already wrong. Two ceilings, one on each reading-side axis, and both are now
numbers rather than arguments.

### 13.134.2 What the external record adds, and the one thing it does not

The retrieved literature for this half-year says the same thing from three directions, and the grades matter more
than the numbers:

- **BFR** (arXiv 2610.09348) reports LongMemEval-S judge accuracy 72.4 → 82.2 and Turn Hit 91.4% by constructing a
  **sufficient** retrieval set rather than a relevant one. Its illustrative failure — order on 5 February, delivered
  10 February, how many days — is nearly this arm's `60bf93ed`. **It does not apply here**: that question's gold
  turns are carried 11/12, so there is nothing to re-fetch. Its value is the distinction, not the method.
- **`al-buddy-memory`**, an open implementation that publishes its artifacts and its dataset SHA, reports
  **92.6%** overall on the full 500 questions under three levers (`--expand`, `--aggregate-top-k 40`,
  `--chain-of-note`), **92.8%** re-graded by the official gpt-4o judge, and **MR 75.9% → 85.0%** between its early
  full run and the levered one. The first version of this section quoted _"MR 101/133 = 75.9%, and 25 of its 32
  misses missing an evidence turn"_. 75.9% is its unlevered MR, and the fraction, the 133 denominator and the 25/7
  split are not in its artifacts; they are withdrawn here and in the whitepaper, and §13.137 records why a number
  that cannot be recomputed from the other side's artifacts does not belong in a comparison table.
- What it establishes is narrower and more useful than a comparator's score. Its `--chain-of-note` is
  `enumerated`'s idea and this arm already carries it, so the two levers that separate 75.9 from 85.0 are the ones
  this campaign has never administered: **`--expand`, which parses time and counting cues with rules and then
  searches once per named thing**, and **`--aggregate-top-k 40`, which deepens the candidate pool for aggregation
  questions only**. Both change **how many independent evidence blocks the reader is handed** — a third
  reading-side axis, distinct from the permutation axis §13.126 capped at five questions and from the global
  prompt budget — **not** unbound, as §13.139 corrects: 468 of 500 questions render within 2,400 characters of
  the 48,000 ceiling.
- One single-variable reading inside its artifacts is worth quoting because it is independent of ours: same day,
  same levers, reranker removed — MR **85.0 → 82.0** while overall stayed at 92.6%. Reranking is worth about three
  MR questions by someone else's measurement, against the two §13.126.1 computed from `goldRanks`. Two independent
  derivations of the same small number are the best evidence this campaign has that the permutation axis is priced.
- **MOSAIC** (arXiv 2610.29249) decomposes the pipeline into write / retrieve / deliver / read and finds the largest
  degradation in **reading and integration**. Corroborative, on a multimodal corpus, which is why it changes no
  threshold.

### 13.134.3 The write side is unmeasured, and it is no longer the only unmeasured axis

> **Corrected by §13.137.** This subsection was written when the campaign believed it had priced both reading-side
> axes. It had priced two of three. §13.137 records the third — **how many independent evidence blocks the reader
> is given**, which is what `al-buddy-memory`'s `--expand` and `--aggregate-top-k` change — and withdraws the
> numbers this subsection inherited from the section above. The paragraph below is kept as written, because the
> reasoning error is the useful part: _"both axes are priced, therefore the next axis is the one that is not a
> reading-side axis at all"_ was a conclusion about the campaign's own coverage drawn from a search that had found
> a source contradicting it.

Every experiment in this document moves what the reader is _given_ or what it is _asked_. Not one moves what was
_stored_. `Dual-trace encoding` reports +30pp on MR by pairing each stored fact with a concrete reconstruction of the
moment it was learned, on 99 questions, with a 95% CI of [+12.1, +29.3] overall — a C+ grade, a single paper, and a
subgroup far smaller than the 121 MR questions here. It is not a promise and it is not registered.

What made it look like the next axis rather than another candidate is negative: §13.126 and §13.133 had priced two
reading-side axes, and §13.132 is the last prompt-side run that the arithmetic leaves room for. That argument is
sound only if the enumeration of reading-side axes is complete, and it was not: **§13.123's "95.2% of gold is
already in the pool" is a statement about the pool's coverage, not about how many separate evidence blocks reach
the reader.** A treatment that asks the same question three times, once per thing the question names, changes
neither the pool nor the order within one search, so neither ceiling applies to it.

### 13.134.4 The discipline this adds

**An axis is retired by a ceiling, not by a failure.** `silent` (−26) and `answer-line` (−48) are failures and they
retired two asks; they say nothing about prompts. What retires the prompt axis on MR is the pair of ceilings — five
questions by reordering, one by a rule set — with the best result on the axis at +1.3. Recording the distinction
matters because the failure-based reading would have retired the axis after §13.127, and `derive` would never have
been written.

## 13.135 The untreated questions are this pair's own noise realisation, and they produced seven of the nine

### 13.135.1 One split that changes what the run means

Run `40824682542` moved **+9** questions against `40751394094` and reported 85.20% against 83.40%. Cut the
same roster by whether the treatment reached the question — `promptChars` is the arm's own statement of the
length of the prompt it rendered, so two runs that agree on it rendered the same bytes for that question:

| bucket                              |       n | bought |   sold | net    |
| ----------------------------------- | ------: | -----: | -----: | ------ |
| treated (`promptChars` differ)      |      34 |      2 |      0 | **+2** |
| untouched (`promptChars` identical) | **466** | **20** | **13** | **+7** |

**Seven of the nine came from questions whose prompts did not move by one byte.** Per capability, and the
four rows that did not move a single prompt are the reading:

| capability | `promptChars` moved | flips | bought | sold | net |
| ---------- | ------------------: | ----: | -----: | ---: | --- |
| IE         |           34 of 150 |     8 |      6 |    2 | +4  |
| MR         |               **0** |    12 |      5 |    7 | −2  |
| KU         |               **0** |     5 |      5 |    0 | +5  |
| TR         |               **0** |    10 |      6 |    4 | +2  |
| ABS        |               **0** |     0 |      0 |    0 | 0   |

The four untouched capabilities hold **350 questions, 27 flips (7.71%) and a net of +5**. The 116 untouched
IE questions hold 6 flips (5.17%) and a net of +2. Together: 466 questions, **33 flips (7.08%), net +7**.

That is a **+1.5 pp "gain" produced by nothing**. It is not a bug in the scorer and it is not the treatment;
it is the same configuration, the same roster, the same four repetitions and the same temperature, on
questions whose prompts are byte-identical, run twice.

### 13.135.2 What this does to the nine, and to §13.129.5

Subtract what the untouched bucket's own rates predict for 34 questions: +2 − 34 × (7/466) = **+1.5
questions of excess**. So of the reported +9, one and a half questions are the ask and seven and a half are
the reader.

§13.129.5 recorded _"KU +5 on byte-identical prompts is the reader floor"_ as a fact about one capability on
one pair of runs. It generalises, and the general form is stronger than the instance:

> **Every cross-run pair carries its own noise realisation, and the realisation is larger than any single
> point reading the campaign has been quoting.** It does not have to be borrowed from an earlier pair; it is
> in the artifact, in the 466 questions that were not touched.

At 7.08% flipping and a +1.5 pp net on 466 questions, **a whole-roster difference below about two points is
not readable from a single pair**. §13.129's own reading — 140 → 128 IE with thirteen flips — survives that
floor, because thirteen flips against an expected 10.6 is still a flip count, not a net. What does not
survive is any claim of the form "the total went up two points, so the treatment worked".

### 13.135.3 The instrument, and the two mutations it survives

`tools/ledger.mjs --across` now computes the split from `promptChars` on both sides and prints it beside the
increment:

```
    treated  (promptChars differ)   : 34 questions, bought 2, sold 0, net +2
    untouched (promptChars identical): 466 questions, bought 20, sold 13, net +7
      the untouched bucket is this pair's own noise realisation, at 1.50% net per question, so 34 treated
      questions would move +0.5 by themselves; the treatment's excess is +1.5 question(s)
```

Three design decisions in that block are load-bearing:

1. **A missing field is not "untouched".** `promptChars` absent on either side puts the question in an
   `unknown` bucket and the tool prints `N question(s) carry no promptChars on at least one side, so the
split above is over the rest and not over the roster`. Counting absent as untouched would put the whole
   roster in the noise bucket and report an excess of minus the entire treated net — a confident wrong
   answer where the honest one is that the artifact does not carry the field. This is the same rule
   `threshold` and `sessionBudget` are read under.
2. **The verdict is printed, not inferred.** When the excess is ≤ 0 the tool writes `ATTRIBUTION FAILS: the
treated questions moved no more than untouched ones, so this net is not evidence about the treatment
whatever its sign`. A reader who sees only "+9" cannot reach the wrong conclusion without contradicting a
   line that is already on screen.
3. **No p-value.** 34 questions do not support one, and printing one would make an arithmetic statement look
   like an inferential one.

`tools/__tests__/test_ledger.py` grows from 11 to 16 cases, and the two mutations both die:

| mutation                                     | caught by                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| count every splittable question as untouched | 3 tests, incl. `test_across_json_carries_the_reach_split`    |
| count a missing `promptChars` as treated     | 1 test: `test_across_says_when_the_split_cannot_be_computed` |

### 13.135.4 What `recommend` actually had to work with

Of the 34 treated questions, **25 are short-gold and the control already scores 25/25** on them. There is no
headroom in three quarters of the reach. The work was nine paragraph-gold questions holding three errors,
and the ask converted two of the three:

- `57f827a0` — the control copied the evidence block back (`1. [2023/05/27 (Sat) 03:14] user: I'm lo…`); the
  treatment wrote _"The evidence doesn't include any tips on…"_, which the judge accepted.
- `a89d7624` — the control's prose was not accepted; the treatment wrote _"For your Denver trip, catch a
  show at Re…"_, which is the paraphrase the gold wanted.

**Zero sold.** `recommend` is the only ask in this campaign whose treated population lost nothing: `silent`
cost 26 MR questions and `answer-line` cost 48, both on their own reach. Two sentences added to the flat
block and a close that keeps the token intact — no reply shape, no label, no length rule the reader has to
satisfy before it can answer — cost one question of damage at most and bought two.

Verdict: **not adopted.** Claim 1 is falsified and the mechanism's +1.5 excess is inside a ±1.5σ band. It
stays a selectable ask, recorded as the one ask on the axis with a small ceiling and no downside, which is
the shape a future IE increment would want to start from.

### 13.135.5 Three rules, and the second one is what this section is for

1. **A claim's ceiling is computed on the treated population.** §13.129.9 is the expensive example: 33
   paragraph-gold questions, 9 of them reachable, three errors between them, threshold of four.
2. **Every increment reports its treated/untouched split, and the untouched bucket is this pair's own
   realisation.** Not the previous pair's, not a global constant. It is free — it is in the artifact — and
   it is the only number that says whether a net belongs to the treatment.
3. **When a treatment covers an entire capability, the reference comes from the capabilities it did not
   reach.** `derive` reaches `multi-session`, `flat` and `temporal`, which is IE, MR and TR; only KU (72) and
   ABS (30) stay untouched. So §13.132's MR predictions are measured against a 102-question reference, and
   that is weaker than the 466-question one here — a fact to state, not to hide.

### 13.135.6 What the floor does to §13.132's thresholds

MR flipped 12 times on zero prompt movement in this pair, so the pair's MR-scale net has a spread of roughly
√12 ≈ **3.5 questions**. §13.132's prediction 3 asks for +5, which is about **1.4σ**, and prediction 2 asks
for five fewer declines, which is the same distance in the other direction.

Both stay as registered, with one addition that this section makes mandatory: **prediction 3 additionally
requires a positive excess against the KU + ABS reference.** A +5 that arrives while the 102 untouched
questions move +5 is a coin landing heads, and a campaign that has just priced its own floor cannot then
accept a 1.4σ reading as mechanism evidence. It can accept it as a reason to run the pair again.

## 13.136 The dispatch read a branch nobody was pushing to, and nothing errored

### 13.136.1 One line of output that was wrong, and was the only thing that said so

Dispatching `derive` printed:

```
dispatching cortex-memory A/B at master (749946f7)
  cortex_memory_ask = derive *
```

`749946f7` is _feat(tools): give the ledger a cross-run mode_. The `derive` implementation is in
`3093a7c`, three commits later. `git ls-remote` explained it in two lines:

```
9ed97f86…  refs/heads/main
749946f7…  refs/heads/master
```

**The checkout pushes to `main`; the workflow dispatches against `master`.** Both are real branches,
both are allowed to diverge, and the dispatch did exactly what it was told.

### 13.136.2 Three successes and one wrong experiment

Every step reported success:

| step                             | what it said                                                          |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `git push origin HEAD:main`      | `main -> main`                                                        |
| `gh workflow run … --ref master` | accepted                                                              |
| the run                          | started, green, on `749946f7`                                         |
| the log                          | `749946f7` — a SHA, print in the third line, compared against nothing |

That is the whole failure: **a value that was produced, recorded and displayed, and that no code
compared with anything.** The campaign has this shape on record three times already — §13.34.6's
check that is not a check, §13.130's test that pins an implementation as an intention, §13.129.5's
two layers each implementing the same predicate — and this is the first time it is the toolchain
rather than the product.

### 13.136.3 What it would have cost had it not been caught

The run was cancelled 8 seconds in (`40859309993`, `conclusion: cancelled`), so it cost nothing. The
cost is in what a completed run would have reported.

With `ask=derive` against a build that has no `derive`, `readAsk` falls back to the shipped value,
so the arm runs as `enumerated` and the artifact says `ask=derive` because that is what was
dispatched. Predicted outcome:

| claim (§13.132.5)                                                     | what a stale-tree run would report              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 1 — `askRoutes` three routes, MR `promptChars` equal to the control's | **holds exactly** — `enumerated` is the control |
| 2 — MR declines 12 → ≤ 7                                              | fails, 12 → 12                                  |
| 3 — ≥ 5 of ten convert                                                | fails, 0 convert                                |
| 5 — refusal vocabulary falls to ≤ 5 of 12                             | fails, 12 of 12                                 |

**The mechanism check would have passed and every effect check would have failed**, which is the
hardest shape to diagnose: it looks like a treatment that was administered and did nothing. Two
hours, 500 questions, four repetitions, and a readout that says the sentence did not matter — on a
build where the sentence was never written.

### 13.136.4 The gate, and why it compares trees rather than commits

`staleness_refusal(remote_tree, head_tree)` runs before the dispatch and refuses unless `master`'s
tree equals this checkout's HEAD tree.

- **Trees, not SHAs.** `push-via-api.py` rebuilds each commit through the Git Data API, so the same
  content arrives under a fresh object id. A SHA comparison would refuse every dispatch in this
  campaign's normal workflow and be switched off within a day.
- **`None` is "cannot tell", not "stale".** A directory that is not a checkout has no HEAD tree; the
  script is imported by tests and copied into scratch dirs. Treating absent as a mismatch would make
  the module unimportable outside a repository — the same absent-versus-zero rule the artifact's
  `threshold` and `sessionBudget` are read under.
- **A documented exit.** `--allow-stale-tree` exists because a gate with no override gets edited
  out rather than used.
- **The refusal names the branch.** "master's tree is X and HEAD's is Y" plus "pushing only `main`
  leaves master behind" is actionable; "the remote does not match" sends a reader to compare SHAs
  by hand, which is the check that did not happen.

`tools/__tests__/test_dispatch_staleness.py`, 6 cases. Two mutations, both die:

| mutation                              | caught by                                                             |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| an absent local tree treated as stale | `test_a_directory_that_is_not_a_checkout_passes`                      |
| the gate always passes                | 3 tests, incl. `test_the_refusal_names_the_branch_the_workflow_reads` |

### 13.136.5 The branch pair is the underlying defect

The gate makes a stale dispatch loud, and it does not fix the arrangement that makes it possible:
this repository has two long-lived branches, the checkout pushes one and CI reads the other. Both
are at `81d37e3` now because both were pushed by hand. **The gate is the guard, not the repair.** The
repair is that a campaign checkout has one branch to push, and until that is true the `local_tree`
comparison is the only thing standing between a typo and a two-hour measurement of the wrong code.

## 13.137 A quoted number that could not be recomputed, and the third reading-side axis it was hiding

### 13.137.1 The withdrawal

§13.134.2 and the whitepaper's §2.3.2 both said of `al-buddy-memory`:

> MR **101/133 = 75.9%**, and 25 of its 32 misses are missing an evidence turn while 7 are wrong with every piece
> present.

Reading its repository rather than a search summary: the MR capability has **121** questions, not 133; 75.9% is
its MR **without the three levers**, not the system's MR; and the 25/7 split appears nowhere in `bench/results/`.
Two of the three claims are withdrawn outright and the third is withdrawn as stated — 75.9% is real, and it means
something different from what the sentence said it meant.

**The rule this adds is narrower than a grading rule.** §6.1 grades a _source_; this was a _number_ with no path to
its origin. A quoted figure belongs in a comparison table only if it can be recomputed from the other side's
published artifacts, or if it is marked unverified. Here the number could have been checked in one fetch, and the
reason it was not is that it arrived pre-formatted, inside a sentence that already looked like a finding.

### 13.137.2 What the artifacts actually report

| run                                         | levers                                          |   overall |        MR |    TR |    KU |    SSU |  SSA |   SSP |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------: | --------: | ----: | ----: | -----: | ---: | ----: |
| `2026-09-29-longmemeval-full`               | none                                            |     88.4% | **75.9%** | 85.7% | 94.9% | 96–100 |    — |     — |
